insight: God cannot be visibly portrayed in any way, and although creatures may be pictured, no image of them may be made or kept in order to worship them or to serve God through them. Refuse every picture of God, carved or imagined, as a way of approaching him, and trust the invisible God to receive worship that needs no image.

text: Q. But may images not be tolerated in the churches as "books for the laity"? A. No, for we should not be wiser than God. He wants His people to be taught not by means of dumb images but by the living preaching of His Word.
insight: Defenders of church images had long called them books for the unlearned, and Heidelberg answered that we should not be wiser than God. You are taught by the living preaching of his Word, so give the sermon your best attention.

text: Q. What is required in the third commandment? A. We are not to blaspheme or to abuse the Name of God by cursing, perjury, or unnecessary oaths, nor to share in such horrible sins by being silent bystanders. In short, we must use the holy Name of God only with fear and reverence, so that we may rightly confess Him, call upon Him, and praise Him in all our words and works.
insight: Awkward silence when a friend mocks God's name can feel harmless, yet the third commandment counts silent bystanders as sharing in the sin. Use his name only with fear and reverence, and ask God for the courage you need to speak kindly for its honor.

text: Q. Is the blaspheming of God's Name by swearing and cursing such a grievous sin that God is angry also with those who do not prevent and forbid it as much as they can? A. Certainly, for no sin is greater or provokes God's wrath more than the blaspheming of His Name. That is why He commanded it to be punished with death.
insight: God is angry with those who blaspheme his name and also with those who do not prevent and forbid it as much as they can, for no sin provokes his wrath more. In your home, your classroom, or your workplace, use whatever authority you have to discourage it, gently and without fear.

text: Q. But may we swear an oath by the Name of God in a godly manner? A. Yes, when the government demands it of its subjects, or when necessity requires it, in order to maintain and promote fidelity and truth, to God's glory and for our neighbour's good. Such oath-taking is based on God's Word and was therefore rightly used by saints in the Old and the New Testament.
insight: Courtroom oaths fall under the words "when the government demands it," and saints of both testaments swore rightly by God's name. When you raise your hand to testify, you call God to guard the truth for his glory and your neighbor's good.

text: Q. May we also swear by saints or other creatures? A. No. A lawful oath is a calling upon God, who alone knows the heart, to bear witness to the truth, and to punish me if I swear falsely. No creature is worthy of such honour.
insight: Swearing on a saint or a mother's grave may sound pious, but a lawful oath calls on God, who alone knows the heart, to witness the truth and to punish you if you lie. Keep your most solemn appeals for the only one able to judge them.

text: Q. What does God require in the fourth commandment? A. First, that the ministry of the gospel and the schools be maintained and that, especially on the day of rest, I diligently attend the church of God to hear God's Word, to use the sacraments, to call publicly upon the LORD, and to give Christian offerings for the poor. Second, that all the days of my life I rest from my evil works, let the LORD work in me through His Holy Spirit, and so begin in this life the eternal sabbath.
insight: The fourth commandment asks that the ministry of the gospel and the schools be maintained, and that on the day of rest you gather to hear God's Word, use the sacraments, call on the LORD, and give to the poor. It also asks you to rest from evil works every day of your life, so that his Spirit works in you and the eternal sabbath begins in this life.

text: Q. What does God require in the fifth commandment? A. That I show all honour, love, and faithfulness to my father and mother and to all those in authority over me, submit myself with due obedience to their good instruction and discipline, and also have patience with their weaknesses and shortcomings, since it is God's will to govern us by their hand.
insight: Practice patience with the weaknesses of parents and bosses, because God is pleased to govern you by their hand. Honor, love, faithfulness, and submission to good instruction all belong to the fifth commandment, and patience is where they get tested.

text: Q. What does God require in the sixth commandment? A. I am not to dishonour, hate, injure, or kill my neighbour by thoughts, words, or gestures, and much less by deeds, whether personally or through another; rather, I am to put away all desire of revenge. Moreover, I am not to harm or recklessly endanger myself. Therefore, also, the government bears the sword to prevent murder.
insight: The sixth commandment reaches past the hand to the heart and tongue, forbidding you to dishonor, hate, or injure your neighbor by thoughts, words, or gestures, and calling you to put away every desire for revenge. Ask God to search the glances and remarks you would never call violence.

text: Q. But does this commandment speak only of killing? A. By forbidding murder God teaches us that He hates the root of murder, such as envy, hatred, anger, and desire of revenge, and that He regards all these as murder.
insight: Jealousy at a friend's promotion rarely feels murderous, yet God hates envy as a root of murder, along with hatred, anger, and the desire for revenge. Treat your small resentment with the seriousness God gives it, and bring it to him before it grows.

text: Q. Is it enough, then, that we do not kill our neighbour in any such way? A. No. When God condemns envy, hatred, and anger, He commands us to love our neighbour as ourselves, to show patience, peace, gentleness, mercy, and friendliness toward him, to protect him from harm as much as we can, and to do good even to our enemies.
insight: Harmlessness is too small a goal for the sixth commandment: God commands you to love your neighbor as yourself, to show patience, peace, gentleness, mercy, and friendliness, and to do good even to your enemies. Think of one person who has wronged you, and pray for a concrete way to do them good.

text: Q. What does the seventh commandment teach us? A. That all unchastity is cursed by God. We must therefore detest it from the heart and live chaste and disciplined lives, both within and outside of holy marriage.
insight: All unchastity is cursed by God, so the seventh commandment calls you to detest it from the heart and to live a chaste and disciplined life, within marriage or outside it. Ask God to make you hate impurity inwardly as well as avoid it outwardly, since he looks at the heart.

text: Q. Does God in this commandment forbid nothing more than adultery and similar shameful sins? A. Since we, body and soul, are temples of the Holy Spirit, it is God's will that we keep ourselves pure and holy. Therefore He forbids all unchaste acts, gestures, words, thoughts, desires, and whatever may entice us to unchastity.
insight: Guard the small doors: gestures, words, glances, and daydreams. Because your body and soul are temples of the Holy Spirit, God forbids everything that may entice toward unchastity, and he gives you his Spirit to keep you pure.

text: Q. What does God forbid in the eighth commandment? A. God forbids not only outright theft and robbery but also such wicked schemes and devices as false weights and measures, deceptive merchandising, counterfeit money, and usury; we must not defraud our neighbour in any way, whether by force or by show of right. In addition God forbids all greed and all abuse or squandering of His gifts.
insight: Would your pricing, your expense report, and your tax return survive being read aloud to the neighbor they affect? God forbids false weights, deceptive merchandising, and every scheme by which you might defraud another, along with greed itself.

text: Q. What does God require of you in this commandment? A. I must promote my neighbour's good wherever I can and may, deal with him as I would like others to deal with me, and work faithfully so that I may be able to give to those in need.
insight: Labor faithfully, in part, so that you have something left over to give to those in need. The eighth commandment turns from forbidding theft to charging you to promote your neighbor's good wherever you can, dealing with others as you would want to be dealt with.

text: Q. What is required in the ninth commandment? A. I must not give false testimony against anyone, twist no one's words, not gossip or slander, nor condemn or join in condemning anyone rashly and unheard. Rather, I must avoid all lying and deceit as the devil's own works, under penalty of God's heavy wrath. In court and everywhere else, I must love the truth, speak and confess it honestly, and do what I can to defend and promote my neighbour's honour and reputation.
insight: Lunch-table verdicts, passed on someone "rashly and unheard," fall under the ninth commandment alongside gossip and slander. Defend your neighbor's honor and reputation the way you would want your own defended, even when the story is tempting to repeat.

text: Q. What does the tenth commandment require of us? A. That not even the slightest thought or desire contrary to any of God's commandments should ever arise in our heart. Rather, we should always hate all sin with all our heart, and delight in all righteousness.
insight: Ahead of the hand and the tongue, a desire flickers, and the tenth commandment reaches back to that first spark. When envy stirs at a neighbor's good news, you can bring it to God right then, before it grows into a plan.

text: Q. But can those converted to God keep these commandments perfectly? A. No. In this life even the holiest have only a small beginning of this obedience. Nevertheless, with earnest purpose they do begin to live not only according to some but to all the commandments of God.
insight: Even the holiest believers have only a small beginning of obedience in this life, yet with earnest purpose they begin to live according to all of God's commandments. If you are discouraged by how little you have changed, you may count your small beginning as genuine and keep aiming at the whole law.

text: Q. If in this life no one can keep the ten commandments perfectly, why does God have them preached so strictly? A. First, that throughout our life we may more and more become aware of our sinful nature, and therefore seek more eagerly the forgiveness of sins and righteousness in Christ. Second, that we may be zealous for good deeds and constantly pray to God for the grace of the Holy Spirit, that He may more and more renew us after God's image, until after this life we reach the goal of perfection.
insight: God has the law preached strictly first so that we grow aware of our sinful nature and seek forgiveness and righteousness in Christ, and second so that we pray for the Spirit to renew us after God's image. When the law exposes a failure, you can let it drive you to Christ for pardon and to prayer for renewal.

text: Q. Why is prayer necessary for Christians? A. Because prayer is the most important part of the thankfulness which God requires of us. Moreover, God will give His grace and the Holy Spirit only to those who constantly and with heartfelt longing ask Him for these gifts and thank Him for them.
insight: Gratitude, in Heidelberg's reckoning, finds its chief outlet in prayer, so asking and thanking belong together. Whatever you ask God for this week, you can pair it with one specific thanks for something He has already given you.

text: Q. What belongs to a prayer which pleases God and is heard by Him? A. First, we must from the heart call upon the one true God only, who has revealed Himself in His Word, for all that He has commanded us to pray. Second, we must thoroughly know our need and misery, so that we may humble ourselves before God. Third, we must rest on this firm foundation that, although we do not deserve it, God will certainly hear our prayer for the sake of Christ our Lord, as He has promised us in His Word.
insight: Among calling on the true God alone, admitting your real need, and resting on Christ's merit when you feel unworthy, which comes hardest for you? A prayer God hears carries all three, so you can bring the hardest one to Him first.

text: Q. What has God commanded us to ask of Him? A. All the things we need for body and soul, as included in the prayer which Christ our Lord Himself taught us.
insight: Heidelberg's final eleven questions walk through the Lord's Prayer, because Christ Himself gave the words for what we may ask for body and soul. When your own words run dry, you can pray His slowly and mean each line.

text: Q. What is the Lord's prayer? A. Our Father who art in heaven, Hallowed be Thy Name. Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done, On earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread; And forgive us our debts, As we also have forgiven our debtors; And lead us not into temptation, But deliver us from the evil one. For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
insight: Christ gave this prayer as a pattern, and its petitions set daily bread, debts, and temptation beside God's name, kingdom, and will. You can pray it slowly, pausing after each line to name one thing in your life it touches, since He cares about all of it.

text: Q. Why has Christ commanded us to address God as Our Father? A. To awaken in us at the very beginning of our prayer that childlike reverence and trust toward God which should be basic to our prayer: God has become our Father through Christ and will much less deny us what we ask of Him in faith than our fathers would refuse us earthly things.
insight: "Our Father" comes first so that reverence and trust are awakened before a single request is made. You can begin every prayer remembering that God has become your Father through Christ and is far readier to give than any earthly father you have known.

text: Q. Why is there added, Who art in heaven? A. These words teach us not to think of God's heavenly majesty in an earthly manner, and to expect from His almighty power all things we need for body and soul.
insight: The words "who art in heaven" keep us from imagining God's majesty in earthly terms, as though He were limited like the powers we know, and teach us to expect from His almighty power all we need for body and soul. When your need looks large, you can ask as one who prays to a Father whose power has no earthly limit.

text: Q. What is the first petition? A. Hallowed be Thy Name. That is: Grant us first of all that we may rightly know Thee, and sanctify, glorify, and praise Thee in all Thy works, in which shine forth Thy almighty power, wisdom, goodness, righteousness, mercy, and truth. Grant us also that we may so direct our whole life-- our thoughts, words, and actions-- that Thy Name is not blasphemed because of us but always honoured and praised.
insight: Embarrassment over a careless word or a short temper can become a prayer. The first petition asks that your thoughts, words, and actions keep God's name from being blasphemed because of you, and you can pray it tonight for tomorrow's conversations.

text: Q. What is the second petition? A. Thy kingdom come. That is: So rule us by Thy Word and Spirit that more and more we submit to Thee. Preserve and increase Thy church. Destroy the works of the devil, every power that raises itself against Thee, and every conspiracy against Thy holy Word. Do all this until the fulness of Thy kingdom comes, wherein Thou shalt be all in all.
insight: The second petition asks God to rule us by His Word and Spirit, to preserve and increase His church, and to destroy the works of the devil until His kingdom comes in fullness and He is all in all. When you pray "Thy kingdom come," you are asking to be ruled more fully yourself and for His church to grow.

text: Q. What is the third petition? A. Thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. That is: Grant that we and all men may deny our own will, and without any murmuring obey Thy will, for it alone is good. Grant also that everyone may carry out the duties of his office and calling as willingly and faithfully as the angels in heaven.
insight: Imagine the angels doing what God says without a murmur, gladly and at once. When a dull or unwanted duty in your calling waits for you, you can ask for that same willing readiness and do the work as service to Him.

text: Q. What is the fourth petition? A. Give us this day our daily bread. That is: Provide us with all our bodily needs so that we may acknowledge that Thou art the only fountain of all good, and that our care and labour, and also Thy gifts, cannot do us any good without Thy blessing. Grant therefore that we may withdraw our trust from all creatures, and place it only in Thee.
insight: Anxiety about money often hides a quiet trust in paychecks and savings. The fourth petition teaches you to withdraw that trust from creatures and place it in God alone, the only fountain of good, and to receive your next meal as His gift.

text: Q. What is the fifth petition? A. And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. That is: For the sake of Christ's blood, do not impute to us, wretched sinners; any of our transgressions, nor the evil which still clings to us, as we also find this evidence of Thy grace in us that we are fully determined wholeheartedly to forgive our neighbor.
insight: The fifth petition asks pardon for the sake of Christ's blood, and the explanation treats a wholehearted determination to forgive our neighbor as evidence of God's grace in us. If you are holding a grudge, you can first ask forgiveness for your own debts, then ask Christ for grace to forgive the person who wronged you.

text: Q. What is the sixth petition? A. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. That is: In ourselves we are so weak that we cannot stand even for a moment. Moreover, our sworn enemies-- the devil, the world, and our own flesh-- do not cease to attack us. Wilt Thou, therefore, uphold and strengthen us by the power of Thy Holy Spirit, so that in this spiritual war we may not go down to defeat, but always firmly resist our enemies, until we finally obtain the complete victory.
insight: The sixth petition begins by admitting that in ourselves we are so weak we cannot stand even for a moment against our sworn enemies, the devil, the world, and our own flesh. When temptation comes, you can ask the Holy Spirit to uphold and strengthen you, trusting Him to carry you on to the complete victory.

text: Q. How do you conclude your prayer? A. For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. That is: All this we ask of Thee because, as our King, having power over all things, Thou art both willing and able to give us all that is good, and because not we but Thy holy Name should so receive all glory for ever.
insight: Whose kingdom, power, and glory are you counting on when you pray? The closing words rest every request on God as King, willing and able to give, so you can end your prayers giving Him the credit before the answer even comes.

text: Q. What does the word Amen mean? A. Amen means: It is true and certain. For God has much more certainly heard my prayer than I feel in my heart that I desire this of Him.
insight: Doubt about whether your prayers get through is met by Heidelberg's last word: God has heard you more certainly than you feel you asked. You can say Amen on the days your heart feels flat, because its certainty rests on Him.

text: Q. Who is the First and Chiefest Being? A. God is the First and Chiefest Being
insight: Baptists in 1695 opened their catechism with God Himself, before sin, salvation, or duty came up. You can order your own morning the same way, turning your first thoughts toward Him before the worries claim that place.

text: Q. Ought every One to believe there is a God? A. Every One ought to believe there is a God; and it is their great Sin and Folly who do not.
insight: Unbelief often passes for mere opinion, one view among many. The 1695 catechism calls it sin and folly together, so you need not apologize for believing in God; you can speak of Him plainly and kindly to friends who doubt.

text: Q. How may we know there is a God? A. The Light of Nature in Man, and the Works of God plainly declare there is a God; but his Word and Spirit only, do it fully and effectually, for the Salvation of Sinners.
insight: Sunlight on a kitchen table, a sparrow, a newborn's grip: the light of nature declares there is a God. Only His Word and Spirit reveal Him fully enough to save, so you can allow creation to start the thought and open Scripture to finish it.

text: Q. What is the Word of God? A. The Holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments are the Word of God, and the only certain Rule of Faith and Obedience.
insight: Canon comes from a Greek word for a measuring rod, and Scripture is named the only certain rule of faith and obedience. Before a hard decision, you can lay it against that rod first and consult your feelings afterward.

text: Q. May all Men make use of the Holy Scriptures? A. All Men are not only permitted, but commanded and exhorted, to read, hear, and understand the Holy Scriptures.
insight: The 1695 Baptists went beyond permitting ordinary people to read Scripture: all are commanded and exhorted to read, hear, and understand it. You need no specialist's permission to open your Bible, only an honest willingness to be addressed by God.

text: Q. What things are chiefly contained in the Holy Scriptures? A. The Holy Scriptures chiefly contain, what Man ought to believe concerning God, and what Duty God requireth of Man.
insight: When you read Scripture, do you ask both questions it answers: what should I believe about God, and what does He require of me? Most of us favor one, so you can try asking the neglected one of your next chapter.

text: Q. What is God? A. God is a Spirit, Infinite, Eternal, and Unchangeable, in his Being, Wisdom, Power, Holiness, Justice, Goodness and Truth.
insight: Adjectives like "Infinite, Eternal, and Unchangeable" govern every attribute that follows, so God's goodness and truth are as limitless and constant as His being. When the people and plans around you keep shifting, you can lean on a goodness that will not change.

text: Q. Are there more Gods than One? A. There is but One only, the Living and True God.
insight: Divided loyalties wear you out, pulling you between approval, comfort, and control. There is but one living and true God, and you can hand each of those rivals back to Him by name.

text: Q. How many Persons are there in the Godhead? A. There are Three Persons in the Godhead, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; and these Three are One God, the same in Essence, equal in Power and Glory.
insight: Theologians distinguish essence from person: one God in essence, three persons, equal in power and glory. You need not solve the mystery to worship; you can pray to the Father, through the Son, by the Spirit, and find all three present to you.

text: Q. What are the Decrees of God? A. The Decrees of God are, his Eternal Purpose according to the Counsel of his Will, whereby, for his own Glory, he hath foreordained whatsoever comes to pass.
insight: God's decree goes beyond knowing the future: by the counsel of His own will, from eternity and for His glory, He has foreordained whatever comes to pass. When tomorrow looks uncertain, you can pray to the One who has purposed it and ask Him to work His good ends in you through whatever He sends.

text: Q. How doth God execute his Decrees? A. God executeth his Decrees in the Works of Creation and Providence
insight: Think of a builder who raises a house and then lives in it and keeps it in repair. God carries out His decrees in both creation and providence, so you can trust Him with the upkeep of your life as surely as with its making.

text: Q. What is the Work of Creation? A. The Work of Creation , is God's making all Things of Nothing, by the Word of his Power, in the space of six Days, and all very Good.
insight: God made all things of nothing, by the word of His power, in the space of six days, and all of it very good. When part of your life looks empty, you can pray to the One who needs no raw material to work with and whose works are good.

text: Q. How did God create Man? A. God created Man, Male and Female, after his own Image, in Knowledge, Righteousness and Holiness, with Dominion over the Creatures.
insight: God created the first man and woman after His image, in knowledge, righteousness, and holiness; the fall lost that original righteousness, yet every person you meet bears God's image. You can speak to the difficult ones with that dignity in view and pray that Christ would renew in them what Adam lost.

text: Q. What are God's Works of Providence? A. God's Works of Providence, are his most Holy, Wise, and Powerful preserving, and governing all his Creatures, and all their Actions.
insight: Is anything in your day too small for God to be governing? He preserves and governs all His creatures and all their actions, holy, wise, and powerful in each, so you can hand Him the unnoticed details as well as the headlines.

text: Q. What special Act of Providence did God exercise towards Man in the Estate wherein he was created? A. When God had created Man, he entered into a Covenant of Life with him, upon Condition of perfect Obedience: forbidding him to eat of the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, upon pain of Death.
insight: The covenant of life required of Adam perfect obedience, with death threatened for eating from one tree, and his failure left his posterity unable to gain life by that road. Your hope rests on Christ, who kept the condition in full, so the obedience you offer God now can be the thanks of someone already given life.

text: Q. Did our first Parents continue in the Estate wherein they were created? A. Our first Parents being left to the freedom of their own Will, fell from the Estate wherein they were created, by sinning against God.
insight: Shame tempts you to blame circumstances, yet our first parents were left to the freedom of their own will and chose to sin. You can confess your own choices honestly, knowing the God who saw that first fall has provided a Redeemer.

text: Q. What is Sin? A. Sin is any want of Conformity unto, or Transgression of the Law of God.
insight: Falling short and crossing over are the two shapes sin takes: any want of conformity to God's law, or any transgression of it. You can examine your week for both, the good you left undone as well as the wrong you did.

text: Q. What was the Sin whereby our first Parents fell from the Estate wherein they were created? A. The Sin whereby our first Parents fell from the Estate wherein they were created, was their eating the forbidden Fruit.
insight: Biting into fruit is an ordinary act, yet it was the sin by which our first parents fell. You can take your own small compromises seriously, because disobedience is measured by whom it defies and not by its size.

text: Q. Did all Mankind fall in Adam's first Transgression? A. The Covenant being made with Adam, not only for himself, but for his Posterity, all Mankind descending from him by ordinary Generation, sinned in him, and fell with him in his first Transgression.
insight: Representation is the idea at work: the covenant was made with Adam for all his posterity, so all fell with him. Because the same principle brings Christ's righteousness to everyone united to him by faith, you can rest in a Head whose obedience counts for you.

text: Q. Into what Estate did the Fall bring Mankind? A. The Fall brought Mankind into an Estate of Sin and Misery.
insight: Grief over broken things, a diagnosis, a ruined friendship, belongs to the estate of misery the fall brought. You can bring each sorrow to God as a sign of what the gospel is rescuing you from.

text: Q. Wherein consists the sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell? A. The sinfulness of that Estate whereinto Man fell, consists in the Guilt of Adam's first Sin, the want of Original Righteousness, and the Corruption of his whole Nature, which is commonly called Original Sin; together with all actual Transgressions which proceed from it.
insight: Why does sin feel so natural, arriving before you choose it? Original sin includes the corruption of your whole nature along with Adam's guilt counted to you, so you can name that pull honestly and run to Christ, who answers guilt and corruption both.

text: Q. What is the Misery of that Estate whereinto Man fell? A. All Mankind by their Fall lost Communion with God, are under his Wrath and Curse; and so make liable to all Miseries in this Life, to Death it self, and to the Pains of Hell for ever.
insight: Lost communion with God heads the list, and wrath, curse, every misery of this life, death, and the pains of hell for ever follow, because all mankind fell guilty in Adam. Hearing it so bluntly, you can see why the gospel is a rescue and flee to Christ, who bore the curse for sinners.

text: Q. Did God leave all Mankind to perish in the Estate of Sin and Misery? A. God, having out of his meer good pleasure, from all Eternity, elected some to Everlasting Life, did enter into a Covenant of Grace, to deliver them out of the Estate of Sin and Misery, and to bring them into an Estate of Salvation by a Redeemer.
insight: Salvation begins in God's mere good pleasure: from all eternity He elected some to everlasting life and entered into a covenant of grace to deliver them by a Redeemer. If you are in Christ, you can credit your rescue to a mercy whose cause lies in Him alone and give up any thought of having earned it by being wiser or better.

text: Q. Who is the Redeemer of God's Elect? A. The only Redeemer of God's Elect, is the Lord Jesus Christ; who being the Eternal Son of God, became Man, and so was; and continueth to be God and Man, in two distinct Natures, and one Person for ever.
insight: Do you need someone close enough to understand or strong enough to save? Christ, God and man in two distinct natures and one person forever, is both, so you can bring Him the need pressing on you now.

text: Q. How did Christ, being the Son of God, become Man? A. Christ the Son of God became Man, by taking to himself a true Body, and a reasonable Soul; being conceived by the Power of the Holy Spirit in the Womb of the Virgin Mary, and born of her, yet without Sin.
insight: Two phrases, "a true Body, and a reasonable Soul," guard against a Christ who only seemed human. Because He took both, you can bring Him your tired body and your troubled mind, knowing He carried both, yet without sin.

text: Q. What Offices doth Christ execute as our Redeemer? A. Christ as our Redeemer executeth the Offices of a Prophet, of a Priest, and of a King, both in his Estate of Humiliation and Exaltation.
insight: Anointed ones in Israel served as prophets, priests, and kings, and Christ holds all three offices in both humiliation and exaltation. You can come to Him for truth when confused, forgiveness when guilty, and rule when your life feels out of order.

text: Q. How doth Christ execute the Office of a Prophet? A. Christ executeth the Office of a Prophet, in revealing to us, by his Word and Spirit, the Will of God for our Salvation.
insight: Come to Scripture expecting Christ to teach you if you trust him, since He reveals the will of God for your salvation by His Word and Spirit. You can ask Him before you read to show you what you need, and trust that nothing needful is hidden.

text: Q. How doth Christ execute the Office of a Priest? A. Christ executeth the Office of a Priest, in his once offering up of himself a Sacrifice to satisfy Divine Justice, and reconcile us to God, and in making continual Intercession for us.
insight: Somewhere beyond your sight, Christ is praying for you at this moment. His one offering satisfied divine justice, and His continual intercession goes on, so you can rest on a prayer that never lapses even when your own do.

text: Q. How doth Christ execute the Office of a King? A. Christ executeth the Office of a King, in subduing us to himself, in ruling, and defending us, and in restraining and conquering all his and our Enemies.
insight: Where in your life is Christ king in name only? He subdues, rules, defends, and restrains every enemy, so you can hand Him one specific area, your schedule, your tongue, or your money, and ask Him to rule it.

text: Q. Wherein did Christ's Humiliation consist? A. Christ's Humiliation consisted in his being born, and that in a low Condition; made under the Law, undergoing the Miseries of this Life, the Wrath of God, and the cursed Death of the Cross; in being buried, and continuing under the Power of Death for a time. Mat. 12:40.
insight: Christ's humiliation went all the way down: born in a low condition, made under the law, bearing the wrath of God and the cursed death of the cross, and held under the power of death for a time. No depth of suffering you reach lies beneath where He has gone, and you can call on Him from wherever you are.

text: Q. Wherein consisteth Christ's Exaltation? A. Christ's Exaltation consisteth in his rising again from the Dead on the third Day, in ascending up into Heaven, in sitting at the right Hand of God the Father, and in coming to judg the World at the last Day.
insight: Easter can seem like the end of the story, yet exaltation runs on through ascension, a seat at the Father's right hand, and a return to judge the world. You can hope in a Christ who reigns now and is coming again.

text: Q. How are we made Partakers of the Redemption purchased by Christ? A. We are made Partakers of the Redemption purchased by Christ, by the effectual Application of it to us by his Holy Spirit.
insight: Receiving redemption, in Baptist catechism terms, means the Holy Spirit effectually applying to you what Christ purchased. You can thank the Spirit for every grace you have, since He is the one who made it yours.

text: Q. How doth the Spirit apply to us the Redemption purchased by Christ? A. The Spirit applieth to us the Redemption purchased by Chrift, by working Faith in us, and thereby uniting us to Christ, in our effectual Calling.
insight: The Spirit applies Christ's redemption by working faith in us and so uniting us to Christ in effectual calling, which makes faith His gift. You can pray with real hope for friends who do not believe, and hold your own faith with humility, since it came from Him.

text: Q. What is effectual Calling? A. Effectual Calling, is the Work of God's Spirit, whereby, convincing us of our Sin and Misery, enlightening our Minds in the knowledge of Christ, and renewing our Wills, he doth persuade and enable us to embrace Jesus Christ freely offered to us in the Gospel.
insight: Effectual calling is the Spirit's decisive work of convincing, enlightening, and renewing, by which He persuades and enables a sinner to embrace Christ freely offered in the gospel. If you have embraced Christ, you can thank the Spirit for doing what your own will could not, and speak of that same Christ freely to others.

text: Q. What Benefits do they that are effectually called, partake of in this Life? A. They that are effectually called, do in this Life partake of Justification, Adoption, Sanctification, and the several Benefits which in this Life do either accompany or flow from them.
insight: Those effectually called share in this life in justification, adoption, sanctification, and the several benefits that accompany or flow from them. If you are in Christ, you can name these gifts over on spiritually poor days, because you need not wait for heaven to begin enjoying what God has given.

text: Q. What is Justification? A. Justification is an Act of God's free Grace, wherein he pardoneth all our Sins, and accepteth us as Righteous in his sight, only for the Righteousness of Christ imputed us, and received by Faith alone.
insight: Feelings make a poor judge of your standing before God. Justification is a verdict God pronounces, pardoning all your sins and accepting you only for Christ's righteousness received by faith alone, so you can stand on it on your worst days.

text: Q. What is Adoption? A. Adoption is an Act of God's free Grace, whereby we are received into the Number, and have a Right to all the Privileges of the Sons of God.
insight: Orphans who are adopted receive a name, a place at the table, and a right to the inheritance. Adoption gives you a right to all the privileges of God's children, so you can come to the Father with the freedom of someone who belongs.

text: Q. What is Sanctification? A. Sanctification is the Work of God's free Grace, whereby we are renewed in the whole Man after the Image of God, and are enabled more and more to die unto Sin, and live unto Righteousness.
insight: Holiness grows by two motions at once, dying to sin and living to righteousness, as God's free grace renews the whole person. You can expect both in an ordinary day: a habit put to death and a kindness newly possible.

text: Q. What are the Benefits which in this Life do accompany or flow from Justification, Adoption, and Sanctification? A. The Benefits which in this Life do accompany or flow from Justification, Adoption, and Sanctification, are Assurance of God's Love, Peace of Conscience, Joy in the Holy Spirit, Increase of Grace, and Perseverance therein to the End.
insight: Assurance of God's love, peace of conscience, joy in the Holy Spirit, increase of grace, and perseverance to the end all accompany or flow from justification, adoption, and sanctification. If one of them feels thin in you, you can ask God for it plainly, leaning on what He has done in Christ more than on your feelings.

text: Q. What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at their Death? A. The Souls of Believers are at their Death made, perfect in Holiness, and do immediately pass into Glory: And their Bodies being still united to Christ, do rest in their Graves till the Refurrection.
insight: At death a believer's soul is made perfect in holiness and passes at once into glory, while the body, united to Christ, rests in the grave until the resurrection. You can grieve at a Christian's grave with hope, knowing the one you love is with the Lord and the body laid there belongs to Christ and will be raised.

text: Q. What Benefits do Believers receive from Christ at the Resurrection? A. At the Resurrection Believers being raised up in Glory, shall be openly acknowledged, and acquitted in the Day of Judgement, and made perfectly blessed, both in Soul and Body, in the full enjoyment of God, to all Eternity.
insight: At the resurrection believers will be raised in glory, openly acknowledged and acquitted on the Day of Judgment, and made perfectly blessed in soul and body in the full enjoyment of God. If you are in Christ, you can face aging and dying with hope, knowing your body has a future and you will be acquitted before all.

text: Q. But what shall be done to the Wicked at their Death? A. The Souls of the Wicked shall at their death be cast into the Torments of Hell, and their Bodies lie in their Graves, till the Refurrection and Judgment of the Great Day.
insight: Remember the unbelievers you know by name and pray for them. The souls of the wicked go at death to torment while their bodies await judgment, and that sober truth can move you toward compassion and witness while there is time.

text: Q. What is the Duty which God requireth of Man? A. The Duty which God requireth of Man, is Obedience to his Revealed Will.
insight: Guessing at God's secret will can paralyze you. Human duty is obedience to His revealed will, so you can make your next decision by what He has plainly said in Scripture and leave hidden things with Him.

text: Q. What did God at first reveal to Man for the Rule of his Obedience? A. The Rule which God at first revealed to Man for his Obedience, was the Moral Law.
insight: Long before the tablets at Sinai, God had revealed the moral law to Adam as the rule of his obedience. Because that law was given at creation, you can trust it to fit human life in every culture and age, including yours.

text: Q. Where is the Moral Law summarily comprehended? A. The Moral Law is summarily comprehended in the Ten Commandments.
insight: Small enough for a child to memorize and searching enough to expose a lifetime, the Ten Commandments hold the whole moral law in summary. You can pray through one commandment each morning and ask where it finds you.

text: Q. What is the Sum of the Ten Commandments? A. The Sum of the Ten Commandments is, to love the Lord our God, with all our Heart, with all our Soul, with all our Strength, and with all our Mind; and our Neighbour as our Selves.
insight: Four times the summary says "with all," heart, soul, strength, and mind, leaving no corner of you exempt from love for God. You can measure your obedience by that double love for God and neighbor, which reaches further than any checklist.

text: Q. What is the Preface to the Ten Commandments? A. The Preface to the Ten Commandments, is in these words, "I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the Land of Egypt, out of the House of Bondage".
insight: Israel heard "I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out" before a single command was given at Sinai. You obey as someone already rescued, so your obedience can be glad thanks and never a bid for rescue.

text: Q. What doth the Preface to the Ten Commandments teach us? A. The Preface to the Ten Commandments teacheth us, that because God is the LORD, and our God, and Redeemer, therefore we are bound to keep all his Commandments.
insight: The preface gives three grounds for obedience: God is the LORD, He is our God by covenant, and He is our Redeemer. You are bound to His commandments by who He is, by the bond He has made with His people, and by the rescue He has accomplished, so each command comes to you from a God who is yours.

text: Q. Which is the first Commandment? A. The first Commandment is, "Thou shalt have no other Gods before me".
insight: The first commandment is short, but it reaches every rival, whether an idol of wood or anything else we trust, love, and fear as only God should be. When trouble comes, the place you run first for security shows what you trust, and you can make the LORD your refuge.

text: Q. What is required in the first Commandment? A. The first Commandment requireth us, to know and acknowledge God to be the only true God, and our God; and to worship and glorify him accordingly.
insight: Say "my God" when you pray, and mean it. The first commandment requires knowing God as the only true God and as your own, and worshiping Him accordingly, so that correct doctrine becomes personal devotion in you.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the first Commandment? A. The first Commandment forbiddeth the denying, or not worshipping and glorifying the true God, as God, and our God; and the giving that Worship and Glory to any other, which is due unto him a alone.
insight: The first commandment forbids two failures: withholding from the true God the worship due to Him as God and our God, and giving that worship and glory to any other. Whatever good gift you enjoy, you can direct your thanks to Him by name, since the glory for it belongs to Him alone.

text: Q. What are we specially taught by these words "before me" in the first Commandment? A. These words "before me" in the first Commandment, teach us, that God who seeth all things, taketh notice of, and is much displeased with the Sin of having any other God.
insight: The words "before me" teach that God, who sees all things, takes notice of the sin of having any other god and is much displeased with it. Since nothing is hidden from Him, your worship on an ordinary workday matters to Him as much as on the Lord's Day, and you can live the whole week in His sight.

text: Q. Which is the second Commandment? A. The second Commandment is, "Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven Image, or any Likeness of any thing that is in Heaven above, or that is in the Earth beneath, or that is in the Water under the Earth; thou shalt not bow down thy self to them, nor serve them: For I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the Iniquity of the Fathers upon the Children, unto the Third and Fourth Generation of them that hate me; and shewing Mercy unto Thousands of them that love me and keep my Commandments.
insight: The second commandment forbids making likenesses of God and bowing to images in His worship, and backs it with His jealousy, visiting iniquity on those who hate Him and showing mercy to thousands who love Him. God sets the terms on which He is worshiped, and you can come to Him by those terms, trusting a mercy that reaches to thousands.

text: Q. What is required in the second Commandment? A. The second Commandment requireth, the receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire all such religious Worship and Ordinances, as God hath appointed in his Word.
insight: The second commandment requires receiving, observing, and keeping pure and entire the worship and ordinances God has appointed in His Word, so the church may add nothing of its own devising. When you gather with God's people, you can treasure the Word read and preached, prayer, praise, baptism, and the Lord's Supper as the means He chose.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the second Commandment? A. The second Commandment forbiddeth the worshipping of God by Images, or any other Way not appointed in his Word.
insight: Measure how you worship by the phrase 'any other Way not appointed in his Word.' God forbids images and every invented rite, because he alone decides how he is approached, and the Word, prayer, song, and sacraments he gave are enough for you to meet him.

text: Q. What are the Reasons annexed to the second Commandment? A. The Reasons annexed to the second Commandment are, God's Sovereignty over us, his Propriety in us, and the Zeal he hath to his own Worship.
insight: "Propriety" is an older word for ownership, so God's claim on your worship rests on three grounds: he rules you, he owns you, and he is zealous for the worship he appointed. When you are tempted to shape worship by preference, remember that you belong to the one who sets its terms.

text: Q. Which is the third Commandment? A. The third Commandment is, "Thou shalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain, For the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his Name in vain".
insight: Naming God vainly reaches further than cursing; it covers careless prayer, hollow praise, and promises made and broken in his name. Weigh your words before you invoke the Lord's name for anything less than truth.

text: Q. What is the Reason annexed to the third Commandment? A. The Reason annexed to the third Commandment, is, that however the breakers of this Commandment may escape Punishment from Men, yet the Lord our God will not suffer them to escape his Righteous Judgment.
insight: Human courts may miss a false oath or a broken vow, yet Q&A 61 holds out a judgment that no breaker of the third commandment can slip past. Speak God's name in every promise as someone whose words reach his ear.

text: Q. Which is the fourth Commandment? A. The fourth Commandment is, "Remember the Sabbath Day to keep it holy: Six Days shalt thou labour, and do all thy Work; but the Seventh Day is the Sabbath of the LORD thy God, in it thou shalt not do any Work, thou, nor thy Son, nor thy Daughter, thy Man-servant, nov thy Maid-servant, nor thy Cattel, nor the Stranger that is within thy Gates: For in six Days the LORD made Heaven and Earth, the Sea, and all that in them is, and rested the Seventh Day; wherefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath Day, and hallowed it".
insight: Imagine six days of plowing, then the ox unyoked, the servant resting, and the stranger at the gate given the same day off; the commandment's rest reaches the whole household. Whoever works under your roof or on your schedule, ask what your week gives them.

text: Q. What is required in the fourth Commandment? A. The fourth Commandment requireth, the keeping Holy to God one whole Day in Seven, to be a Sabbath to himself
insight: How much of your Lord's Day would survive if you listed what you gave God and what you kept for yourself? The requirement is "one whole Day in Seven," kept holy to him, which leaves no room for trimming it to a morning slot.

text: Q. Which Day of the Seven hath God appointed to be the Weekly Sabbath? A. Before the Refurrection of Christ, God appointed the Seventh Day of the Week to be the Weekly Sabbath, and the First Day of the Week ever since, to continue to the End of the World, which is the Christian Sabbath.
insight: Early on a first day, women walking to a tomb found it empty, and the weekly Sabbath moved to meet that morning. Each Sunday you rise and gather, you are keeping an appointment the resurrection made.

text: Q. How is the Sabbath to be sanctified? A. The Sabbath is to be sanctified by a holy Resting all that Day, even from such worldly Employments and Recreations as are lawful on other Days; and spending the whole Time in the Public and Private Exercises of God's Worship, except so much as is to be taken up in the Works of Necessity and Mercy.
insight: Some treat the Sabbath as a list of things to avoid; the Baptist Catechism fills it with public and private worship and makes room for works of necessity and mercy. Plan your Sunday by what you will do with God and for your neighbor, and the lawful things you set aside will feel lighter.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the fourth Commandment? A. The fourth Commandment forbiddeth the Omission or careless Performance of the Duties required, and the profaning the Day by Idleness, or doing that which is in it self sinful; or by unnecessary Thoughts, Words, or Works about worldly Employments or Recreations.
insight: The fourth commandment can be broken by omission as well as by open sin: careless worship, idleness, and needless thoughts about work or recreation all fall under its ban. Ask God to make the Lord's Day a delight, and bring your attention to worship along with your body.

text: Q. What are the Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment? A. The Reasons annexed to the fourth Commandment, are God's allowing us six Days of the Week for our own lawful Employments, his challenging a special Propriety in a Seventh, his own Example, and his blessing the Sabbath Day.
insight: Resentment at losing a day fades once you notice God has handed you six for your own lawful work and claimed only one, which he blessed and first kept himself. If Sunday feels like a tax, count the six days it leaves in your hands.

text: Q. Which is the fifth Commandment? A. The fifth Commandment is, "Honour thy Father and thy Mother; that thy Days may be long upon the Land which the LORD thy God give it thee."
insight: The fifth commandment begins the duties owed to our neighbor with father and mother, and it attaches a promise of long days to honoring them. Honor your parents in tone and patience, even long after you have left their house.

text: Q. What is required in the fifth Commandment? A. The fifth Commandment requireth the preserving the Honour, and performing the Duties belonging to every one in their several Places and Relations, as Superiours, Inferiors, or Equals.
insight: Who sits above you, who beside you, and who under your care? The fifth commandment assigns honor and duty to each of those places, so your boss, your coworker, and your child all have something owed them by you this week.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the fifth Commandment? A. The fifth Commandment forbiddeth the neglecting of, or doing any thing against the Honor and Duty which belongeth to every one in their several Places and Relations.
insight: An unreturned call to an aging father, a sarcastic reply to a manager, a younger sibling ignored: each is a small neglect of the honor owed to someone in their place and relation. Watch for these withholdings in yourself before they settle into habit.

text: Q. What is the Reason annexed to the fifth Commandment? A. The reason annexed to the fifth Commandment, is a Promise of long Life and Prosperity (as far as it shall serve for God's Glory, and their own Good) to all such as keep this Commandment.
insight: A promise rides alongside this command: long life and prosperity, so far as they serve God's glory and our good, for those who honor their relations well. Trust that God attaches blessing to ordinary faithfulness, even when you cannot trace the connection.

text: Q. What is the sixth Commandment? A. The sixth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not kill".
insight: Jesus taught in Matthew 5 that anger and contempt toward a brother already fall under "Thou shalt not kill," long before any hand is raised. When you catch yourself nursing contempt for someone, confess it as the root of what this commandment forbids, and remember that the person bears God's image.

text: Q. What is required in the sixth Commandment? A. The sixth Commandment requireth all lawful Endeavors to preserve our own Life, and the Life of others.
insight: Obedience to the sixth commandment is mostly ordinary: sleep, food, a doctor's visit, careful driving, a call to a friend in despair, since it requires "all lawful Endeavors" to preserve life. Your own body counts too, so caring for it is service to the God who made it.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the sixth Commandment? A. The sixth Commandment absolutely forbiddeth the taking away of our own Life; or the Life of our Neighbor unjustly, or whatsoever tendeth thereunto.
insight: God's law guards your own life as firmly as your neighbor's, forbidding whatever tends toward taking either. If despair ever makes your life seem worth ending, the God who forbids it wants you alive, so tell someone you trust and bring that weight to Christ, who carries the weary.

text: Q. Which is the seventh Commandment? A. The seventh Commandment is, "Thou shalt not commit adultery".
insight: The seventh commandment is given in five words, and the questions that follow unfold it into chastity of heart, speech, and behavior. Guard your marriage, or your future one, in small glances and private conversations long before any open line comes near.

text: Q. What is required in the seventh Commandment? A. The seventh Commandment requireth the Preservation of our own, and out Neighbor's Chastity, in Heart, Speech, and Behavior.
insight: The duty of chastity covers your neighbor as well as yourself: it requires the preservation of "our own" chastity and our neighbor's, in heart, speech, and behavior. Think about how your jokes, your attention, and your company make purity easier or harder for the people around you.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the seventh Commandment? A. The seventh Commandment forbiddeth all unchast Thoughts, Words and Actions.
insight: Unchaste thoughts fall under this commandment right alongside unchaste acts; imagination gets no pass that behavior is denied. Take a wandering thought as seriously as you would take a wandering hand.

text: Q. Which is the eighth Commandment? A. The eighth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not steal".
insight: What have you taken lately that no one would miss: an hour of your employer's time, a borrowed book never returned, a figure fudged on a form? The eighth commandment's four words reach every quiet way of taking what belongs to another.

text: Q. What is required in the eighth Commandment? A. The eighth Commandment requireth the lawful procuring, and furthering the Wealth and outward Estate of our selves, and others.
insight: Work honestly and give generously, because the eighth commandment asks you to further the wealth and outward estate of others as well as your own. Look for one way this month your paycheck or your skill can make a neighbor's life more secure.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the eighth Commandment? A. The eighth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever doth, or may, unjustly hinder our own, or our Neighbour's Wealth, or outward Estate.
insight: Hindering a neighbor's livelihood counts as theft under this commandment even when nothing physically changes hands. Consider whether your bargains and your silence ever cost someone else more than they cost you.

text: Q. Which is the ninth Commandment? A. The ninth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour".
insight: Around a dinner table someone mentions an absent friend, and a small exaggeration would get a laugh; that moment is where false witness usually happens. Speak about people who are out of the room as if they could hear every word you say.

text: Q. What is required in the ninth Commandment? A. The ninth Commandment requireth the maintaining and promoting of Truth between Man and Man, and of our own and our Neighbor's good Name, especially in Witness-bearing.
insight: The ninth commandment asks for more than avoiding lies: it requires you to maintain and promote truth and to guard your neighbor's good name as well as your own, especially when bearing witness. When a conversation turns to gossip, be the one who says the kind and accurate thing.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the ninth Commandment? A. The ninth Commandment forbiddeth whatsoever is prejudicial to Truth, or injurious to our own or our Neighbor's good name.
insight: Damage to truth can come through a half-told story, a raised eyebrow, or a silence that lets a lie stand, and the ninth commandment forbids all of it. Before you repeat something about a person, ask whether you know it is true and whether saying it is fair to them.

text: Q. Which is the tenth Commandment? A. The tenth Commandment is, "Thou shalt not covet thy Neighbor's House, that shalt not covet thy Neighbor's Wife, nor his Man-servant, nor his Maid-servant, nor his Ox, nor his Ass, nor any thing that is thy Neighbor's".
insight: Paul said it was this commandment, "Thou shalt not covet," that exposed sin in him (Romans 7:7), because desire hides where outward law-keeping cannot reach. Notice what you keep scrolling back to look at, and name it before God.

text: Q. What is required in the tenth Commandment? A. The tenth Commandment requireth the full Contentment with our own Condition, with a right and charitable frame of Spirit toward our Neighbor, and all that is his.
insight: Envy makes a neighbor's promotion feel like your loss, and the tenth commandment answers with "full Contentment" and a "charitable frame of Spirit" toward all that is his. When good news comes to someone else, practice thanking God for it out loud.

text: Q. What is forbidden in the tenth Commandment? A. The tenth Commandment forbiddeth all Discontentment with our own Estate; envying or grieving at the Good of our Neighbor, and all inordinate Motions and Affections to any thing that is his.
insight: Oddly, the catechism names "grieving at the Good of our Neighbor" as sin, because envy often feels more like sorrow than greed. When another's blessing makes you sad, bring that sadness to God as confession and ask him to make you glad with them.

text: Q. Is any Man able perfectly to keep the Commandments of God? A. No meer Man since the Fall, is able in this Life, perfectly to keep the Commandments of God, but doth daily break them, in Thought, Work, or Deed.
insight: The word "meer" leaves one exception, since Christ was more than a mere man and kept God's commandments perfectly. Your own daily failures are a reason to confess them without pretending and to rest your whole hope on his obedience.

text: Q. Are all Transgressions of the Law equally heinous? A. Some Sins in themselves, and by reason of several Aggravations, are more heinous in the sight of God than others.
insight: Flattening every sin to the same weight can sound humble, yet Scripture weighs some as heavier by their aggravations, such as sinning against clear light or against many people. Measure your own sin by what you knew and whom it hurt, and leave off comparing it with a neighbor's.

text: Q. What doth every Sin deserve? A. Every Sin deserveth God's Wrath and Curse, both in this Life, and that which is to come.
insight: Is there a sin in your life you consider too small to matter? Every sin deserves God's wrath and curse in this life and the next, so the cross you trust was sized for exactly that sin as well.

text: Q. What doth God require of us, that we may escape his Wrath and Curse, due to us for Sin? A. To escape the Wrath and Curse of God due to us for Sin, God requireth of us Faith in Jesus Christ, Repentance unto Life, with the diligent use all the outward Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption.
insight: To escape the wrath due for sin, God requires faith in Christ and repentance unto life, together with a diligent use of the outward means through which Christ gives his benefits. Keep hearing the Word and praying through dry weeks as well as warm ones, since he has chosen to give his benefits through the means you keep using.

text: Q. What is Faith in Jesus Christ? A. Faith in Jesus Christ is a saving Grace, whereby we receive, and rest upon him alone for Salvation, as he is offered to us in the Gospel.
insight: Sitting down in a chair, you stop holding yourself up; the catechism's two verbs for faith, "receive" and "rest upon," describe that kind of trust in Christ alone. Put your full weight on him for salvation as he is offered to you in the gospel.

text: Q. What is Repentance unto Life? A. Repentance unto Life is a saving Grace, whereby a Sinner, out of a true Sense of his Sin, and Apprehension of the Mercy of God in Christ, doth, with grief and hatred of his Sin, turn from it unto God, with full Purpose of, and Endeavor after, new Obedience.
insight: Genuine repentance, as Q&A 92 defines it, moves from a true sense of sin and a grasp of mercy in Christ to grief, hatred of sin, and a turning toward God with purpose of new obedience. Expect your next confession to change your direction as well as your mood.

text: Q. What are the outward Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption? A. The outward in ordinary Means, whereby Christ communicateth to us the Benefits of Redemption, are his Ordinances, especially the Word, Baptism, the Lord's Supper, and Prayer; all which Means are made effectual to the Elect for Salvation.
insight: Boredom with the ordinary things of sermon, water, bread, and prayer can tempt you toward something louder, yet these are the very ordinances Christ uses to communicate the benefits of redemption. Show up to the plain things expecting the Spirit to make them effectual for you.

text: Q. How is the Word made effectual to Salvation? A. The Spirit of God maketh the Reading, but especially the Preaching of the Word, an effectual Means of convincing and converting Sinners; and of building them up in Holiness and Comfort through Faith unto Salvation.
insight: Notice the words "but especially the Preaching": the Spirit uses your private reading of Scripture, yet he gives particular weight to the sermon for convincing, converting, and building up sinners. Listen on Sunday as someone the Spirit may be addressing directly.

text: Q. How is the Word to be read and heard, that it may become effectual to Salvation? A. That the Word may become effectual to Salvation, we must attend thereunto with Diligence, Preparation, and Prayer; receive it with Faith and Love, lay it up in our Hearts, and practice it in our Lives.
insight: On Saturday night, pray over the passage you will hear, get to bed at a decent hour, and plan to lay the sermon up in your heart and practice it in your life. Diligence, preparation, and prayer are the posture the catechism asks of every hearer.

text: Q. How do Baptism and the Lord's Supper, become effectual Means of Salvation? A. Baptism and the Lord's Supper become effectual Means of Salvation, not for any Virtue in them, or in him that doth administer them, but only by the Blessing of Christ, and the working of the Spirit in those that by Faith received them.
insight: Baptism and the Supper carry no power of their own, and none from the holiness of the one who administers them; Q&A 96 locates their effect in Christ's blessing and the Spirit's work in those who receive by faith. So come to the font and table with confidence, even when an ordinary, imperfect pastor serves you.

text: Q. What is Baptism? A. Baptism is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ, to be unto the Party baptised, a Sign of his Fellowship with him, in his Death, Burial, and Resurrection; of his being ingrafted into him; of Remission of Sins; and of his giving up himself unto God through Jesus Christ, to live and walk in newness of Life.
insight: Baptism signs union with Christ in his death, burial, and resurrection, and the word "ingrafted" pictures a cutting set into living stock to draw on its root. If you are in Christ, your fruit in newness of life comes from the life you draw from him.

text: Q. To whom is Baptism to be administered? A. Baptism is to be administered to all those, who actually profess Repentance toward God, Faith in, and Obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ, and to none other.
insight: Baptism belongs to those who themselves profess repentance toward God and faith in and obedience to Christ, "and to none other." If you trust Christ and have never been baptized, speak with a pastor about confessing that faith in the water.

text: Q. Are the Infants of such as are Professing Believers to be baptized? A. The Infants of such as are professing Believers are not to be baptized, because there is neither Command, or Example in the Holy Scriptures, or certain Consequence from them to baptize such.
insight: Particular Baptists in seventeenth-century England, dissenting from the national church's practice of infant baptism, argued from Scripture's lack of command, example, or certain consequence. Whatever your convictions on baptism, trace them to Scripture as carefully as they did.

text: Q. How is Baptism rightly administered? A. Baptism is rightly administered, by Immersion, wore dipping the whole Body of the Party in Water, into the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, according to Christ's Institution, and the Practice of the Apostles; and not by the sprinkling or pouring of Water, or dipping some Part of the Body, after the Tradition of Men.
insight: The catechism requires immersion, dipping "the whole Body" into water in the triune name, because it reads that as Christ's institution and the apostles' practice. When you next watch a baptism, see in the going under and rising the burial and resurrection with Christ that Q&A 97 names.

text: Q. What is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized? A. It is the Duty of such who are rightly baptized, to give up themselves to some particular and orderly Church of Jesus Christ, that they may walk in all the Commandments and Ordinances of the Lord blameless.
insight: Join a specific congregation, learn names, and submit to its care, because the baptized are told to give themselves up to "some particular and orderly Church." Drifting between churches can keep you from the accountability that helps you walk blameless.

text: Q. What is the Lord's Supper? A. The Lord's Supper is an Ordinance of the New Testament instituted by Jesus Christ; wherein by giving and receiving Bread and Wine, according to his Appointment, his Death is shewed forth; and the worthy Receivers are, not after a Corporal and Carnal manner, but by Faith, made Partakers of his Body and Blood, with all his Benefits, to their spiritual Nourishment, and growth in Grace.
insight: In the giving and receiving of bread and wine, Christ's death is shown forth, and those who receive by faith partake of his body and blood with all his benefits, though in no bodily manner. Take the bread as a proclamation you make with your hands as well as a meal for your soul.

text: Q. Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance? A. They who have been baptized upon a personal Profession of their Faith in Jesus Christ, and Repentance from dead Works.
insight: Why do you come to the table: from a living faith in Christ, or from habit and family custom? The Supper is for those baptized on their own profession of faith and repentance from dead works, so make sure your coming is your own.

text: Q. What is required to the worthy receiving of the Lord's Supper? A. It is required of them that would worthily partake of the Lord's Supper, that they examine themselves, of their Knowledge to discern the Lord's Body, of their Faith to feed upon him, of their Repentance, Love, and new Obedience; lest coming unworthily, they eat and drink Judgment to themselves.
insight: Take two quiet minutes before communion and ask five things: do I discern the Lord's body, do I feed on him by faith, have I repented, do I love, am I obeying? Coming unworthily brings judgment, and honest self-examination is how you come worthily.

text: Q. What is Prayer? A. Prayer is an offering up our Desires to God, by the Assistance of the Holy Spirit, for things agreeable to his Will, in the Name of Christ believing, with Confession of our Sins, and thankful Acknowledgment of his Mercies.
insight: Prayer, in Q&A 105, is an offering up of our desires to God by the Spirit's help and in Christ's name, joined with confession of sins and thanks for mercies. Clumsy words do not disqualify you, so bring the honest desire, the specific sin, and a mercy you can name.

text: Q. What Rule hath God given for our Direction in Prayer? A. The whole Word of God is of use to direct us in Prayer; but the special Rule of Direction is, that Prayer which Christ taught his Disciples, commonly called, The Lord's Prayer.
insight: Use the Lord's Prayer as a map, lingering on each petition and filling it with your own needs, since Christ gave it as the special rule for directing prayer. The rest of Scripture supplies the details, and his pattern gives your praying its order.

text: Q. What doth the Preface of the Lord's Prayer teach us? A. The Preface of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "Our Father which art in Heaven," teacheth us to draw near to God with all holy Reverence and Confidence, as Children to a Father, able and ready to help us; and that we should pray with and for others.
insight: Kids burst into a father's study without an appointment, yet they know whose room it is; "Our Father which art in Heaven" teaches you that same mix of confidence and reverence. That little "Our" also means you pray with and for others, so bring someone else's need along with your own.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the first Petition? A. In the first Petition, which is, "Hallowed be thy Name," we pray, that God would enable us and others, to glorify him in all that, whereby he maketh himself known; and that he would dispose all things to his own Glory.
insight: Hallowing God's name means honoring everything by which he makes himself known: his names, titles, attributes, ordinances, Word, and works. Pray the petition over your own schedule, asking him to order every hour of it, including the ones you guard, toward his glory.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the Second Petition? A. In the second Petition, which is, "Thy Kingdom come," we pray that Satan's Kingdom may be destroyed, and that the Kingdom of Grace may be advanced, our selves and others brought into it and kept in it, and that the Kingdom of Glory may be hastened.
insight: Three kingdoms crowd into "Thy Kingdom come": Satan's to be destroyed, grace's to advance and keep us, glory's to hasten. When you pray it, you are asking for a war to be won and for the end to come, so pray it with a particular person you long to see brought in.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the third Petition? A. In the third Petition, which is, "Thy Will be done on Earth, as it is in Heaven," we pray, that God by his Grace would make us able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his Will in all things, as the Angels do in Heaven.
insight: Resigning yourself to whatever happens can pass for obedience, yet the third petition asks God to make you able and willing to know, obey, and submit to his will as the angels do in heaven. Ask for a heart that wants his will as well as a life that bows to it.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the fourth Petition? A. In the fourth Petition, which is, "Give us this Day our daily Bread," we pray, that of God's free Gift, we may receive a competent Portion of the good Things of this Life, and enjoy his Blessing with them.
insight: Anxiety about next month's bills meets a petition that asks only for this day's bread, received as God's free gift in a competent portion along with his blessing. Ask him for your portion one day at a time, thank him when it comes, and leave tomorrow's in his hands.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the fifth Petition? A. In the fifth Petition, which is, "And forgive us our Debts as we forgive our Debtors," we pray, that God for Christ's sake would freely pardon all our Sins; which we are the rather encouraged to ask, because by his Grace we are enabled from the Heart to forgive others.
insight: Forgiveness asked for and forgiveness extended are tied together in this petition: we ask pardon for Christ's sake, encouraged to ask it because grace has already enabled us to forgive others. Let an unforgiven grudge be the first thing this prayer exposes in you.

text: Q. What do we pray for in the sixth Petition? A. In the sixth Petition, which is, "And lead us not into Temptation, but deliver us from Evil," we pray that God would either keep us from being tempted to Sin, or support and deliver us when we are tempted.
insight: Ask God each morning, before the predictable weak spot in your day, either to keep you from being tempted or to hold you up and deliver you when you are. The sixth petition assumes you need help before the fall as much as after it.

text: Q. What doth the Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer teach? A. The Conclusion of the Lord's Prayer, which is, "For thine is the Kingdom, and the Power, and the Glory, for ever, Amen," teacheth us to take our Encouragement in Prayer from God only, and in our Prayers to praise him, ascribing Kingdom, Power and Glory to him: And in testimony of our Desire, and Assurance to be heard, we say, Amen.
insight: Ending a prayer with "Amen," the catechism explains, testifies both to your desire and to your assurance of being heard. Say it on purpose, as someone confident that kingdom, power, and glory belong to the one you have asked.

text: I believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. I believe in Jesus Christ, God's only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died, and was buried; he descended to the dead. On the third day he rose again; he ascended into heaven, he is seated at the right hand of the Father, and he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.
insight: Besides the Lord himself, the creed names only Mary and Pontius Pilate, fixing the cross to a real governor's term in Judea. The forgiveness of sins confessed a few lines later rests on something done in history, so bring your guilt to Christ on the days you feel least forgiven.

text: We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible.
insight: Does anything in your life feel beyond God's reach, whether a diagnosis you cannot see or a fear you cannot name? The first article calls the Father maker of all things visible and invisible, so nothing hidden from you sits outside his making or his rule.

witness.voice: First Council of Constantsnople, First Council of Nicaea

text: And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all worlds; God of God, Light of Light, very God of very God; begotten, not made, being of one substance with the Father, by whom all things were made.
insight: Arius taught that the Son had a beginning, and the council at Nicaea in 325 answered that he is "of one substance with the Father," very God of very God. Worship Jesus without hedging, because the one who saves you is fully God.

witness.voice: First Council of Constantsnople, First Council of Nicaea

text: Who, for us men and for our salvation, came down from heaven, and was incarnate by the Holy Spirit of the virgin Mary, and was made man; and was crucified also for us under Pontius Pilate; He suffered and was buried; and the third day He rose again, according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven, and sits on the right hand of the Father; and He shall come again, with glory, to judge the quick and the dead; whose kingdom shall have no end.
insight: 'For us men and for our salvation' comes before the incarnation, the cross, and the empty tomb, and gives the reason for all of them. Read each line that follows with your own name in the margin, since he came down for you.

witness.voice: First Council of Constantsnople, First Council of Nicaea

text: And we believe in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Giver of Life; who proceeds from the Father and the Son; who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; who spoke by the prophets.
insight: The Spirit is confessed as "the Lord," proceeding from the Father and the Son and worshipped and glorified together with them, so he is a divine Person to be adored and never a force to be used. Pray to him by name, and ask the Giver of Life to make the words he spoke by the prophets live in you.

witness.voice: First Council of Constantsnople, First Council of Nicaea

text: And we believe in one holy catholic and apostolic Church. We acknowledge one baptism for the remission of sins; and we look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.
insight: Lonely in a small congregation? The one holy catholic and apostolic Church includes every believer across every century, all sharing one baptism and waiting for the same resurrection, so you never pray alone.

witness.voice: First Council of Constantsnople, First Council of Nicaea

text: Whosoever will be saved, before all things it is necessary that he hold the catholic faith. Which faith unless every one do keep whole and undefiled, without doubt he shall perish everlastingly. And the catholic faith is this: that we worship one God in Trinity, and Trinity in Unity; neither confounding the Persons, nor dividing the Essence. For there is one Person of the Father; another of the Son; and another of the Holy Ghost. But the Godhead of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, is all one; the Glory equal, the Majesty coeternal. Such as the Father is; such is the Son; and such is the Holy Ghost. The Father uncreated; the Son uncreated; and the Holy Ghost uncreated.
insight: Despite its name, this creed was written in Latin, most likely generations after Athanasius died, yet it carries his lifelong concern for a whole and undefiled faith in the Trinity. Treat careful thinking about God as part of loving him, since your worship depends on knowing whom you worship.
