text: The Father unlimited; the Son unlimited; and the Holy Ghost unlimited. The Father eternal; the Son eternal; and the Holy Ghost eternal. And yet they are not three eternals; but one eternal. As also there are not three uncreated; nor three infinites, but one uncreated; and one infinite. So likewise the Father is Almighty; the Son Almighty; and the Holy Ghost Almighty. And yet they are not three Almighties; but one Almighty. So the Father is God; the Son is God; and the Holy Ghost is God. And yet they are not three Gods; but one God. So likewise the Father is Lord; the Son Lord; and the Holy Ghost Lord. And yet not three Lords; but one Lord.
insight: Unity of essence means the three Persons share one eternity, one almightiness, one Godhead, so the creed counts "one eternal" and "one Almighty" even as it names Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Whenever you pray to any Person, you are addressing the whole undivided God.

text: For like as we are compelled by the Christian verity; to acknowledge every Person by himself to be God and Lord; So are we forbidden by the catholic religion; to say, There are three Gods, or three Lords. The Father is made of none; neither created, nor begotten. The Son is of the Father alone; not made, nor created; but begotten. The Holy Ghost is of the Father and of the Son; neither made, nor created, nor begotten; but proceeding. So there is one Father, not three Fathers; one Son, not three Sons; one Holy Ghost, not three Holy Ghosts. And in this Trinity none is before, or after another; none is greater, or less than another. But the whole three Persons are coeternal, and coequal.
insight: Can you explain how the Son is begotten and the Spirit proceeds, while none is before or after another? The creed asks you to confess what you cannot picture, so worship a God larger than your diagrams.

text: So that in all things, as aforesaid; the Unity in Trinity, and the Trinity in Unity, is to be worshipped. He therefore that will be saved, let him thus think of the Trinity.
insight: Sing to the Father, Son, and Spirit by name when your church gathers, because the Unity in Trinity is to be worshipped, and thinking of God rightly is meant to end in praise. Choose one hymn that does this and learn it by heart.

text: Furthermore it is necessary to everlasting salvation; that he also believe faithfully the Incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ. For the right Faith is, that we believe and confess; that our Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, is God and Man; God, of the Essence of the Father; begotten before the worlds; and Man, of the Essence of his Mother, born in the world. Perfect God; and perfect Man, of a reasonable soul and human flesh subsisting. Equal to the Father, as touching his Godhead; and inferior to the Father as touching his Manhood. Who although he is God and Man; yet he is not two, but one Christ. One; not by conversion of the Godhead into flesh; but by assumption of the Manhood by God.
insight: God did not turn into a man; the one Christ came "by assumption of the Manhood by God," so he is equal to the Father as God and inferior to the Father as man. When you read of Jesus tired, weeping, or praying to his Father, you are seeing that assumed manhood, and the one who took it lost none of his Godhead.

text: One altogether; not by confusion of Essence; but by unity of Person. For as the reasonable soul and flesh is one man; so God and Man is one Christ; Who suffered for our salvation; descended into hell; rose again the third day from the dead. He ascended into heaven, he sitteth on the right hand of the God the Father Almighty, from whence he will come to judge the living and the dead. At whose coming all men will rise again with their bodies; And shall give account for their own works. And they that have done good shall go into life everlasting; and they that have done evil, into everlasting fire. This is the catholic faith; which except a man believe truly and firmly, he cannot be saved.
insight: The creed pictures one general resurrection at Christ's coming, when all people rise with their bodies to give account for their works, some going to life everlasting and others to everlasting fire. Pray for one neighbor who does not know Christ, and ask God for an opening to speak of him.

text: Therefore, following the holy fathers, we all with one accord teach men to acknowledge one and the same Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, at once complete in Godhead and complete in manhood, truly God and truly man, consisting also of a reasonable soul and body; of one substance with the Father as regards his Godhead, and at the same time of one substance with us as regards his manhood; like us in all respects, apart from sin; as regards his Godhead, begotten of the Father before the ages, but yet as regards his manhood begotten, for us men and for our salvation, of Mary the Virgin, the God-bearer;
insight: The title "God-bearer" guards Christ's person more than Mary's honor: the child she carried was one and the same Son begotten of the Father before the ages. When you picture the baby at Bethlehem, worship him, because that infant was already your Lord and your God.

text: one and the same Christ, Son, Lord, Only-begotten, recognized in two natures, without confusion, without change, without division, without separation; the distinction of natures being in no way annulled by the union, but rather the characteristics of each nature being preserved and coming together to form one person and subsistence, not as parted or separated into two persons, but one and the same Son and Only-begotten God the Word, Lord Jesus Christ; even as the prophets from earliest times spoke of him, and our Lord Jesus Christ himself taught us, and the creed of the fathers has handed down to us.
insight: Hold on to all four negatives, without confusion, change, division, or separation, whenever you think about Jesus, because each one blocks a way of making him less than he is. Pray to him as the one person who is both your brother and your God.

text: The books commonly called Apocrypha, not being of divine inspiration, are no part of the Canon of the Scripture; and therefore are of no authority in the Church of God, nor to be any otherwise approved, or made use of, than other human writings.
insight: In 1546 the Council of Trent declared these books canonical, and a century later Westminster answered by ranking them with other human writings. Read Maccabees with profit if you like, yet give the right to bind your conscience only to what God breathed out.

text: The authority of the holy Scripture, for which it ought to be believed and obeyed, dependeth not upon the testimony of any man or church, but wholly upon God (who is truth itself), the Author thereof; and therefore it is to be received, because it is the Word of God.
insight: Why do you believe the Bible: because a church vouched for it, or because God, "who is truth itself," is speaking in it? Your faith will only be as sturdy as the answer you give, so trace your trust back to the Author.

text: All things in Scripture are not alike plain in themselves, nor alike clear unto all; yet those things which are necessary to be known, believed, and observed, for salvation, are so clearly propounded and opened in some place of Scripture or other, that not only the learned, but the unlearned, in a due use of the ordinary means, may attain unto a sufficient understanding of them.
insight: Perhaps you feel out of your depth beside people who read Greek and quote theologians. What is necessary for salvation is set out plainly enough for "the unlearned" too, so open your Bible with ordinary diligence and expect to understand what matters most.

text: The infallible rule of interpretation of Scripture is the Scripture itself; and therefore, when there is a question about the true and full sense of any scripture (which is not manifold, but one), it must be searched and known by other places that speak more clearly.
insight: Picture a hard verse as a locked room whose key hangs down the hall, in the plainer passages on the same subject. When a text puzzles you, go looking through the rest of Scripture before you reach for a clever theory of your own.

text: The Supreme Judge, by which all controversies of religion are to be determined, and all decrees of councils, opinions of ancient writers, doctrines of men, and private spirits, are to be examined, and in whose sentence we are to rest, can be no other but the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scripture.
insight: Every court has a last bench beyond which no appeal goes, and for every dispute about faith that bench belongs to the Holy Spirit speaking in Scripture. When a teacher, a council, or your own inner hunch disagrees with the Bible, you know whose verdict to rest in.

text: There is but one only living and true God, who is infinite in being and perfection, a most pure spirit, invisible, without body, parts, or passions, immutable, immense, eternal, incomprehensible, almighty, most wise, most holy, most free, most absolute, working all things according to the counsel of his own immutable and most righteous will, for his own glory; most loving, gracious, merciful, long-suffering, abundant in goodness and truth, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin; the rewarder of them that diligently seek him; and withal most just and terrible in his judgments; hating all sin, and who will by no means clear the guilty.
insight: Mercy and justice sit side by side in this long list of attributes, and neither one is allowed to cancel the other out. The God you pray to is both at once, which is exactly why he can be trusted and feared together.

text: In the unity of the Godhead there be three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity: God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost. The Father is of none, neither begotten nor proceeding; the Son is eternally begotten of the Father; the Holy Ghost eternally proceeding from the Father and the Son.
insight: Nicaea in 325 settled that the Son is fully God, and Constantinople in 381 took up the Spirit's deity; these clauses carry both answers, one substance, the Son eternally begotten, the Spirit eternally proceeding. When you pray to the Father through the Son by the Spirit, you stand inside that same confessed faith.

text: God from all eternity did, by the most wise and holy counsel of his own will, freely and unchangeably ordain whatsoever comes to pass; yet so as thereby neither is God the author of sin, nor is violence offered to the will of the creatures, nor is the liberty or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established.
insight: God ordains whatever comes to pass, yet he is not the author of sin, and the liberty of second causes is "rather established" by his decree. So make your choices and pray your prayers as a real agent, answerable for what you do and upheld by a counsel wiser than your own.

text: Although God knows whatsoever may or can come to pass upon all supposed conditions, yet hath he not decreed anything because he foresaw it as future, or as that which would come to pass upon such conditions.
insight: Imagine God peering down the corridor of time to see what you will do and then drawing up plans to match. Westminster denies that order outright: he decreed nothing because he foresaw it, so your future rests on his will, which no surprise can revise.

text: By the decree of God, for the manifestation of his glory, some men and angels are predestinated unto everlasting life, and others fore-ordained to everlasting death.
insight: If this sentence makes you uneasy, you are reading it honestly; the words "for the manifestation of his glory" ask for reverence before explanation. Bring your unease to the God who decreed it, and speak to him about it on your knees before you argue about it with anyone else.

text: These angels and men, thus predestinated and fore-ordained, are particularly and unchangeably designed; and their number is so certain and definite that it can not be either increased or diminished.
insight: The number of those predestinated is "certain and definite," so nothing in history can increase or diminish it. That number is known to God alone, and the offer of Christ in the gospel is addressed to you, so give your attention to that offer and answer it.

text: Those of mankind that are predestinated unto life, God, before the foundation of the world was laid, according to his eternal and immutable purpose, and the secret counsel and good pleasure of his will, hath chosen in Christ, unto everlasting glory, out of his mere free grace and love, without any foresight of faith or good works, or perseverance in either of them, or any other thing in the creature, as conditions, or causes moving him thereunto; and all to the praise of his glorious grace.
insight: God chose his people out of "mere free grace and love," with no foreseen faith, good works, or perseverance serving as a condition or cause, and all of it ends "to the praise of his glorious grace." If you trust Christ, give God the credit for that faith too, since nothing in you moved him to choose.

text: As God hath appointed the elect unto glory, so hath he, by the eternal and most free purpose of his will, fore-ordained all the means thereunto. Wherefore they who are elected, being fallen in Adam, are redeemed by Christ, are effectually called unto faith in Christ by his Spirit working in due season; are justified, adopted, sanctified, and kept by his power through faith unto salvation. Neither are any other redeemed by Christ, effectually called, justified, adopted, sanctified, and saved, but the elect only.
insight: Notice how the list runs from "redeemed" through "called" and "justified" to "kept by his power through faith," because the God who appointed the elect to glory also ordained every means of getting them there. If you trust Christ, see your calling and faith as links in that chain, and take comfort in the purpose behind them.

text: The rest of mankind God was pleased, according to the unsearchable counsel of his own will, whereby he extendeth or withholdeth mercy as he pleaseth, for the glory of his sovereign power over his creatures, to pass by, and to ordain them to dishonor and wrath for their sin, to the praise of his glorious justice.
insight: God is said to do two things to the rest of mankind: pass them by, withholding a mercy no one was owed, and ordain them to wrath "for their sin," so that condemnation rests on real guilt and praises his justice. Let that keep you from calling reprobation cruel, and send you to Christ, who freely offers mercy to sinners.

text: The doctrine of this high mystery of predestination is to be handled with special prudence and care, that men attending the will of God revealed in his Word, and yielding obedience thereunto, may, from the certainty of their effectual vocation, be assured of their eternal election. So shall this doctrine afford matter of praise, reverence, and admiration of God; and of humility, diligence, and abundant consolation to all that sincerely obey the gospel.
insight: Carry predestination the way you would carry a lit candle through a crowded room: with care, aimed at praise and humility instead of guesswork about others. Look to your own calling and obedience, and if you are trusting him, assurance of your election will grow out of that ground.

text: It pleased God the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, for the manifestation of the glory of his eternal power, wisdom, and goodness, in the beginning, to create or make of nothing the world, and all things therein, whether visible or invisible, in the space of six days, and all very good.
insight: Father, Son, and Holy Ghost made the world "of nothing," with no material to work on and no need to meet, and called all of it very good. Everything you have therefore came as a gift, so receive your food, your breath, and the ground under you with thanks to the God who made them.

text: After God had made all other creatures, he created man, male and female, with reasonable and immortal souls, endued with knowledge, righteousness, and true holiness, after his own image, having the law of God written in their hearts, and power to fulfil it; and yet under a possibility of transgressing, being left to the liberty of their own will, which was subject unto change. Beside this law written in their hearts, they received a command not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; which while they kept they were happy in their communion with God, and had dominion over the creatures.
insight: Adam was made with God's law written on his heart and power to fulfil it, yet left to a will "subject unto change," with one outward command beside that inward law. If obedience feels like friction to you, the strain measures what the fall cost, and Christ came to write that law on hearts again.

text: God, the great Creator of all things, doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all creatures, actions, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, according to his infallible fore-knowledge and the free and immutable counsel of his own will, to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, goodness, and mercy.
insight: Empires and afterthoughts alike fall under the same providence, from the greatest thing happening anywhere to the smallest. The same wisdom that governs galaxies is the one governing whatever just interrupted you.

text: Although in relation to the foreknowledge and decree of God, the first cause, all things come to pass immutably and infallibly, yet by the same providence he ordereth them to fall out, according to the nature of second causes, either necessarily, freely, or contingently.
insight: God's decree makes every outcome certain, yet he orders events to fall out "according to the nature of second causes": some necessarily, some freely, some contingently. So when the weather turns or a plan falls through, treat the ordinary causes as real and deal with them wisely, trusting that none of them slipped out of his hand.

text: God, in his ordinary providence, maketh use of means, yet is free to work without, above, and against them, at his pleasure.
insight: Bread on the table, a surgeon's skill, a spring rain: these are the ordinary means God usually works through, and he remains free to work without them, above them, or against them. So take your medicine and pray for healing, since both belong to the same Lord.

text: The almighty power, unsearchable wisdom, and infinite goodness of God so far manifest themselves in his providence that it extendeth itself even to the first fall, and all other sins of angels and men, and that not by a bare permission, but such as hath joined with it a most wise and powerful bounding, and otherwise ordering and governing of them, in a manifold dispensation, to his own holy ends; yet so as the sinfulness thereof proceedeth only from the creature, and not from God; who, being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be the author or approver of sin.
insight: To bound something is to set its limits, and God so bounds and orders every sin, from the first fall onward, toward his holy ends, while the sinfulness comes only from the creature. Whatever evil has touched you had a border drawn around it by a holy God who never approved it.

text: The most wise, righteous, and gracious God doth oftentimes leave for a season his own children to manifold temptations and the corruption of their own hearts, to chastise them for their former sins, or to discover unto them the hidden strength of corruption and deceitfulness of their hearts, that they be humbled; and to raise them to a more close and constant dependence for their support unto himself, and to make them more watchful against all future occasions of sin, and for sundry other just and holy ends.
insight: Maybe you have felt left alone with your worst impulses, surprised by how strong they turned out to be. God sometimes leaves his children "for a season" just so, to humble them and draw them into closer dependence, and that season has an end he has already set.

text: As for those wicked and ungodly men whom God, as a righteous judge, for former sins, doth blind and harden, from them he not only withholdeth his grace, whereby they might have been enlightened in their understandings and wrought upon in their hearts, but sometimes also withdraweth the gifts which they had, and exposeth them to such objects as their corruption makes occasion of sin; and withal, gives them over to their own lusts, the temptations of the world, and the power of Satan; whereby it comes to pass that they harden themselves, even under those means which God useth for the softening of others.
insight: God hardens the wicked by withholding grace, withdrawing gifts they once had, and giving them over to lusts they already love, so that they harden themselves under the very means that soften others. Hear the gospel as a summons to answer promptly, since refusing it again and again is how a heart grows hard.

text: As the providence of God doth, in general, reach to all creatures, so, after a most special manner, it taketh care of his Church, and disposeth all things to the good thereof.
insight: God's providence reaches every creature, yet it cares for his Church "after a most special manner," disposing all things for the good of Christ's body in every age and place. When your own congregation struggles, pray for it trusting that Christ will never abandon the Church he bought, even when a local body falters.

text: Our first parents, being seduced by the subtlety and temptation of Satan, sinned in eating the forbidden fruit. This their sin God was pleased, according to his wise and holy counsel, to permit, having purposed to order it to his own glory.
insight: Did the serpent's cunning catch God off guard? The paragraph answers that God permitted this first sin, "having purposed to order it to his own glory." If the Lord could take the fall itself in hand, you can trust him with the failure that keeps you awake at night.

text: By this sin they fell from their original righteousness and communion with God, and so became dead in sin, and wholly defiled in all the faculties and parts of soul and body.
insight: Which part of you escaped the fall untouched? None, since it left us "wholly defiled in all the faculties and parts of soul and body." Because no room of your house was spared, you need a Redeemer who renovates the whole of it.

text: They being the root of all mankind, the guilt of this sin was imputed, and the same death in sin and corrupted nature conveyed to all their posterity descending from them by ordinary generation.
insight: Adam stood as the root of all mankind, so the guilt of his first sin was imputed, reckoned to his posterity, and a corrupted nature passed to them by ordinary generation. You never had to learn selfishness from anyone, which is why you need a second Adam whose righteousness God counts to those who trust him.

text: From this original corruption, whereby we are utterly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite to all good, and wholly inclined to all evil, do proceed all actual transgressions.
insight: Discouraged that the same sins keep sprouting no matter how many you prune? They grow from one root, an original corruption that leaves us "wholly inclined to all evil," so bring the root to Christ along with every branch you confess.

text: This corruption of nature, during this life, doth remain in those that are regenerated; and although it be through Christ pardoned and mortified, yet both itself and all the motions thereof are truly and properly sin.
insight: Remaining corruption in the regenerate is pardoned through Christ and mortified by his Spirit, yet the text calls both it and all its motions "truly and properly sin." So do not excuse the impulses you never act on; confess them too, and look to Christ for both the forgiveness and the killing of them.

text: Every sin, both original and actual, being a transgression of the righteous law of God, and contrary thereunto, doth, in its own nature, bring guilt upon the sinner, whereby he is bound over to the wrath of God and curse of the law, and so made subject to death, with all miseries spiritual, temporal, and eternal.
insight: Small, respectable sins find no hiding place under the words "every sin, both original and actual," because each one breaks the same righteous law. Take the quiet faults in your week as seriously as the loud ones, and carry them all to the cross.

text: The distance between God and the creature is so great that although reasonable creatures do owe obedience unto him as their Creator, yet they could never have any fruition of him as their blessedness and reward but by some voluntary condescension on God's part, which he hath been pleased to express by way of covenant.
insight: The distance between Creator and creature is so great that no one could enjoy God as a reward by earning him, so God crossed it by "voluntary condescension," expressed by way of covenant. Every promise you might lean on exists because he stooped first, so come to him on the terms he set and ask boldly.

text: The first covenant made with man was a covenant of works, wherein life was promised to Adam, and in him to his posterity, upon condition of perfect and personal obedience.
insight: Life in the first covenant was promised to Adam, and in him to his posterity, on one condition: "perfect and personal obedience," with nothing partial accepted. Measure your own record by that bar, and you will stop hoping in your effort and start hoping in Christ, who obeyed perfectly for his people.

text: Man by his fall having made himself incapable of life by that covenant, the Lord was pleased to make a second, commonly called the covenant of grace: wherein he freely offered unto sinners life and salvation by Jesus Christ, requiring of them faith in him that they may be saved, and promising to give unto all those that are ordained unto life his Holy Spirit, to make them willing and able to believe.
insight: Near the close of the paragraph God promises his Spirit "to make them willing and able to believe," so the faith the covenant requires is also a faith the covenant supplies. If your trust feels small, ask him for more; he pledged to give it.

text: This covenant of grace is frequently set forth in the Scripture by the name of a testament, in reference to the death of Jesus Christ the testator, and to the everlasting inheritance, with all things belonging to it, therein bequeathed.
insight: Wills take effect only when the one who made them dies, and a testament is exactly such a will. Christ is the testator whose death released the inheritance, so everything promised to you in him is as secure as a death that has already happened.

text: This covenant was differently administered in the time of the law and in the time of the gospel: under the law it was administered by promises, prophecies, sacrifices, circumcision, the paschal lamb, and other types and ordinances delivered to the people of the Jews, all fore-signifying Christ to come, which were for that time sufficient and efficacious, through the operation of the Spirit, to instruct and build up the elect in faith in the promised Messiah, by whom they had full remission of sins and eternal salvation; and is called the Old Testament.
insight: Lambs on Passover night, the knife of circumcision, smoke rising from the altar: each was a signpost toward a Messiah yet to come, and through them the Spirit gave real faith and full remission. Old Testament saints looked ahead to the same Christ you look back to.

text: Under the gospel, when Christ the substance was exhibited, the ordinances in which this covenant is dispensed are the preaching of the Word and the administration of the sacraments of Baptism and the Lord's Supper; which, though fewer in number, and administered with more simplicity and less outward glory, yet in them it is held forth in more fulness, evidence, and spiritual efficacy, to all nations, both Jews and Gentiles; and is called the New Testament. There are not, therefore, two covenants of grace differing in substance, but one and the same under various dispensations.
insight: Under the gospel the one covenant of grace is dispensed by preaching and two sacraments, fewer and plainer than the old ceremonies, yet holding Christ forth "in more fulness, evidence, and spiritual efficacy." Come to the sermon and the Lord's table expecting much, because plain bread and ordinary words are the means God has chosen for this age.

text: It pleased God, in his eternal purpose, to choose and ordain the Lord Jesus, his only-begotten Son, to be the Mediator between God and man, the Prophet, Priest, and King; the Head and Saviour of his Church, the Heir of all things, and Judge of the world; unto whom he did, from all eternity, give a people to be his seed, and to be by him in time redeemed, called, justified, sanctified, and glorified.
insight: Whatever you fear this week, ignorance, guilt, or powers bigger than you, some office of Christ answers it: prophet to teach, priest to atone, king to rule and defend. The Father appointed him to all three from eternity, so none of your needs catches him unprepared.

text: The Son of God, the second person in the Trinity, being very and eternal God, of one substance, and equal with the Father, did, when the fulness of time was come, take upon him man's nature, with all the essential properties and common infirmities thereof, yet without sin: being conceived by the power of the Holy Ghost in the womb of the Virgin Mary, of her substance. So that two whole, perfect, and distinct natures, the Godhead and the manhood, were inseparably joined together in one person, without conversion, composition, or confusion. Which person is very God and very man, yet one Christ, the only mediator between God and man.
insight: Two whole natures, Godhead and manhood, are joined in one person without blending into some third thing, the narrowest path between two ancient errors about who Christ is. Because he is fully both, he alone can stand between a holy God and sinful people like you, representing each side without shortchanging either.

text: The Lord Jesus, in his human nature thus united to the divine, was sanctified and anointed with the Holy Spirit above measure; having in him all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, in whom it pleased the Father that all fulness should dwell; to the end that, being holy, harmless, undefiled, and full of grace and truth, he might be thoroughly furnished to execute the office of a mediator and surety. Which office he took not unto himself, but was thereunto called by his Father, who put all power and judgment into his hand, and gave him commandment to execute the same.
insight: In his human nature Christ was anointed with the Spirit "above measure," so that he was "thoroughly furnished" to be mediator and surety, and he took that office by his Father's call. You can bring him every need, because the one who stands between sinners and God lacks nothing and was sent by God himself.

text: This office the Lord Jesus did most willingly undertake, which, that he might discharge, he was made under the law, and did perfectly fulfill it; endured most grievous torments immediately in his soul, and most painful sufferings in his body; was crucified, and died; was buried, and remained under the power of death, yet saw no corruption. On the third day he arose from the dead, with the same body in which he suffered; with which also he ascended into heaven, and there sitteth at the right hand of his Father, making intercession; and shall return to judge men and angels at the end of the world.
insight: Christ undertook his office "most willingly," and that willingness carried him through torments of soul and body, death, and the grave to the resurrection and his intercession at the Father's right hand. When you pray, you come to a Savior who went to the cross gladly and pleads for his people with the same will.

text: The Lord Jesus, by his perfect obedience and sacrifice of himself, which he through the eternal Spirit once offered up unto God, hath fully satisfied the justice of his Father, and purchased not only reconciliation, but an everlasting inheritance in the kingdom of heaven, for all those whom the Father hath given unto him.
insight: Released debtors do not expect to be handed an estate on their way out the prison door, yet Christ's one offering purchased both reconciliation and "an everlasting inheritance" for all the Father gave him. If you are in Christ, you have been forgiven and then enriched, so live like an heir.

text: Although the work of redemption was not actually wrought by Christ till after his incarnation, yet the virtue, efficacy, and benefits thereof were communicated unto the elect, in all ages successively from the beginning of the world, in and by those promises, types, and sacrifices, wherein he was revealed, and signified to be the seed of the woman which should bruise the serpent's head, and the Lamb slain from the beginning of the world, being yesterday and today the same, and forever.
insight: The first gospel promise, that the seed of the woman would bruise the serpent's head, carried the benefits of a redemption Christ had not yet wrought. Read Genesis 3:15 as the gospel's first announcement, and let it tell you that the enemy who tempts you was marked for defeat from the start.

text: Christ, in the work of mediation, acteth according to both natures; by each nature doing that which is proper to itself; yet, by reason of the unity of the person, that which is proper to one nature is sometimes, in Scripture, attributed to the person denominated by the other nature.
insight: Theologians call this the communication of properties: because Christ is one person, Scripture can say "the Lord of glory" was crucified, though he died in his human nature. You may say without flinching that the One who made you also bled for you.

text: To all those for whom Christ hath purchased redemption he doth certainly and effectually apply and communicate the same; making intercession for them, and revealing unto them, in and by the Word, the mysteries of salvation; effectually persuading them by his Spirit to believe and obey; and governing their hearts by his Word and Spirit; overcoming all their enemies by his almighty power and wisdom, in such manner and ways as are most consonant to his wonderful and unsearchable dispensation.
insight: The Christ who purchased redemption is the same Christ who applies it, and he does so "certainly and effectually": interceding, revealing the mysteries of salvation by his Word, and persuading by his Spirit to believe and obey. So listen to the Word expecting him to work through it, since that is how he brings sinners to faith.

text: God hath endued the will of man with that natural liberty, that is neither forced nor by any absolute necessity of nature determined to good or evil.
insight: God gave the human will a natural liberty, neither forced from outside nor determined by any necessity of nature toward good or evil. Your choices are truly your own, so own them before God instead of laying the blame on your circumstances.

text: Man, in his state of innocency, had freedom and power to will and to do that which is good and well-pleasing to God, but yet mutably, so that he might fall from it.
insight: Innocence in Eden sounds like the ideal state, yet Adam held his freedom "mutably," and it could be lost in an afternoon. Your hope rests on something sturdier: a Christ whose obedience never wavered and who keeps those the Father gave him.

text: Man, by his fall into a state of sin, hath wholly lost all ability of will to any spiritual good accompanying salvation; so as a natural man, being altogether averse from that good, and dead in sin, is not able, by his own strength, to convert himself, or to prepare himself thereunto.
insight: Fallen man has "wholly lost all ability of will" to any spiritual good accompanying salvation, and, being dead in sin, cannot convert himself or even prepare himself for it. If you have come to Christ, thank God for moving first; if you have not, call on him for the grace you cannot supply.

text: When God converts a sinner, and translates him into the state of grace, he freeth him from his natural bondage under sin, and by his grace alone enables him freely to will and to do that which is spiritually good; yet so as that, by reason of his remaining corruption, he doth not perfectly, nor only, will that which is good, but doth also will that which is evil.
insight: A converted sinner is freed from bondage and enabled by grace alone to will what is spiritually good, yet remaining corruption means he does not "perfectly, nor only" will the good. If you are in Christ and want God's will in the morning and sin by afternoon, bring the shame to him and keep choosing the good he has made you able to will.

text: The will of man is made perfectly and immutably free to good alone, in the state of glory only.
insight: The will becomes "perfectly and immutably free to good alone" only in the state of glory, which places that freedom ahead of every believer. If you trust Christ and grieve over a divided will, look forward: the tug-of-war you feel belongs to this life and will not follow you into the next.

text: All those whom God hath predestinated unto life, and those only, he is pleased, in his appointed and accepted time, effectually to call, by his Word and Spirit, out of that state of sin and death, in which they are by nature, to grace and salvation by Jesus Christ; enlightening their minds, spiritually and savingly, to understand the things of God; taking away their heart of stone, and giving unto them an heart of flesh; renewing their wills, and by his almighty power determining them to that which is good, and effectually drawing them to Jesus Christ; yet so as they come most freely, being made willing by his grace.
insight: Surgeons do not argue a failing heart into health; they replace it, and God takes away the heart of stone and gives a heart of flesh. When you came to Christ you came freely, because he had made you willing first.

text: This effectual call is of God's free and special grace alone, not from anything at all foreseen in man; who is altogether passive therein, until, being quickened and renewed by the Holy Spirit, he is thereby enabled to answer this call, and to embrace the grace offered and conveyed in it.
insight: Before the Spirit quickens you, you contribute nothing to your own calling; grace does not find a willing partner but creates one out of what was entirely passive. Even your capacity to answer God's call is itself a gift of the grace that called you.

text: Elect infants, dying in infancy, are regenerated and saved by Christ through the Spirit, who worketh when, and where, and how he pleaseth. So also are all other elect persons who are incapable of being outwardly called by the ministry of the Word.
insight: Grieving parents who have buried an infant may take real comfort from this line: the Spirit works "when, and where, and how he pleaseth," and needs no sermon to save the elect. You may commend such a little one to that sovereign mercy and trust his heart where your understanding runs out.

text: Others, not elected, although they may be called by the ministry of the Word, and may have some common operations of the Spirit, yet they never truly come unto Christ, and therefore cannot be saved: much less can men, not professing the Christian religion, be saved in any other way whatsoever, be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature and the law of that religion they do profess; and to assert and maintain that they may is very pernicious, and to be detested.
insight: Pray for your moral, sincere, religious neighbors as people who need Christ, because the paragraph is blunt that diligence in another religion or by the light of nature cannot save. Your kindness to them should include telling them his name.

text: Those whom God effectually calleth he also freely justifieth; not by infusing righteousness into them, but by pardoning their sins, and by accounting and accepting their persons as righteous: not for anything wrought in them, or done by them, but for Christ's sake alone; nor by imputing faith itself, the act of believing, or any other evangelical obedience to them, as their righteousness; but by imputing the obedience and satisfaction of Christ unto them, they receiving and resting on him and his righteousness by faith; which faith they have not of themselves, it is the gift of God.
insight: Trent's decree of 1547 taught justification by righteousness infused into the soul; Westminster answers that God justifies by pardoning sin and imputing Christ's obedience and satisfaction. Rest on Christ's record by faith, and you can stop auditing your own.

text: Faith, thus receiving and resting on Christ and his righteousness, is the alone instrument of justification; yet is it not alone in the person justified, but is ever accompanied with all other saving graces, and is no dead faith, but worketh by love.
insight: Hands receive a gift without earning it, yet a hand is always attached to a living body; so faith alone justifies, while the faith that does so is never alone and "worketh by love." Look for that love in how you treat the people nearest you.

text: Christ, by his obedience and death, did fully discharge the debt of all those that are thus justified, and did make a proper, real, and full satisfaction to his Father's justice in their behalf. Yet inasmuch as he was given by the Father for them, and his obedience and satisfaction accepted in their stead, and both freely, not for anything in them, their justification is only of free grace; that both the exact justice and rich grace of God might be glorified in the justification of sinners.
insight: Christ made "a proper, real, and full satisfaction" to his Father's justice, and the Father freely gave him and accepted his payment, so the justification of sinners displays exact justice and rich grace at once. If you trust Christ, you were never simply let off; your debt was paid in full.

text: God did, from all eternity, decree to justify all the elect, and Christ did, in the fulness of time, die for their sins, and rise again for their justification: nevertheless, they are not justified until the Holy Spirit doth, in due time, actually apply Christ unto them.
insight: God decreed from eternity to justify the elect, and Christ died and rose for their justification, yet no one is justified until the Spirit, in due time, applies Christ to them. So do not rest on a decree you cannot see; come to Christ in faith, since that is how the Spirit joins a sinner to him.

text: God doth continue to forgive the sins of those that are justified; and although they can never fall from the state of justification, yet they may by their sins fall under God's fatherly displeasure, and not have the light of his countenance restored unto them, until they humble themselves, confess their sins, beg pardon, and renew their faith and repentance.
insight: Those who are justified can never fall from that state, yet their sins can bring God's fatherly displeasure and hide the light of his countenance until they humble themselves. If you trust Christ and his face seems hidden after a sin you have excused, the way back is plain: confess it, beg pardon, and renew your faith and repentance.

text: The justification of believers under the Old Testament was, in all these respects, one and the same with the justification of believers under the New Testament.
insight: Many picture Old Testament believers saved by law-keeping and New Testament believers saved by grace. Westminster calls their justification "one and the same," so Abraham and you stand on identical ground: Christ's righteousness credited to those who trust God's promise.

text: All those that are justified God vouchsafeth, in and for his only Son Jesus Christ, to make partakers of the grace of adoption; by which they are taken into the number, and enjoy the liberties and privileges of the children of God; have his name put upon them; receive the Spirit of adoption; have access to the throne of grace with boldness; are enabled to cry, Abba, Father; are pitied, protected, provided for, and chastened by him as by a father; yet never cast off, but sealed to the day of redemption, and inherit the promises, as heirs of everlasting salvation.
insight: The grace of adoption gives believers God's name, the Spirit of adoption, bold access to the throne of grace, and the cry "Abba, Father," and even his chastening comes as a father's. If you are in Christ, receive correction as a child who will never be cast off and is sealed to the day of redemption.

text: They who are effectually called and regenerated, having a new heart and a new spirit created in them, are further sanctified, really and personally, through the virtue of Christ's death and resurrection, by his Word and Spirit dwelling in them; the dominion of the whole body of sin is destroyed, and the several lusts thereof are more and more weakened and mortified, and they more and more quickened and strengthened, in all saving graces, to the practice of true holiness, without which no man shall see the Lord.
insight: Sanctification is real and personal: the dominion of the whole body of sin is destroyed, and its lusts are weakened "more and more" by Christ's Word and Spirit. If you belong to Christ, expect holiness to grow slowly, and fight each temptation as someone whose old master has lost the throne.

text: This sanctification is throughout in the whole man, yet imperfect in this life; there abideth still some remnants of corruption in every part, whence ariseth a continual and irreconcilable war, the flesh lusting against the spirit, and the spirit against the flesh.
insight: Sanctification reaches the whole person yet is imperfect in this life, so the war between flesh and spirit is "continual and irreconcilable," with no truce on either side. If you belong to Christ, do not read a hard fight as a failed faith; take it to him, and rest your assurance on his promises.

text: In which war, although the remaining corruption for a time may much prevail, yet, through the continual supply of strength from the sanctifying Spirit of Christ, the regenerate part doth overcome; and so the saints grow in grace, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
insight: Ask the Spirit of Christ for the strength you lack on days when corruption seems to be winning, because the paragraph promises a "continual supply" and says the regenerate part does overcome. You are fighting with borrowed resources that never run out.

text: The grace of faith, whereby the elect are enabled to believe to the saving of their souls, is the work of the Spirit of Christ in their hearts, and is ordinarily wrought by the ministry of the Word; by which also, and by the administration of the sacraments and prayer, it is increased and strengthened.
insight: Faith is the Spirit's work in the heart, ordinarily wrought by the ministry of the Word and then increased by the sacraments and prayer as well. If your faith feels thin, go to the means he has promised to use: the preaching of the Word, the Lord's table, and prayer.

text: By this faith a Christian believeth to be true whatsoever is revealed in the Word, for the authority of God himself speaking therein; and acteth differently upon that which each particular passage thereof containeth; yielding obedience to the commands, trembling at the threatenings, and embracing the promises of God for this life and that which is to come. But the principal acts of saving faith are accepting, receiving, and resting upon Christ alone for justification, sanctification, and eternal life, by virtue of the covenant of grace.
insight: Three verbs, "accepting, receiving, and resting," name faith's chief work, and every one describes open hands. Obey the commands and tremble at the warnings as you read, but put your whole weight on Christ alone.

text: This faith is different in degrees, weak or strong; may be often and many ways assailed and weakened, but gets the victory; growing up in many to the attainment of a full assurance through Christ, who is both the author and finisher of our faith.
insight: Faith comes in degrees, weak or strong, and though it is "often and many ways assailed and weakened," it gets the victory, because Christ is its author and finisher. Trust him with whatever faith you have, and let full assurance come as he grows it in you.

text: Repentance unto life is an evangelical grace, the doctrine whereof is to be preached by every minister of the gospel, as well as that of faith in Christ.
insight: Luther opened his Ninety-five Theses in 1517 by calling the whole Christian life one of repentance, and Westminster keeps that note by requiring every minister to preach repentance alongside faith. Expect sermons to call you to both, and welcome the call.

text: By it a sinner, out of the sight and sense, not only of the danger, but also of the filthiness and odiousness of his sins, as contrary to the holy nature and righteous law of God, and upon the apprehension of his mercy in Christ to such as are penitent, so grieves for and hates his sins as to turn from them all unto God, purposing and endeavoring to walk with him in all the ways of his commandments.
insight: Sorrow over sin can look like repentance while being mere despair or fear of consequences; the paragraph requires a sight of sin's "filthiness and odiousness" joined to an apprehension of mercy in Christ. Grieve your sins with your eyes on his mercy, and you will find yourself turning toward God.

text: Although repentance be not to be rested in as any satisfaction for sin, or any cause of the pardon thereof, which is the act of God's free grace in Christ; yet is it of such necessity to all sinners that none may expect pardon without it.
insight: Repenting purchases none of your pardon, since forgiveness rests wholly on God's free grace in Christ; yet no one who hopes for that pardon may go on expecting it without also turning from sin. Turning does not earn mercy, but mercy always meets those who are turning toward God.

text: As there is no sin so small but it deserves damnation, so there is no sin so great that it can bring damnation upon those who truly repent.
insight: Refuse both lies this line exposes: that any sin is too small to matter, and that any sin is too large to forgive. Whichever one tempts you, answer it with Christ, whose mercy meets every sinner who truly repents.

text: Men ought not to content themselves with a general repentance, but it is every man's duty to endeavor to repent of his particular sins particularly.
insight: Vague sorrow over sin in general leaves your specific failures undisturbed and easy to keep hiding. Name exactly what you did, one sin at a time, since that particular honesty is where real repentance begins.

text: As every man is bound to make private confession of his sins to God, praying for the pardon thereof, upon which, and the forsaking of them, he shall find mercy; so he that scandalizeth his brother, or the Church of Christ, ought to be willing, by a private or public confession and sorrow for his sin, to declare his repentance to those that are offended, who are thereupon to be reconciled to him, and in love to receive him.
insight: Embarrassment makes you want to settle things with God alone and skip the harder conversation. When your sin has wounded a brother, the divines ask you to declare your repentance to him as well, so that he can be reconciled and receive you in love.

text: Good works are only such as God hath commanded in his holy Word, and not such as, without the warrant thereof, are devised by men out of blind zeal, or upon any pretense of good intention.
insight: Sincerity feels like enough, and many assume a good intention sanctifies whatever it produces. Westminster calls such inventions the fruit of blind zeal; before you launch your next spiritual project, ask where God asked for it.

text: These good works, done in obedience to God's commandments, are the fruits and evidences of a true and lively faith; and by them believers manifest their thankfulness, strengthen their assurance, edify their brethren, adorn the profession of the gospel, stop the mouths of the adversaries, and glorify God, whose workmanship they are, created in Christ Jesus thereunto, that, having their fruit unto holiness, they may have the end, eternal life.
insight: Both nouns, "fruits and evidences," put good works downstream of faith, growing from a life already joined to Christ. Your obedience can be thanks to God and a quiet sign to others, and it never has to be your ticket in.

text: Their ability to do good works is not at all of themselves, but wholly from the Spirit of Christ. And that they may be enabled thereunto, besides the graces they have already received, there is required an actual influence of the same Holy Spirit to work in them to will and to do of his good pleasure; yet are they not hereupon to grow negligent, as if they were not bound to perform any duty unless upon a special motion of the Spirit; but they ought to be diligent in stirring up the grace of God that is in them.
insight: Ask for help before you start the hard thing, and then start it. Your ability to do good comes wholly from the Spirit of Christ, and that same Spirit expects you to stir up the grace he gave instead of waiting for a mood to arrive.

text: They who in their obedience attain to the greatest height which is possible in this life, are so far from being able to supererogate and to do more than God requires, as that they fall short of much which in duty they are bound to do.
insight: Picture a ledger where your good weeks are meant to cover the bad ones. The divines tear it up: even the most advanced saint falls short of what duty already required, so you have no surplus to spend and no need to keep books.

text: We cannot, by our best works, merit pardon of sin, or eternal life at the hand of God, by reason of the great disproportion that is between them and the glory to come, and the infinite distance that is between us and God, whom by them we can neither profit nor satisfy for the debt of our former sins; but when we have done all we can, we have done but our duty, and are unprofitable servants; and because, as they are good, they proceed from his Spirit; and as they are wrought by us, they are defiled and mixed with so much weakness and imperfection that they cannot endure the severity of God's judgment.
insight: Earning means holding a claim on payment, a debt the other party owes you. Between you and an infinite God no such claim can exist, so your best works become gifts of gratitude to a Father who has already covered what you owed.

text: Yet notwithstanding, the persons of believers being accepted through Christ, their good works also are accepted in him, not as though they were in this life wholly unblamable and unreprovable in God's sight; but that he, looking upon them in his Son, is pleased to accept and reward that which is sincere, although accompanied with many weaknesses and imperfections.
insight: Shame whispers that your half-hearted obedience is worthless to God. The Father looks on believers' works in his Son and is pleased to accept and reward what is sincere, though mixed with many weaknesses, so offer him yours.

text: Works done by unregenerate men, although for the matter of them they may be things which God commands, and of good use both to themselves and others; yet because they proceed not from a heart purified by faith, nor are done in a right manner, according to the Word, nor to a right end, the glory of God; they are therefore sinful, and cannot please God, or make a man meet to receive grace from God. And yet their neglect of them is more sinful and displeasing unto God.
insight: Why would a kind deed from an unbelieving heart fail to please God? It lacks a heart purified by faith and an aim at his glory, and yet neglecting it is worse, so do the good in front of you and ask God for the heart behind it.

text: They whom God hath accepted in his Beloved, effectually called and sanctified by his Spirit, can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace; but shall certainly persevere therein to the end, and be eternally saved.
insight: Those whom God has accepted in his Beloved, effectually called and sanctified by his Spirit, can neither totally nor finally fall away, because their perseverance is God's work in them. If you trust Christ, let that certainty send you to the Word, prayer, and the sacraments, the means through which he keeps his people to the end.

text: This perseverance of the saints depends, not upon their own free will, but upon the immutability of the decree of election, flowing from the free and unchangeable love of God the Father; upon the efficacy of the merit and intercession of Jesus Christ; the abiding of the Spirit and of the seed of God within them; and the nature of the covenant of grace: from all which ariseth also the certainty and infallibility thereof.
insight: Four supports hold up perseverance: the Father's unchangeable love, the Son's intercession, the abiding Spirit, and the covenant of grace, with your free will absent from the list. When you doubt you can last, look at what is holding you.

text: Nevertheless they may, through the temptations of Satan and of the world, the prevalency of corruption remaining in them, and the neglect of the means of their preservation, fall into grievous sins; and for a time continue therein: whereby they incur God's displeasure, and grieve his Holy Spirit; come to be deprived of some measure of their graces and comforts; have their hearts hardened, and their consciences wounded; hurt and scandalize others, and bring temporal judgments upon themselves.
insight: Believers may, through temptation, remaining corruption, and neglect of the means of their preservation, fall into grievous sins for a time, and so incur God's displeasure and grieve his Spirit. Guard the means of grace you are most tempted to let slide, and if you have fallen, return to the Father through Christ without delay.

text: Although hypocrites and other unregenerate men may vainly deceive themselves with false hopes and carnal presumptions of being in the favour of God and estate of salvation, which hope of theirs shall perish: yet such as truly believe in the Lord Jesus, and love him in sincerity, endeavoring to walk in all good conscience before him, may in this life be certainly assured that they are in a state of grace, and may rejoice in the hope of the glory of God, which hope shall never make them ashamed.
insight: Hypocrites can deceive themselves with false hopes of God's favour, so the divines tie certain assurance to those who truly believe in Jesus, love him in sincerity, and endeavour to walk in good conscience before him. Test your hope by those marks instead of by the strength of a feeling, and take heart if you find them.

text: This certainty is not a bare conjectural and probable persuasion, grounded upon a fallible hope; but an infallible assurance of faith, founded upon the divine truth of the promises of salvation, the inward evidence of those graces unto which these promises are made, the testimony of the Spirit of adoption witnessing with our spirits that we are the children of God: which Spirit is the earnest of our inheritance, whereby we are sealed to the day of redemption.
insight: Genuine assurance, as the divines define it, rests on three things: the divine truth of God's promises, the inward evidence of grace, and the Spirit of adoption witnessing that you are God's child, if you trust him. You can lean your whole weight on something that solid.

text: God gave to Adam a law, as a covenant of works, by which he bound him and all his posterity to personal, entire, exact, and perpetual obedience; promised life upon the fulfilling, and threatened death upon the breach of it; and endued him with power and ability to keep it.
insight: God gave Adam a law as a covenant of works, binding him and all his posterity to "personal, entire, exact, and perpetual obedience," with life promised and death threatened. Your own obedience cannot meet those terms, so look to Christ, who kept them in full for those who are his.

text: This law, after his fall, continued to be a perfect rule of righteousness; and, as such, was delivered by God upon mount Sinai in ten commandments, and written in two tables; the first four commandments containing our duty towards God, and the other six our duty to man.
insight: Imagine the two stone tables side by side, four commands facing God and six facing your neighbor. Most of us are fond of one table and careless of the other; look this week at the one you tend to neglect.

text: Beside this law, commonly called moral, God was pleased to give to the people of Israel, as a Church under age, ceremonial laws, containing several typical ordinances, partly of worship, prefiguring Christ, his graces, actions, sufferings, and benefits; and partly holding forth divers instructions of moral duties. All which ceremonial laws are now abrogated under the New Testament.
insight: Israel was "a Church under age," given ceremonial laws that partly prefigured Christ, his sufferings, and his benefits, and partly held forth moral duties, and all of them are now abrogated. As you read Leviticus, look for Christ in its rites and for the moral duties they taught, without taking up the ceremonies themselves.

text: To them also, as a body politic, he gave sundry judicial laws, which expired together with the State of that people, not obliging any other, now, further than the general equity thereof may require.
insight: Civil statutes given to Israel died with that nation's particular life as a state, though the equity woven into them has something to teach any government weighing justice. Ask what fairness those old laws protected, and press for the same where you live.

text: The moral law doth forever bind all, as well justified persons as others, to the obedience thereof; and that not only in regard of the matter contained in it, but also in respect of the authority of God the Creator who gave it. Neither doth Christ in the gospel any way dissolve, but much strengthen, this obligation.
insight: Some hear that they are justified and assume the moral law has lost its claim on them. Christ in the gospel much strengthens that obligation, so you keep God's commands as a forgiven child obeying a Father, with no condemnation left in them for you.

text: Neither are the forementioned uses of the law contrary to the grace of the gospel, but do sweetly comply with it: the Spirit of Christ subduing and enabling the will of man to do that freely and cheerfully which the will of God, revealed in the law, requireth to be done.
insight: Law and gospel "sweetly comply," the divines write, because the Spirit of Christ subdues and enables the will to do freely and cheerfully what the law requires. When obedience feels forced, ask him to change what you want, since his work reaches the will itself.

text: God alone is Lord of the conscience, and hath left it free from the doctrines and commandments of men which are in anything contrary to his Word, or beside it, in matters of faith or worship. So that to believe such doctrines, or to obey such commands out of conscience, is to betray true liberty of conscience; and the requiring of an implicit faith, and an absolute and blind obedience, is to destroy liberty of conscience, and reason also.
insight: Refuse to carry rules on your conscience that God never gave, however devout the person who handed them to you. God alone is Lord of the conscience, and obeying such commands out of conscience betrays the liberty he bought for everyone who trusts him.

text: They who, upon pretense of Christian liberty, do practice any sin, or cherish any lust, do thereby destroy the end of Christian liberty; which is, that, being delivered out of the hands of our enemies, we might serve the Lord without fear, in holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.
insight: What is your freedom in Christ for? The divines answer in the words of Zechariah's song: delivered from our enemies, we serve the Lord without fear, in holiness, all our days, so when a liberty you claim is feeding a lust, ask what it was meant to serve.

text: The light of nature showeth that there is a God, who hath lordship and sovereignty over all; is good, and doeth good unto all; and is therefore to be feared, loved, praised, called upon, trusted in, and served with all the heart, and with all the soul, and with all the might. But the acceptable way of worshipping the true God is instituted by himself, and so limited to his own revealed will, that he may not be worshipped according to the imaginations and devices of men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representations or any other way not prescribed in the Holy Scripture.
insight: The light of nature can teach you that God is to be feared, loved, and served, but it cannot teach you how to worship him, because the acceptable way is instituted by God and limited to his revealed will. Before anything is added to worship, ask whether Scripture prescribes it, and leave it out if Scripture does not.

text: Religious worship is to be given to God, the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost; and to him alone: not to angels, saints, or any other creature: and since the fall, not without a Mediator; nor in the mediation of any other but of Christ alone.
insight: Pray to the Father through the Son by the Spirit, and to no one else. Angels and saints are fellow creatures, and since the fall there has been one Mediator only, so you never need a go-between for your go-between.

text: Prayer with thanksgiving, being one special part of religious worship, is by God required of all men; and that it may be accepted, it is to be made in the name of the Son, by the help of his Spirit, according to his will, with understanding, reverence, humility, fervency, faith, love, and perseverance; and, if vocal, in a known tongue.
insight: Prayer with thanksgiving is required of all people, and it is accepted when made in the Son's name, by the Spirit's help, according to God's will, with understanding, reverence, humility, fervency, faith, love, and perseverance. Pick the quality most missing from your prayers and ask the Spirit, who helps you pray, to supply it.

text: Prayer is to be made for things lawful, and for all sorts of men living, or that shall live hereafter; but not for the dead, nor for those of whom it may be known that they have sinned the sin unto death.
insight: Prayer is to be made for lawful things and for all sorts of people, living or yet to live, but not for the dead, nor for those known to have sinned the sin unto death. That leaves nearly everyone you know within reach of your intercession, so name before God the neighbor you had quietly stopped praying for.

text: The reading of the Scriptures with godly fear; the sound preaching; and conscionable hearing of the Word, in obedience unto God with understanding, faith, and reverence; singing of Psalms with grace in the heart; as, also, the due administration and worthy receiving of the sacraments instituted by Christ; are all parts of the ordinary religious worship of God: besides religious oaths, vows, solemn fastings, and thanksgivings upon several occasions; which are, in their several times and seasons, to be used in an holy and religious manner.
insight: Bible read, sermon heard, psalm sung, bread and cup received: the parts of ordinary worship sound plain because they are meant for every week. On a Sunday that feels unremarkable, you are receiving exactly what God appointed.

text: Neither prayer, nor any other part of religious worship, is now, under the gospel, either tied unto, or made more acceptable by any place in which it is performed, or towards which it is directed: but God is to be worshipped everywhere in spirit and truth; as in private families daily, and in secret each one by himself, so more solemnly in the public assemblies, which are not carelessly or willfully to be neglected or forsaken, when God, by his Word or providence, calleth thereunto.
insight: Loneliness can make a kitchen table feel like the only place you meet God. He is worshipped everywhere in spirit and truth, in families daily and in secret, and he calls you to the public assembly too, so bring your private faith into the gathered church this Sunday.

text: As it is of the law of nature that, in general, a due proportion of time be set apart for the worship of God; so, in his Word, by a positive, moral, and perpetual commandment, binding all men in all ages, he hath particularly appointed one day in seven for a Sabbath, to be kept holy unto him: which, from the beginning of the world to the resurrection of Christ, was the last day of the week; and, from the resurrection of Christ, was changed into the first day of the week, which in Scripture is called the Lord's day, and is to be continued to the end of the world, as the Christian Sabbath.
insight: Easter morning moved the day: from creation to the resurrection the Sabbath was the last day of the week, and from then on the first, called the Lord's Day. Plan your week around that morning, since your rest now begins from his finished work.

text: This Sabbath is then kept holy unto the Lord, when men, after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering of their common affairs beforehand, do not only observe an holy rest all the day from their own works, words, and thoughts, about their worldly employments and recreations; but also are taken up the whole time in the public and private exercises of his worship, and in the duties of necessity and mercy.
insight: Finish the errands on Saturday. The divines picture a day of holy rest reached through hearts prepared and common affairs ordered beforehand, then filled with worship and duties of necessity and mercy, and you will keep Sunday better with the list already done.

text: A lawful oath is a part of religious worship, wherein, upon just occasion, the person swearing solemnly calleth God to witness what he asserteth or promiseth; and to judge him according to the truth or falsehood of what he sweareth.
insight: Behind every lawful oath stands God himself, summoned as witness to what you say and judge of whether it is true. That is why an oath counts as worship, and why the words "I swear to God" should never leave your mouth casually.

text: The name of God only is that by which men ought to swear, and therein it is to be used with all holy fear and reverence; therefore to swear vainly or rashly by that glorious and dreadful name, or to swear at all by any other thing, is sinful, and to be abhorred. Yet as, in matters of weight and moment, an oath is warranted by the Word of God, under the New Testament, as well as under the Old, so a lawful oath, being imposed by lawful authority, in such matters ought to be taken.
insight: God's name is the only one to swear by, and using it vainly or rashly is sinful, yet an oath in matters of weight, imposed by lawful authority, ought to be taken. When a court or an office asks you for one, take it with reverence, because you are calling on the one name fit to bear it.

text: Whosoever taketh an oath ought duly to consider the weightiness of so solemn an act, and therein to avouch nothing but what he is fully persuaded is the truth. Neither may any man bind himself by oath to anything but what is good and just, and what he believeth so to be, and what he is able and resolved to perform. Yet it is a sin to refuse an oath touching anything that is good and just, being imposed by lawful authority.
insight: Pause before you promise under oath, and weigh it. You may bind yourself only to what is good and just, what you believe to be true, and what you are able and resolved to perform; anything short of that is a promise you should decline.

text: An oath is to be taken in the plain and common sense of the words, without equivocation or mental reservation. It cannot oblige to sin; but in anything not sinful, being taken, it binds to performance, although to a man's own hurt: nor is it to be violated, although made to heretics or infidels.
insight: An oath is to be taken in the plain and common sense of its words, with no equivocation or mental reservation, and in anything not sinful it binds even to your own hurt, including an oath sworn to an unbeliever. When a lawful promise turns out to cost you, keep it, and mean your words the way your hearer understood them.

text: A vow is of the like nature with a promissory oath, and ought to be made with the like religious care, and to be performed with the like faithfulness.
insight: Private resolutions made to God can seem softer than courtroom oaths because nobody is watching. Westminster puts a vow on the same footing as a promissory oath, so when you vow something to God, make it with religious care and keep it with faithfulness.

text: It is not to be made to any creature, but to God alone: and that it may be accepted, it is to be made voluntarily, out of faith and conscience of duty, in way of thankfulness for mercy received, or for the obtaining of what we want; whereby we more strictly bind ourselves to necessary duties, or to other things, so far and so long as they may fitly conduce thereunto.
insight: A vow is made to God alone, freely, out of faith and conscience of duty, either in thankfulness for mercy received or to obtain what we want, and it binds us more strictly to duties that serve those ends. You may bring a vow to God in need as well as in gratitude, so long as what you promise helps you toward what he already requires.

text: No man may vow to do anything forbidden in the Word of God, or what would hinder any duty therein commanded, or which is not in his own power, and for the performance whereof he hath no promise or ability from God. In which respect, Popish monastical vows of perpetual single life, professed poverty, and regular obedience, are so far from being degrees of higher perfection, that they are superstitious and sinful snares, in which no Christian may entangle himself.
insight: Medieval monasteries asked for vows of perpetual single life, professed poverty, and regular obedience, and Westminster calls them superstitious and sinful snares. Before you promise God anything, ask whether he has promised you the strength to keep it.

text: God, the Supreme Lord and King of all the world, hath ordained civil magistrates to be under him, over the people, for his own glory and the public good, and to this end hath armed them with the power of the sword, for the defense and encouragement of them that are good, and for the punishment of evil-doers.
insight: God, the supreme Lord and King of all the world, ordained civil magistrates under himself and armed them with the sword for his glory and the public good, to encourage those who do good and punish evildoers. Pray for the officials over you by name, asking that they wield that power for the purpose God gave it.

text: It is lawful for Christians to accept and execute the office of a magistrate when called thereunto; in the managing whereof, as they ought especially to maintain piety, justice, and peace, according to the wholesome laws of each commonwealth, so, for that end, they may lawfully, now under the New Testament, wage war upon just and necessary occasion.
insight: Public office is not off-limits to a Christian conscience, and neither, in a just cause, is bearing arms in its defense; piety and justice can share the same hands. Serve faithfully in whatever public role you hold, without treating it as beneath your calling.

text: The civil magistrate may not assume to himself the administration of the Word and Sacraments, or the power of the keys of the kingdom of heaven: yet he hath authority, and it is his duty to take order, that unity and peace be preserved in the Church, that the truth of God be kept pure and entire, that all blasphemies and heresies be suppressed, all corruptions and abuses in worship and discipline prevented or reformed, and all the ordinances of God duly settled, administered, and observed. For the better effecting whereof he hath power to call synods, to be present at them, and to provide that whatsoever is transacted in them be according to the mind of God.
insight: Even the 1647 text denies any ruler the administration of Word and Sacraments or the power of the keys, a line American Presbyterians kept in 1788 while striking out his power to call synods and suppress heresies. Pray for rulers who leave preaching, baptism, the Supper, and church discipline to the officers Christ appointed.

text: It is the duty of people to pray for magistrates, to honor their persons, to pay them tribute and other dues, to obey their lawful commands, and to be subject to their authority, for conscience' sake. Infidelity or difference in religion doth not make void the magistrate's just and legal authority, nor free the people from their due obedience to him: from which ecclesiastical persons are not exempted; much less hath the Pope any power or jurisdiction over them in their dominions, or over any of their people; and least of all to deprive them of their dominions or lives, if he shall judge them to be heretics, or upon any other pretense whatsoever.
insight: Keep honoring the ruler whose religion you reject. Unbelief or difference in religion does not void a magistrate's just and legal authority, so you pray for him, pay what is owed, and obey his lawful commands for conscience' sake.

text: Marriage is to be between one man and one woman: neither is it lawful for any man to have more than one wife, nor for any woman to have more than one husband at the same time.
insight: Marriage joins one man and one woman, and the divines forbid any man to have more than one wife, or any woman more than one husband, at the same time. Whether you are married or hope to be, give your whole marital loyalty to one person and guard it from every rival.

text: Marriage was ordained for the mutual help of husband and wife; for the increase of mankind with a legitimate issue, and of the Church with an holy seed; and for preventing of uncleanness.
insight: Westminster names three ends of marriage: the mutual help of husband and wife, the increase of mankind and of the church with a holy seed, and the prevention of uncleanness. If you are married, count the ordinary help you give each other on a tired evening as one of the purposes God gave marriage.

text: It is lawful for all sorts of people to marry who are able with judgment to give their consent. Yet it is the duty of Christians to marry only in the Lord. And therefore, such as profess the true reformed religion should not marry with infidels, Papists, or other idolaters: neither should such as are godly be unequally yoked, by marrying with such as are notoriously wicked in their life, or maintain damnable heresies.
