insight: Weigh a person's faith before you weigh their charm. Anyone able to consent with judgment may lawfully marry, yet Christians are called to marry only in the Lord, since a shared faith carries a home through what affection alone cannot.

text: Marriage ought not to be within the degrees of consanguinity or affinity forbidden in the Word; nor can such incestuous marriages ever be made lawful by any law of man, or consent of parties, so as those persons may live together as man and wife. The man may not marry any of his wife's kindred nearer in blood than he may of his own, nor the woman of her husband's kindred nearer in blood than of her own.
insight: A man may not marry any of his wife's kindred nearer in blood than he may of his own, so kinship by marriage follows the lines of kinship by blood, and no law or consent can make such a union lawful. Marriage makes your spouse's family truly your own, so give your in-laws the regard you owe your own relatives.

text: Adultery or fornication, committed after a contract, being detected before marriage, giveth just occasion to the innocent party to dissolve that contract. In the case of adultery after marriage, it is lawful for the innocent party to sue out a divorce, and after the divorce to marry another, as if the offending party were dead.
insight: Adultery or fornication discovered during a betrothal lets the innocent party end the contract, and adultery after marriage permits divorce and remarriage "as if the offending party were dead." If another's unfaithfulness has broken a promise made to you, you need not carry their guilt as your own.

text: Although the corruption of man be such as is apt to study arguments, unduly to put asunder those whom God hath joined together in marriage; yet nothing but adultery, or such wilful desertion as can no way be remedied by the Church or civil magistrate, is cause sufficient of dissolving the bond of marriage; wherein a public and orderly course of proceeding is to be observed; and the persons concerned in it, not left to their own wills and discretion in their own case.
insight: Human corruption is apt to study arguments for putting asunder what God has joined, so the divines allow only adultery or wilful desertion that neither church nor magistrate can remedy, and require a public and orderly process. Be wary of the case your own heart builds, since the text refuses to leave anyone judge in their own cause.

text: The catholic or universal Church, which is invisible, consists of the whole number of the elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one, under Christ the head thereof; and is the spouse, the body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.
insight: Can a church you have never seen be as real as the one you sit in each Sunday? The whole number of the elect, past, present, and future, gathered under Christ, is his spouse and body, and your congregation is one small window onto it.

text: The visible Church, which is also catholic or universal under the gospel (not confined to one nation as before under the law) consists of all those, throughout the world, that profess the true religion, and of their children; and is the kingdom of the Lord Jesus Christ, the house and family of God, out of which there is no ordinary possibility of salvation.
insight: Membership in the visible church belongs to all who profess the true religion together with their children, and outside it there is no ordinary possibility of salvation. Treat the children in your pew as members being raised, and bring your own into its life.

text: Unto this catholic visible Church Christ hath given the ministry, oracles, and ordinances of God, for the gathering and perfecting of the saints, in this life, to the end of the world: and doth by his own presence and Spirit, according to his promise, make them effectual thereunto.
insight: Christ has given his visible church the ministry, the oracles, and the ordinances of God for gathering and perfecting the saints, and by his own presence and Spirit he makes them effectual. The preaching in your church is one of the means he uses to gather people, so pray for your minister and bring someone to hear.

text: This catholic Church hath been sometimes more, sometimes less visible. And particular churches, which are members thereof, are more or less pure, according as the doctrine of the gospel is taught and embraced, ordinances administered, and public worship performed more or less purely in them.
insight: Particular churches are more or less pure according as the gospel is taught and embraced, the ordinances administered, and public worship performed in them. If you are choosing a congregation, give those marks more weight than the commute or the coffee.

text: The purest churches under heaven are subject both to mixture and error; and some have so degenerated as to become no churches of Christ, but synagogues of Satan. Nevertheless, there shall be always a Church on earth to worship God according to his will.
insight: Corruption can reach even the best churches, and some communities calling themselves Christian drift entirely away, yet God has promised there will always be a Church on earth, however visible or hidden it looks at a given moment. Trust that promise on the days your own congregation looks weak.

text: There is no other Head of the Church but the Lord Jesus Christ: nor can the Pope of Rome, in any sense be head thereof; but is that Antichrist, that man of sin and son of perdition, that exalteth himself in the Church against Christ, and all that is called God.
insight: Only Christ heads the church, a claim aimed squarely at papal authority in its own day and just as squarely at any pastor, council, or institution tempted to sit where he alone belongs. Give your ultimate loyalty to Christ alone, and hold every human leader accountable to him.

text: All saints that are united to Jesus Christ their head, by his Spirit and by faith, have fellowship with him in his graces, sufferings, death, resurrection, and glory: and being united to one another in love, they have communion in each other's gifts and graces, and are obliged to the performance of such duties, public and private, as do conduce to their mutual good, both in the inward and outward man.
insight: Hands and feet share one bloodstream, and saints share something like it, joined to Christ their head and to one another in love, with communion in each other's gifts and graces. Offer someone in your congregation the gift God gave you, and receive what others bring without embarrassment.

text: Saints, by profession, are bound to maintain an holy fellowship and communion in the worship of God, and in performing such other spiritual services as tend to their mutual edification; as also in relieving each other in outward things, according to their several abilities and necessities. Which communion, as God offereth opportunity, is to be extended unto all those who, in every place, call upon the name of the Lord Jesus.
insight: Pay the electric bill, bring the meal, or drive the kid to practice. Saints are bound to relieve each other in outward things according to their abilities, and that communion reaches all who call on the name of the Lord Jesus, so find a real need in your church and meet it with what you have.

text: This communion which the saints have with Christ, doth not make them in any wise partakers of the substance of his Godhead, or to be equal with Christ in any respect: either of which to affirm is impious and blasphemous. Nor doth their communion one with another, as saints, take away or infringe the title or propriety which each man hath in his goods and possessions.
insight: Mystical talk of union can blur into the idea that believers become divine, or that fellowship abolishes private property. Westminster calls the first blasphemous and rejects the second, so you can be fully joined to Christ, remain a creature, and keep your house.

text: Sacraments are holy signs and seals of the covenant of grace, immediately instituted by God, to represent Christ and his benefits, and to confirm our interest in him: as also to put a visible difference between those that belong unto the Church and the rest of the world; and solemnly to engage them to the service of God in Christ, according to his Word.
insight: Wax on an old letter proved who sent it, and Westminster calls sacraments "signs and seals" of the covenant of grace in that sense, representing Christ and confirming your interest in him. At the Table you are handed God's own confirmation that you belong.

text: There is in every sacrament a spiritual relation or sacramental union, between the sign and the thing signified; whence it comes to pass that the names and the effects of the one are attributed to the other.
insight: Scripture calls the cup the new covenant and baptism a washing away of sins because sign and thing signified are joined in a spiritual relation, so the name of one passes to the other. Look through the bread to Christ, whose benefits it truly signifies for you.

text: The grace which is exhibited in or by the sacraments, rightly used, is not conferred by any power in them; neither doth the efficacy of a sacrament depend upon the piety or intention of him that doth administer it, but upon the work of the Spirit, and the word of institution, which contains, together with a precept authorizing the use thereof, a promise of benefit to worthy receivers.
insight: Worry about a flawed pastor can shadow your memory of your own baptism. The grace exhibited in a sacrament never depended on the piety or intention of the one administering it; it rests on the Spirit's work and Christ's word of institution, and you can rest there too.

text: There be only two sacraments ordained by Christ our Lord in the Gospel, that is to say, Baptism and the Supper of the Lord: neither of which may be dispensed by any but by a minister of the Word lawfully ordained.
insight: Does it matter who holds the cup? Christ ordained only baptism and the Supper, and entrusted both to lawfully ordained ministers, so receive them from the church's hands as gifts you could never arrange for yourself.

text: The sacraments of the Old Testament, in regard of the spiritual things thereby signified and exhibited, were, for substance, the same with those of the New.
insight: Blood on the doorposts and water in the font carry one gift: for substance, the sacraments of the Old Testament signified the same spiritual things as those of the New. When you read about the Passover, you are reading about your Savior.

text: Baptism is a sacrament of the New Testament, ordained by Jesus Christ, not only for the solemn admission of the party baptized into the visible Church, but also to be unto him a sign and seal of the covenant of grace, of his ingrafting into Christ, of regeneration, of remission of sins, and of his giving up unto God, through Jesus Christ, to walk in newness of life: which sacrament is, by Christ's own appointment, to be continued in his Church until the end of the world.
insight: Ingrafting pictures a cut branch bound into living stock, and baptism signs and seals that union with Christ, along with regeneration, remission of sins, and a life given up to God. A seal points past itself, so let the thought of baptism send you to the Christ it signifies and to the newness of life it calls you to walk in.

text: The outward element to be used in this sacrament is water, wherewith the party is to be baptized in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, by a minister of the gospel lawfully called thereunto.
insight: Christ appointed plain water for baptism, applied in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost by a minister lawfully called, and the divines add no other element to it. When you next watch a baptism, listen for the triune name, since the sign is ordinary and the God named over it is holy.

text: Dipping of the person into the water is not necessary; but baptism is rightly administered by pouring or sprinkling water upon the person.
insight: Arguments over mode can make baptism feel invalid unless you were fully immersed. Westminster judges dipping unnecessary and says pouring or sprinkling administers baptism rightly; whatever quantity of water touched you, the promise it signed was whole.

text: Not only those that do actually profess faith in and obedience unto Christ, but also the infants of one or both believing parents are to be baptized.
insight: Abraham's household received the covenant sign on infants long before any of them could profess faith, and Westminster keeps that pattern: infants of one or both believing parents are to be baptized. Raise your children inside that promise, praying it takes root in real faith.

text: Although it be a great sin to contemn or neglect this ordinance, yet grace and salvation are not so inseparably annexed unto it, as that no person can be regenerated or saved without it, or that all that are baptized are undoubtedly regenerated.
insight: Is the water what saves you? Neglecting baptism is a great sin, yet grace is not so tied to it that no one can be saved without it, nor are all the baptized regenerated; trust Christ himself, and receive baptism as his gift.

text: The efficacy of baptism is not tied to that moment of time wherein it is administered; yet, notwithstanding, by the right use of this ordinance the grace promised is not only offered, but really exhibited and conferred by the Holy Ghost, to such (whether of age or infants) as that grace belongeth unto, according to the counsel of God's own will, in his appointed time.
insight: Baptism's efficacy is not tied to the moment the water is applied, and the Holy Ghost confers the grace it promises on those to whom that grace belongs, according to God's own counsel and in his appointed time. If a baptized child of yours shows no faith yet, keep pleading the promise and leave its timing and its reach with God.

text: The sacrament of baptism is but once to be administered to any person.
insight: Wedding days happen once, and every anniversary looks back to them; baptism works in a similar way, given to any person a single time. When you sin, return to the meaning of the washing you already received instead of hunting for a new one.

text: Our Lord Jesus, in the night wherein he was betrayed, instituted the sacrament of his body and blood, called the Lord's Supper, to be observed in his Church, unto the end of the world; for the perpetual remembrance of the sacrifice of himself in his death, the sealing all benefits thereof unto true believers, their spiritual nourishment and growth in him, their further engagement in and to all duties which they owe unto him; and to be a bond and pledge of their communion with him, and with each other, as members of his mystical body.
insight: Christ instituted the Supper to remember his death, seal its benefits to true believers, nourish them in him, engage them further to their duties, and bind them in communion with him and with each other. Come to the Table ready to be fed and also to renew your commitment to serve him and his people.

text: In this sacrament Christ is not offered up to his Father, nor any real sacrifice made at all for remission of sins of the quick or dead, but only a commemoration of that one offering up of himself, by himself, upon the cross, once for all, and a spiritual oblation of all possible praise unto God for the same; so that the Popish sacrifice of the mass, as they call it, is most abominably injurious to Christ's one only sacrifice, the alone propitiation for all the sins of the elect.
insight: In the Supper Christ is not offered up to his Father, and no real sacrifice is made; his one offering on the cross is commemorated, and praise is offered to God for it. Come to the Table with thanks, since the sacrifice that paid for sin was made once for all and will never need repeating.

text: The Lord Jesus hath, in this ordinance, appointed his ministers to declare his word of institution to the people, to pray, and bless the elements of bread and wine, and thereby to set them apart from a common to an holy use; and to take and break the bread, to take the cup, and (they communicating also themselves) to give both to the communicants; but to none who are not then present in the congregation.
insight: Gather with your congregation when the bread is broken. Christ appointed ministers to declare the words of institution, bless the elements, and give them to the communicants present, so the meal belongs to a church at table together, and you belong at it.

text: Private masses, or receiving this sacrament by a priest, or any other, alone; as likewise the denial of the cup to the people; worshipping the elements, the lifting them up, or carrying them about for adoration, and the reserving them for any pretended religious use, are all contrary to the nature of this sacrament, and to the institution of Christ.
insight: Adoration of the bread, a withheld cup, and private masses all bend the Supper away from its nature and from Christ's institution. Take both bread and cup with your church, and give your worship to the Lord they point to.

text: The outward elements in this sacrament, duly set apart to the uses ordained by Christ, have such relation to him crucified, as that truly, yet sacramentally only, they are sometimes called by the name of the things they represent, to wit, the body and blood of Christ; albeit, in substance and nature, they still remain truly, and only, bread and wine, as they were before.
insight: Superstition turns the bread into something else, and cynicism shrugs it off as a prop; Westminster answers both by calling the elements "truly, and only, bread and wine" while they bear Christ's name. You can eat without magic and without indifference, trusting him by faith.

text: That doctrine which maintains a change of the substance of bread and wine, into the substance of Christ's body and blood (commonly called transubstantiation) by consecration of a priest, or by any other way, is repugnant, not to Scripture alone, but even to common sense and reason; overthroweth the nature of the sacrament; and hath been, and is the cause of manifold superstitions, yea, of gross idolatries.
insight: Lateran IV in 1215 gave transubstantiation official standing, and four centuries later Westminster called it repugnant to Scripture and even to common sense. You need no priestly change in the bread to meet Christ; faith meets him in the supper exactly as he gave it.

text: Worthy receivers, outwardly partaking of the visible elements in this sacrament, do then also inwardly by faith, really and indeed, yet not carnally and corporally, but spiritually, receive and feed upon Christ crucified, and all benefits of his death: the body and blood of Christ being then not corporally or carnally in, with, or under the bread and wine; yet as really, but spiritually, present to the faith of believers in that ordinance, as the elements themselves are, to their outward senses.
insight: Westminster says worthy receivers feed on Christ crucified "really and indeed," yet spiritually, so that he is as present to their faith as the bread is to their senses. When you come to the table trusting him, you receive him and all the benefits of his death, and no less truly for its being by faith.

text: Although ignorant and wicked men receive the outward elements in this sacrament, yet they receive not the thing signified thereby; but by their unworthy coming thereunto are guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, to their own damnation. Wherefore all ignorant and ungodly persons, as they are unfit to enjoy communion with him, so are they unworthy of the Lord's table, and can not, without great sin against Christ, while they remain such, partake of these holy mysteries, or be admitted thereunto.
insight: Fear of the table can keep a tender believer away, yet this warning is aimed at the ignorant and ungodly who come without faith. If you come hungry for Christ and grieved over your sin, you are exactly the guest he invited.

text: The Lord Jesus, as king and head of his Church, hath therein appointed a government in the hand of Church officers, distinct from the civil magistrate.
insight: Headship means Christ alone governs his church, and he placed that rule in church officers distinct from the civil magistrate. When your elders shepherd you, they answer to him first, so pray for them as men who will give him an account.

text: To these officers the keys of the kingdom of heaven are committed, by virtue whereof they have power respectively to retain and remit sins, to shut that kingdom against the impenitent, both by the Word and censures; and to open it unto penitent sinners, by the ministry of the gospel, and by absolution from censures, as occasion shall require.
insight: Westminster commits the keys to church officers, who open the kingdom to penitent sinners by the ministry of the gospel and by absolution from censures, and shut it against the impenitent by the Word and censures. When you hear pardon declared to all who repent and believe, receive it as Christ's word through the ministry he appointed.

text: Church censures are necessary for the reclaiming and gaining of offending brethren; for deterring of others from the like offenses; for purging out of that leaven which might infect the whole lump; for vindicating the honor of Christ, and the holy profession of the gospel; and for preventing the wrath of God, which might justly fall upon the Church, if they should suffer his covenant, and the seals thereof, to be profaned by notorious and obstinate offenders.
insight: Westminster names five ends for church censures, beginning with the reclaiming and gaining of offending brethren and including the protection of the whole lump from leaven. If you ever receive correction from your elders, you can hear it first as an effort to win you back.

text: For the better attaining of these ends, the officers of the Church are to proceed by admonition, suspension from the Sacrament of the Lord's Supper for a season, and by excommunication from the Church, according to the nature of the crime and demerit of the person.
insight: Westminster gives church officers a graded set of censures, admonition, suspension from the Lord's Supper for a season, and excommunication, applied "according to the nature of the crime and demerit of the person." Pray for your elders, that they would weigh each case with that kind of care.

text: For the better government and further edification of the Church, there ought to be such assemblies as are commonly called synods or councils.
insight: For the better government and further edification of the church, Westminster calls for assemblies known as synods or councils, where churches deliberate together. Thank God that your congregation is not meant to stand alone, and pray for the assemblies that serve it.

text: As magistrates may lawfully call a synod of ministers and other fit persons to consult and advise with about matters of religion; so, if magistrates be open enemies to the Church, the ministers of Christ, of themselves, by virtue of their office, or they, with other fit persons, upon delegation from their churches, may meet together in such assemblies.
insight: Written while Parliament and king were at war, this provision allows ministers to meet on their own authority if rulers become open enemies of the church. You belong to a body whose right to gather comes from Christ, whatever the government of your day thinks of it.

text: It belongeth to synods and councils, ministerially, to determine controversies of faith, and cases of conscience; to set down rules and directions for the better ordering of the public worship of God, and government of his Church; to receive complaints in cases of maladministration, and authoritatively to determine the same: which decrees and determinations, if consonant to the Word of God, are to be received with reverence and submission, not only for their agreement with the Word, but also for the power whereby they are made, as being an ordinance of God, appointed thereunto in his Word.
insight: Westminster gives synods and councils a ministerial power to settle controversies, order public worship, and hear complaints, and their decrees, when consonant with the Word, are received "with reverence and submission." If a church assembly rules on a matter that touches you, test its decision by Scripture, and where it agrees, honor it as God's ordinance.

text: All synods or councils since the apostles' times, whether general or particular, may err, and many have erred; therefore they are not to be made the rule of faith or practice, but to be used as a help in both.
insight: Westminster admits that synods and councils since the apostles "may err, and many have erred," so they serve as a help to faith and practice and never as its rule. Read the church's past decisions gratefully, and keep Scripture as the judge you test them by.

text: Synods and councils are to handle or conclude nothing but that which is ecclesiastical: and are not to intermeddle with civil affairs which concern the commonwealth, unless by way of humble petition in cases extraordinary; or by way of advice, for satisfaction of conscience, if they be thereunto required by the civil magistrate.
insight: Westminster limits synods and councils to what is ecclesiastical, allowing them into civil affairs only by humble petition in extraordinary cases or by advice the magistrate requests. You can expect your church's assemblies to keep to the church's business, and pray that they do.

text: The bodies of men, after death, return to dust, and see corruption; but their souls (which neither die nor sleep), having an immortal subsistence, immediately return to God who gave them. The souls of the righteous, being then made perfect in holiness, are received into the highest heavens, where they behold the face of God in light and glory, waiting for the full redemption of their bodies: and the souls of the wicked are cast into hell, where they remain in torments and utter darkness, reserved to the judgment of the great day. Besides these two places for souls separated from their bodies, the Scripture acknowledgeth none.
insight: Grief at a graveside often asks where the person went, and Westminster answers without hedging: the souls of the righteous "immediately return to God." If you have buried a believer, you can picture them beholding God's face, awake and made perfect in holiness.

text: At the last day, such as are found alive shall not die, but be changed; and all the dead shall be raised up with the self-same bodies, and none other, although with different qualities, which shall be united again to their souls forever.
insight: At the last day the dead will be raised "with the self-same bodies, and none other," though with different qualities, and joined again to their souls forever. Care for the body you have with that in view, since the one you wash, feed, and one day lay down is the one God will raise.

text: The bodies of the unjust shall, by the power of Christ, be raised to dishonor; the bodies of the just, by his Spirit, unto honor, and be made conformable to his own glorious body.
insight: Westminster pictures one general resurrection with two outcomes: the bodies of the unjust raised by Christ's power to dishonor, the bodies of the just raised by his Spirit to honor and shaped like his glorious body. Since your body will rise either way, come to Christ while he invites you, for his Spirit raises to glory.

text: God hath appointed a day wherein he will judge the world in righteousness by Jesus Christ, to whom all power and judgment is given of the Father. In which day, not only the apostate angels shall be judged, but likewise all persons, that have lived upon earth, shall appear before the tribunal of Christ, to give an account of their thoughts, words, and deeds; and to receive according to what they have done in the body, whether good or evil.
insight: Suppose you believed that every thought, word, and deed will be brought before Christ's tribunal: how would your week change? You would likely speak more gently in private and confess more quickly, knowing the Judge is also the Savior who died for you.

text: The end of God's appointing this day, is for the manifestation of the glory of his mercy in the eternal salvation of the elect; and of his justice in the damnation of the reprobate, who are wicked and disobedient. For then shall the righteous go into everlasting life, and receive that fulness of joy and refreshing which shall come from the presence of the Lord: but the wicked, who know not God, and obey not the gospel of Jesus Christ, shall be cast into eternal torments, and be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power.
insight: Westminster says God appointed the day of judgment to display the glory of his mercy in saving the elect and of his justice in condemning the wicked who obey not the gospel. Hear both halves as a summons to obey the gospel now, so that the fulness of joy promised to the righteous may be yours.

text: As Christ would have us to be certainly persuaded that there shall be a day of judgment, both to deter all men from sin, and for the greater consolation of the godly in their adversity: so will he have that day unknown to men, that they may shake off all carnal security, and be always watchful, because they know not at what hour the Lord will come; and may be ever prepared to say, Come, Lord Jesus, come quickly. Amen.
insight: Pray the closing words as your own: "Come, Lord Jesus, come quickly." Christ hid the hour so you would shake off carnal security, so keep your lamp trimmed on ordinary days as eagerly as on dramatic ones.

text: We all believe in our hearts and confess with our mouths that there is a single and simple spiritual being, whom we call God- eternal, incomprehensible, invisible, unchangeable, infinite, almighty; completely wise, just, and good, and the overflowing source of all good.
insight: Guido de Brès wrote the Belgic Confession in 1561 for persecuted Reformed believers in the Low Countries, and its first article confesses God as "the overflowing source of all good." When trouble presses on you, begin where he began, with a God who is completely wise, just, and good.

text: We know God by two means: First, by the creation, preservation, and government of the universe, since that universe is before our eyes like a beautiful book in which all creatures, great and small, are as letters to make us ponder the invisible things of God: God's eternal power and divinity, as the apostle Paul says in Romans 1:20. All these things are enough to convict humans and to leave them without excuse. Second, God makes himself known to us more clearly by his holy and divine Word, as much as we need in this life, for God's glory and for our salvation.
insight: Open a picture book with a child and small letters become a story; de Brès calls creation that kind of book, every creature a letter pointing to God. On your walk to the car, read a few letters, then go to Scripture, where he speaks more clearly.

text: We confess that this Word of God was not sent nor delivered "by human will," but that "men and women moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God," as Peter says. (2 Pet. 1:21) Afterward our God- with special care for us and our salvation- commanded his servants, the prophets and apostles, to commit this revealed Word to writing. God, with his own finger, wrote the two tables of the law. Therefore we call such writings holy and divine Scriptures.
insight: The Belgic traces Scripture from speech to writing: men and women moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God, and afterward God commanded prophets and apostles to write down that revealed Word. When you open your Bible, you are reading what he had set down "with special care for us and our salvation."

text: We receive all these books and these only as holy and canonical, for the regulating, founding, and establishing of our faith. And we believe without a doubt all things contained in them- not so much because the church receives and approves them as such but above all because the Holy Spirit testifies in our hearts that they are from God, and also because they prove themselves to be from God. For even the blind themselves are able to see that the things predicted in them do happen.
insight: Some ground their confidence in Scripture on a church's approval; de Brès grounds it on the Spirit's testimony in believers' hearts and on the books proving themselves. You can trust your Bible because God himself vouches for it, and fulfilled prophecy shows it to be his.

text: We distinguish between these holy books and the apocryphal ones, which are the third and fourth books of Esdras; the books of Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Jesus Sirach, Baruch; what was added to the Story of Esther; the Song of the Three Children in the Furnace; the Story of Susannah; the Story of Bel and the Dragon; the Prayer of Manasseh; and the two books of Maccabees. The church may certainly read these books and learn from them as far as they agree with the canonical books. But they do not have such power and virtue that one could confirm from their testimony any point of faith or of the Christian religion. Much less can they detract from the authority of the other holy books.
insight: Enjoy Tobit or Maccabees if you like, but test them against the canonical books, because they cannot confirm "any point of faith." Give your trust to the sixty-six, and treat every other book, however beloved, as a companion and never an authority.

text: We believe and confess also that the Holy Spirit proceeds eternally from the Father and the Son- neither made, nor created, nor begotten, but only proceeding from the two of them. In regard to order, the Spirit is the third person of the Trinity- of one and the same essence, and majesty, and glory, with the Father and the Son, being true and eternal God, as the Holy Scriptures teach us.
insight: The Belgic confesses that the Holy Spirit proceeds eternally from the Father and the Son, neither made nor begotten, and shares one essence, majesty, and glory with them. When you pray to the Father through the Son, the Spirit who helps you is true and eternal God, owed the same worship and trust as the Father and the Son.

text: We believe that- all Adam's descendants having thus fallen into perdition and ruin by the sin of Adam- God showed himself to be as he is: merciful and just. God is merciful in withdrawing and saving from this perdition those who, in the eternal and unchangeable divine counsel, have been elected and chosen in Jesus Christ our Lord by his pure goodness, without any consideration of their works. God is just in leaving the others in their ruin and fall into which they plunged themselves.
insight: Belgic 16 grounds election in God's pure goodness, "without any consideration of their works," so the rescued have no quality to boast of over those left in ruin. If you are in Christ, meet the person you are tempted to look down on with mercy, since grace alone drew you out of the same fall.

text: We believe that our good God, by marvelous divine wisdom and goodness, seeing that Adam and Eve had plunged themselves in this manner into both physical and spiritual death and made themselves completely miserable, set out to find them, though they, trembling all over, were fleeing from God. And God comforted them, promising to give them his Son, born of a woman, (Gal. 4:4) to crush the head of the serpent, (Gen. 3:15) and to make them blessed.
insight: Hiding among the trees, "trembling all over," Adam and Eve hear God coming to find them with a promise of his Son in hand. If you are hiding from him in shame this week, expect the same approach: he comes seeking, and he comes speaking of a Savior.

text: We believe that God- who is perfectly merciful and also very just- sent the Son to assume the nature in which the disobedience had been committed, in order to bear in it the punishment of sin by his most bitter passion and death. So God made known his justice toward his Son, who was charged with our sin, and he poured out his goodness and mercy on us, who are guilty and worthy of damnation, giving to us his Son to die, by a most perfect love, and raising him to life for our justification, in order that by him we might have immortality and eternal life.
insight: The Belgic says God made known his justice toward his Son, who was charged with our sin, and poured out goodness and mercy on the guilty, raising Christ for their justification. When your conscience accuses you, look to the cross, where God's justice and his mercy met in one Savior.

text: We believe that the ceremonies and symbols of the law have ended with the coming of Christ, and that all foreshadowings have come to an end, so that the use of them ought to be abolished among Christians. Yet the truth and substance of these things remain for us in Jesus Christ, in whom they have been fulfilled. Nevertheless, we continue to use the witnesses drawn from the law and prophets to confirm us in the gospel and to regulate our lives with full integrity for the glory of God, according to the will of God.
insight: Skipping Leviticus can feel justified once the ceremonies have ended, yet de Brès says their "truth and substance" remain for us in Jesus Christ. Read the sacrifices as portraits of your Savior, and the law and prophets will confirm you in the gospel.

text: We also believe that although it is useful and good for those who govern the churches to establish and set up a certain order among themselves for maintaining the body of the church, they ought always to guard against deviating from what Christ, our only Master, has ordained for us. Therefore we reject all human innovations and all laws imposed on us, in our worship of God, which bind and force our consciences in any way. So we accept only what is proper to maintain harmony and unity and to keep all in obedience to God. To that end excommunication, with all it involves, according to the Word of God, is required.
insight: Welcome church order that keeps harmony, and resist any human rule that tries to bind your conscience in the worship of God. De Brès rejects "all human innovations" there, so you are free to obey your elders gladly while answering to Christ alone as Master.

text: We believe that because of the depravity of the human race, our good God has ordained kings, princes, and civil officers. God wants the world to be governed by laws and policies so that human lawlessness may be restrained and that everything may be conducted in good order among human beings. For that purpose God has placed the sword in the hands of the government, to punish evil people and protect the good.
insight: De Brès traces civil government to the depravity of the human race: God ordained rulers and placed the sword in their hands to restrain lawlessness, punish evil, and protect the good. You can thank God for the officer patrolling your street without mistaking the state for your savior.

text: As all men have sinned in Adam, lie under the curse, and are deserving of eternal death, God would have done no injustice by leaving them all to perish, and delivering them over to condemnation on account of sin, according to the words of the apostle, "that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world may become guilty before God" (Rom. 3:19). And verse 23: "For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God." And Romans 6:23: "For the wages of sin is death".
insight: The Synod of Dort opened its first head with Romans 3:19, "that every mouth may be stopped," so that guilt is confessed before a word about grace is spoken. Come before God without a defense, since his mercy is offered to those who have stopped pleading their own case.

text: But in this the love of God was manifested, that He sent His only begotten Son into the world, that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish, but have everlasting life. "In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent His only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through Him" (1 John 4:9). "For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life" (John 3:16).
insight: Both verses Dort quotes, 1 John 4:9 and John 3:16, put love first and sending second. When you wonder whether God's heart toward you has cooled, start where Dort starts: he gave his only begotten Son so that you might live through him.

text: And that men may be brought to believe, God mercifully sends the messengers of these most joyful tidings to whom He will and at what time He pleaseth; by whose ministry men are called to repentance and faith in Christ crucified. "How then shall they call on Him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?" (Rom. 10:14-15).
insight: Could anyone call on a Christ they have never heard of? Dort borrows Paul's chain of questions to show that God sends messengers "to whom He will and at what time He pleaseth." Who in your life has never heard the gospel plainly, and could you be the one sent?

text: The wrath of God abideth upon those who believe not this gospel. But such as receive it, and embrace Jesus the Savior by a true and living faith, are by Him delivered from the wrath of God and from destruction, and have the gift of eternal life conferred upon them.
insight: Dort draws a line between two groups: God's wrath abides on those who do not believe the gospel, while those who embrace Jesus by a true and living faith are delivered and given eternal life as a gift. If you are unsure which side you stand on, the gospel invites you to embrace Jesus the Savior, and he delivers all who do.

text: The cause or guilt of this unbelief, as well as of all other sins, is no wise in God, but in man himself; whereas faith in Jesus Christ and salvation through Him is the free gift of God, as it is written: "For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God" (Eph. 2:8). "For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on Him," etc. (Phil. 1:29).
insight: Blame and credit are easy to split evenly, as if God and you each did half. Dort assigns unbelief wholly to man and faith wholly to God's gift, quoting Ephesians 2:8, so when you believe, thank him for the very faith you exercise.

text: There are not various decrees of election, but one and the same decree respecting all those who shall be saved, both under the Old and New Testament; since the Scripture declares the good pleasure, purpose and counsel of the divine will to be one, according to which He hath chosen us from eternity, both to grace and glory, to salvation and the way of salvation, which He hath ordained that we should walk therein.
insight: Dort says there are not various decrees of election but one, covering all who shall be saved under both testaments and choosing them to grace and glory and to the way of salvation. When you read of Abraham or David, you are reading of people saved by the same purpose and the same Christ the gospel offers you.

text: This election was not founded upon foreseen faith, and the obedience of faith, holiness, or any other good quality or disposition in man, as the prerequisite, cause or condition on which it depended; but men are chosen to faith and to the obedience of faith, holiness, etc.; therefore election is the fountain of every saving good, from which proceeds faith, holiness, and the other gifts of salvation, and finally eternal life itself, as its fruits and effects, according to that of the apostle: "He hath chosen us [not because we were but] that we should be holy, and without blame, before Him in love" (Eph. 1:4).
insight: Dort denies that election rests on foreseen faith, holiness, or any good quality: people are chosen "to faith and to the obedience of faith," so holiness is election's fruit and never its condition. If you trust Christ, see your fight against sin as that fruit growing, and thank God for the root.

text: The good pleasure of God is the sole cause of this gracious election, which doth not consist herein, that out of all possible qualities and actions of men God has chosen some as a condition of salvation; but that He was pleased out of the common mass of sinners to adopt some certain persons as a peculiar people to Himself, as it is written, "For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil," etc., it was said (namely to Rebecca): "The elder shall serve the younger. As it is written, Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated" (Rom. 9:11-13). "And as many as were ordained to eternal life believed" (Acts 13:48).
insight: Remonstrant theologians taught that God chose people on the condition of foreseen faith, and Dort answered with Jacob and Esau, set apart before either was born. You can stop auditing your spiritual performance, because God's good pleasure is the sole cause of your adoption, if you belong to him.

text: And as God Himself is most wise, unchangeable, omniscient and omnipotent, so the election made by Him can neither be interrupted nor changed, recalled or annulled; neither can the elect be cast away, nor their number diminished.
insight: Anxiety whispers that even if you belong to Christ, one bad season could cancel your salvation, and Dort answers with four verbs: election cannot be "interrupted nor changed, recalled or annulled." On the morning you feel least chosen, you are as firmly held as on the day you believed.

text: The elect in due time, though in various degrees and in different measures, attain the assurance of this their eternal and unchangeable election, not by inquisitively prying into the secret and deep things of God, but by observing in themselves, with a spiritual joy and holy pleasure, the infallible fruits of election pointed out in the Word of God - such as a true faith in Christ, filial fear, a godly sorrow for sin, a hungering and thirsting after righteousness, etc.
insight: Stop prying into God's secret decree and look for its fruit: true faith in Christ, filial fear, godly sorrow for sin, and hunger for righteousness. If you find even a small hunger in yourself, count it as evidence, and thank God with the "spiritual joy" Dort describes.

text: The sense and certainty of this election afford to the children of God additional matter for daily humiliation before Him, for adoring the depth of His mercies, for cleansing themselves, and rendering grateful returns of ardent love to Him, who first manifested so great love towards them. The consideration of this doctrine of election is so far from encouraging remissness in the observance of the divine commands or from sinking men in carnal security, that these, in the just judgment of God, are the usual effects of rash presumption or of idle and wanton trifling with the grace of election in those who refuse to walk in the ways of the elect.
insight: Dort answers the charge that election breeds carelessness by saying its certainty gives God's children matter for daily humility, adoration, and ardent love, while remissness is the fruit of rash presumption. If you trust Christ, let the thought of his choosing move you to gratitude and glad obedience.

text: Since we are to judge of the will of God from His Word which testifies that the children of believers are holy, not by nature, but in virtue of the covenant of grace, in which they, together with the parents, are comprehended, godly parents have no reason to doubt of the election and salvation of their children whom it pleaseth God to call out of this life in their infancy.
insight: Dort grounds this comfort in the covenant of grace, which comprehends the children of believers with their parents, so godly parents who lose an infant have no reason to doubt that child's salvation. If you grieve a little one, the way to that comfort runs through trust in Christ, so bring your sorrow to him and to a pastor who can open his promise with you.

text: God is not only supremely merciful, but also supremely just. And His justice requires (as He hath revealed Himself in His Word), that our sins committed against His infinite majesty should be punished, not only with temporal, but with eternal punishment, both in body and soul; which we cannot escape unless satisfaction be made to the justice of God.
insight: According to Dort, God's justice requires that sins against his infinite majesty be punished with eternal as well as temporal punishment, in body and soul, unless satisfaction is made. When you are tempted to treat your sin as small, measure it by whom it offends, and then run to the one who made satisfaction.

text: Since therefore we are unable to make that satisfaction in our own persons or to deliver ourselves from the wrath of God, He hath been pleased in His infinite mercy to give His only begotten Son, for our surety, who was made sin, and became a curse for us and in our stead, that He might make satisfaction to divine justice on our behalf.
insight: Co-signers take on a debt the borrower could never repay, and "surety" is Dort's name for Christ in that role. When the debt of your sin comes to mind, remember that your guarantor was made a curse in your stead and paid the whole account, if you trust him.

text: The death of the Son of God is the only and most perfect sacrifice and satisfaction for sin, and is of infinite worth and value, abundantly sufficient to expiate the sins of the whole world.
insight: Does any sin outweigh a sacrifice of "infinite worth and value"? Dort calls the Son's death abundantly sufficient for the whole world, so when your guilt looks enormous, ask whether it outweighs the Son of God, and answer honestly: it cannot.

text: This death derives its infinite value and dignity from these considerations because the person who submitted to it was not only really man and perfectly holy, but also the only begotten Son of God, of the same eternal and infinite essence with the Father and the Holy Spirit, which qualifications were necessary to constitute Him a Savior for us; and because it was attended with a sense of the wrath and curse of God due to us for sin.
insight: Four qualifications, "really man," "perfectly holy," the "only begotten Son," and one essence with the Father and Spirit, give Christ's death its infinite dignity. On days when your faith feels thin, rest on the person who died, because the value of your salvation depends on who he is, if you are in Christ.

text: Moreover, the promise of the gospel is, that whosoever believeth in Christ crucified, shall not perish, but have everlasting life. This promise, together with the command to repent and believe, ought to be declared and published to all nations, and to all persons promiscuously and without distinction, to whom God out of His good pleasure sends the gospel.
insight: Dort wants the gospel promise, with the command to repent and believe, published "to all persons promiscuously and without distinction." Think of a neighbor or coworker you have quietly ruled out, and ask God for an opening to set that promise in front of them.

text: And whereas many who are called by the gospel do not repent nor believe in Christ, but perish in unbelief, this is not owing to any defect or insufficiency in the sacrifice offered by Christ upon the cross, but is wholly to be imputed to themselves.
insight: When a friend walks away from the gospel, you may wonder whether Christ's sacrifice fell short. Dort places the failure "wholly" on unbelief and never on any defect in the cross, so keep offering Christ with confidence in his sufficiency.

text: But as many as truly believe, and are delivered and saved from sin and destruction through the death of Christ, are indebted for this benefit solely to the grace of God, given them in Christ from everlasting, and not to any merit of their own.
insight: Self-congratulation creeps in quietly after years of faithful church attendance, and Dort shuts it down with one word: "solely." Every benefit you have from Christ's death was grace given you from everlasting, so answer every compliment on your faithfulness with thanks to God.

text: This purpose proceeding from everlasting love towards the elect has from the beginning of the world to this day been powerfully accomplished, and will henceforward still continue to be accomplished, notwithstanding all the ineffectual opposition of the gates of hell, so that the elect in due time may be gathered together into one, and that there never may be wanting a church composed of believers, the foundation of which is laid in the blood of Christ, which may steadfastly love and faithfully serve Him as their Savior, who as a bridegroom for his bride, laid down His life for them upon the cross, and which may celebrate His praises here and through all eternity.
insight: Dort traces the church's survival to God's everlasting love: the elect will be gathered, and a church founded in Christ's blood will never be wanting, whatever the gates of hell attempt. When your congregation feels small or tired, serve in the knowledge that Christ, who laid down his life as a bridegroom for his bride, will not lose his church.

text: That Christ by His satisfaction merited neither salvation itself for anyone, nor faith, whereby this satisfaction of Christ unto salvation is effectually appropriated; but that He merited for the Father only the authority or the perfect will to deal again with man, and to prescribe new conditions as He might desire, obedience to which, however, depended on the free will of man, so that it therefore might have come to pass that either none or all should fulfill these conditions. For these adjudge too contemptuously of the death of Christ, do in no wise acknowledge the most important fruit or benefit thereby gained, and bring again out of hell the Pelagian error.
insight: Centuries after Pelagius troubled Augustine's church, Dort heard his error again in the claim that Christ merely earned the Father a right to set new conditions. Your salvation, if you are trusting him, hangs on what Christ merited for you, faith included, and never on your free will meeting terms.

text: That all men have been accepted unto the state of reconciliation and unto the grace of the covenant, so that no one is worthy of condemnation on account of original sin, and that no one shall be condemned because of it, but that all are free from the guilt of original sin For this opinion is repugnant to Scripture which teaches that we are by nature children of wrath (Eph. 2:3).
insight: Were you born neutral, needing only to avoid bad choices? Dort rejects that view with Ephesians 2:3, "by nature children of wrath," so when you look at your own heart, skip the pretense of innocence and go straight to Christ for mercy.

text: Man was originally formed after the image of God. His understanding was adorned with a true and saving knowledge of his Creator and of spiritual things; his heart and will were upright; all his affections pure; and the whole man was holy; but revolting from God by the instigation of the devil, and abusing the freedom of his own will, he forfeited these excellent gifts; and on the contrary entailed on himself blindness of mind, horrible darkness, vanity and perverseness of judgment, became wicked, rebellious, and obdurate in heart and will, and impure in his affections.
insight: Dort describes man as created with a true and saving knowledge of his Creator, an upright will, and pure affections, all forfeited when he revolted from God. When you grieve the blindness and perverseness you find in your own heart, know them as losses from a good creation, and ask God for the renewal only his grace gives.

text: Man after the fall begat children in his own likeness. A corrupt stock produced a corrupt offspring. Hence all the posterity of Adam, Christ only excepted, have derived corruption from their original parent, not by imitation, as the Pelagians of old asserted, but by the propagation of a vicious nature.
insight: Against the Pelagians, Dort says Adam's corruption passes to all his posterity, Christ alone excepted, by the propagation of a vicious nature and not by imitation. When a toddler grabs a toy without being taught, you are watching that inheritance at work, which calls for patience and prayer more than surprise.

text: Therefore all men are conceived in sin, and by nature children of wrath, incapable of saving good, prone to evil, dead in sin, and in bondage thereto, and without the regenerating grace of the Holy Spirit, they are neither able nor willing to return to God, to reform the depravity of their nature, or to dispose themselves to reformation.
insight: Dort says that without the regenerating grace of the Holy Spirit no one is "able nor willing to return to God," or even to dispose themselves to reform. If you are praying for a hard-hearted relative, that same line means everything rests on the Spirit, so pray with more hope than your arguments could give you.

text: There remain, however, in man since the fall, the glimmerings of natural light, whereby he retains some knowledge of God, of natural things, and of the differences between good and evil, and discovers some regard for virtue, good order in society, and for maintaining an orderly external deportment. But so far is this light of nature from being sufficient to bring him to a saving knowledge of God and to true conversion, that he is incapable of using it aright even in things natural and civil. Nay, further, this light, such as it is, man in various ways renders wholly polluted and holds it in unrighteousness, by doing which he becomes inexcusable before God.
insight: Dort grants fallen people glimmerings of natural light, some knowledge of God and some regard for good order, yet says they cannot use it aright even in things natural and civil and render it wholly polluted. When you are tempted to rest on your own decency, seek the saving knowledge of God that only the gospel gives.

text: In the same light are we to consider the law of the decalogue, delivered by God to His peculiar people the Jews by the hands of Moses. For though it discovers the greatness of sin, and more and more convinces man thereof, yet as it neither points out a remedy nor imparts strength to extricate him from misery, and thus being weak through the flesh leaves the transgressor under the curse, man cannot by this law obtain saving grace.
insight: Dort sets the decalogue beside the light of nature: it exposes the greatness of sin and convinces more and more, yet it points out no remedy and imparts no strength, so no one obtains saving grace by it. When the commandments show you your failures, let them send you to Christ for the rescue they were never given to supply.

text: What therefore neither the light of nature, nor the law could do, that God performs by the operation of the Holy Spirit through the Word or ministry of reconciliation, which is the glad tidings concerning the Messiah, by means whereof it hath pleased God to save such as believe, as well under the Old, as under the New Testament.
insight: Which of your efforts to change are running on rules alone? Dort says what neither nature nor law could do, God performs by the Spirit through the glad tidings of the Messiah, so put your hope in that news before your next resolution.

text: As many as are called by the gospel are unfeignedly called. For God hath most earnestly and truly declared in His Word what will be acceptable to Him; namely, that all who are called, should comply with the invitation. He, moreover, seriously promises eternal life and rest to as many as shall come to Him and believe on Him.
insight: Everyone called by the gospel is "unfeignedly called," Dort says, because God earnestly declares that all who are called should come and seriously promises rest to all who believe. If you have hesitated because you suspect the offer hides a catch, take God at his word and come to Christ.

text: The manner of this operation cannot be fully comprehended by believers in this life. Notwithstanding which, they rest satisfied with knowing and experiencing that by this grace of God they are enabled to believe with the heart, and love their Savior.
insight: Frustration at not understanding how God changed your heart is normal, and Dort admits believers cannot fully comprehend it in this life. You can rest satisfied with the evidence, that you believe with the heart and love your Savior, the way you enjoy sunlight without knowing physics.

text: Faith is therefore to be considered as the gift of God, not on account of its being offered by God to man, to be accepted or rejected at his pleasure; but because it is in reality conferred, breathed, and infused into him; or even because God bestows the power or ability to believe, and then expects that man should by the exercise of his own free will, consent to the terms of salvation and actually believe in Christ; but because He who works in man both to will and to do, and indeed all things in all, produces both the will to believe and the act of believing also.
insight: Stacking "conferred, breathed, and infused," Dort makes sure no one pictures faith as a package left on the porch for us to accept or refuse. When you believe, God is producing both the will and the act in you, so your faith itself becomes a reason for worship.

text: That it cannot properly be said that original sin in itself suffices to condemn the whole human race or to deserve temporal and eternal punishment. For these contradict the apostle, who declares: "Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned" (Rom. 5:12). And: "The judgment was by one to condemnation" (Rom. 5:16). And: "The wages of sin is death" (Rom. 6:23).
insight: Dort rejects the view that original sin by itself is too slight to condemn, citing Romans 5:16, "The judgment was by one to condemnation." If you have measured your standing with God only by the sins you remember committing, let Romans 5 show you a deeper need, and bring it to Christ.

text: That the spiritual gifts or the good qualities and virtues, such as goodness, holiness, righteousness, could not belong to the will of man when he was first created, and that these, therefore, could not have been separated therefrom in the fall. For such is contrary to the description of the image of God which the apostle gives in Ephesians 4:24, where he declares that it consists in righteousness and holiness, which undoubtedly belong to the will.
insight: Dort rejects the claim that goodness, holiness, and righteousness never belonged to Adam's created will, because Ephesians 4:24 says the image of God consisted in righteousness and holiness. Since holiness belonged to the will from the start, you can pray for a renewed will knowing you ask for nothing foreign to human nature.

text: Whom God calls, according to his purpose, to the communion of his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, and regenerates by the Holy Spirit, he delivers also from the dominion and slavery of sin in this life; though not altogether from the body of sin, and from the infirmities of the flesh, so long as they continue in this world.
insight: Rule and residue are different things: God breaks sin's dominion over you the moment he regenerates you, while the infirmities of the flesh linger until you leave this world. When an old temptation flares, you can fight it as a freed person resisting a deposed tyrant.

text: Hence spring daily sins of infirmity, and hence spots adhere to the best works of the saints; which furnish them with constant matter for humiliation before God, and flying for refuge to Christ crucified; for mortifying the flesh more and more by the spirit of prayer, and by holy exercises of piety; and for pressing forward to the goal of perfection, till being at length delivered from this body of death, they are brought to reign with the Lamb of God in heaven.
insight: Look closely at your kindest act or most earnest prayer and you will find spots, which Dort says adhere to the best works of the saints. Treat each one as a summons to fly to Christ crucified and press toward the goal, since the Lamb waits at the end of the race.

text: By reason of these remains of indwelling sin, and the temptations of sin and of the world, those who are converted could not persevere in a state of grace, if left to their own strength. But God is faithful, who having conferred grace, mercifully confirms, and powerfully preserves them herein, even to the end.
insight: Back in 1610 the Remonstrants had left open whether true believers could fall from grace, and Dort answered that God "powerfully preserves" them to the end. If you suspect you would drop out on your own strength, you are right, and God's faithfulness is why you won't.

text: By such enormous sins, however, they very highly offend God, incur a deadly guilt, grieve the Holy Spirit, interrupt the exercise of faith, very grievously wound their consciences, and sometimes lose the sense of God's favor, for a time, until on their returning into the right way of serious repentance, the light of God's fatherly countenance again shines upon them.
insight: Darkness after serious sin can feel like God has turned his face away, and Dort is candid that believers may lose the sense of his favor for a time. If you are in that shadow, serious repentance is the road back, and the light of his fatherly countenance shines again on those who walk it.

text: But God, who is rich in mercy, according to his unchangeable purpose of election, does not wholly withdraw the Holy Spirit from his own people, even in their melancholy falls; nor suffers them to proceed so far as to lose the grace of adoption, and forfeit the state of justification, or to commit sins unto death; nor does he permit them to be totally deserted, and to plunge themselves into everlasting destruction.
insight: Dort teaches that God, rich in mercy, never wholly withdraws his Spirit from his own people in their melancholy falls, nor lets them forfeit the grace of adoption. If you belong to Christ and have fallen hard, return to him as a child to a Father who has not disowned you.

text: For in the first place, in these falls he preserves them in the incorruptible seed of regeneration from perishing, or being totally lost; and again, by his Word and Spirit, certainly and effectually renews them to repentance, to a sincere and godly sorrow for their sins, that they may seek and obtain remission in the blood of the Mediator, may again experience the favor of a reconciled God, through faith adore his mercies, and henceforward more diligently work out their own salvation with fear and trembling.
insight: Borrowing Peter's "incorruptible seed," Dort says regeneration survives every fall, as God's Word and Spirit renew the fallen to godly sorrow. When you sin again, the seed in you has not died, so if you belong to him, repent quickly and work out your salvation with fear and trembling.

text: Thus, it is not in consequence of their own merits, or strength, but of God's free mercy, that they do not totally fall from faith and grace, nor continue and perish finally in their backslidings; which, with respect to themselves, is not only possible, but would undoubtedly happen; but with respect to God, it is utterly impossible, since his counsel cannot be changed, nor his promise fail, neither can the call according to his purpose be revoked, nor the merit, intercession and preservation of Christ be rendered ineffectual, nor the sealing of the Holy Spirit be frustrated or obliterated.
insight: Perseverance can sound like a prize for the tenacious, yet Dort says that with respect to themselves believers would "undoubtedly" fall away. You finish the race because God's counsel cannot change and Christ's intercession cannot fail, so boast in him when you reach the end.

text: Of this preservation of the elect to salvation, and of their perseverance in the faith, true believers for themselves may and ought to obtain assurance according to the measure of their faith, whereby they arrive at the certain persuasion, that they ever will continue true and living members of the church; and that they experience forgiveness of sins, and will at last inherit eternal life.
insight: Many treat lingering doubt about their salvation as a mark of modesty, yet Dort calls assurance something believers 'may and ought to obtain' in the measure of their faith. If you have been nursing uncertainty as if it were humility, ask God plainly for the persuasion he means you to have.

text: This assurance, however, is not produced by any peculiar revelation contrary to, or independent of the Word of God; but springs from faith in God's promises, which he has most abundantly revealed in his Word for our comfort; from the testimony of the Holy Spirit, witnessing with our spirit, that we are children and heirs of God, Romans 8:16; and lastly, from a serious and holy desire to preserve a good conscience, and to perform good works. And if the elect of God were deprived of this solid comfort, that they shall finally obtain the victory, and of this infallible pledge or earnest of eternal glory, they would be of all men the most miserable.
insight: Dort roots assurance first in 'faith in God's promises' revealed in the Word, and only then in the Spirit's witness and a holy desire to keep a good conscience and do good works. When your conscience accuses you and your feelings go quiet, go back to the promises first, since the other two confirm that trust and cannot stand in for it.

text: The Scripture moreover testifies, that believers in this life have to struggle with various carnal doubts, and that under grievous temptations they are not always sensible of this full assurance of faith and certainty of persevering. But God, who is the Father of all consolation, does not suffer them to be tempted above that they are able, but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that they may be able to bear it, I Corinthians 10:13, and by the Holy Spirit again inspires them with the comfortable assurance of persevering.
insight: Fear that your faith has quietly died often arrives in the thick of temptation, and Dort names that very season, when believers 'are not always sensible' of full assurance. God will not let you be tried beyond bearing; he makes the way of escape and breathes comfort back into you.

text: This certainty of perseverance, however, is so far from exciting in believers a spirit of pride, or of rendering them carnally secure, that on the contrary, it is the real source of humility, filial reverence, true piety, patience in every tribulation, fervent prayers, constancy in suffering, and in confessing the truth, and of solid rejoicing in God: so that the consideration of this benefit should serve as an incentive to the serious and constant practice of gratitude and good works, as appears from the testimonies of Scripture, and the examples of the saints.
insight: Dort denies that the certainty of perseverance breeds pride or carnal security, calling it 'the real source of humility, filial reverence, true piety,' patience, and fervent prayer. If you are in Christ, let the hope that God will keep you drive you toward gratitude and good works, and treat carelessness as a sign you have misread the promise.

text: Neither does renewed confidence or persevering produce licentiousness, or a disregard to piety in those who are recovering from backsliding; but it renders them much more careful and solicitous to continue in the ways of the Lord, which he hath ordained, that they who walk therein may maintain an assurance of persevering, lest by abusing his fatherly kindness, God should turn away his gracious countenance from them, to behold which is to the godly dearer than life: the withdrawing thereof is more bitter than death, and they in consequence hereof should fall into more grievous torments of conscience.
insight: Anyone who has come back from a fall knows what Dort means by God's face being 'dearer than life' and its withdrawal 'more bitter than death.' Carry that memory with you as a guard, and walk more carefully in the ways the Lord has marked out for you.

text: And as it hath pleased God, by the preaching of the gospel, to begin this work of grace in us, so he preserves, continues, and perfects it by the hearing and reading of his Word, by meditation thereon, and by the exhortations, threatenings, and promises thereof, as well as by the use of the sacraments.
insight: God begins grace 'by the preaching of the gospel' and keeps it alive through the same Word, heard, read, and meditated on, with its exhortations, threatenings, and promises, and through the sacraments. So sit under preaching and come to the Lord's Table as well as reading at home, because Dort names these public means as the way God perfects his work.

text: Who teach: That true believers and regenerate can sin the sin unto death or against the Holy Spirit. Since the same Apostle John, after having spoken in the fifth chapter of his first epistle, vss. 16 and 17, of those who sin unto death and having forbidden to pray for them, immediately adds to this in vs. 18: "We know that whosoever is begotten of God sinneth not (meaning a sin of that character), but he that is begotten of God keepeth himself, and the evil one toucheth him not," I John 5:18.
insight: Dort denies that true believers can sin the sin unto death, pointing to John's word that whoever is begotten of God keeps himself and 'the evil one toucheth him not.' If fear of that sin torments you, bring the fear to Christ and ask his forgiveness, since he has promised to cast out no one who comes to him.

text: Who teach: That the faith of those, who believe for a time, does not differ from justifying and saving faith except only in duration. For Christ himself, in Matthew 13:20, Luke 8:13, and in other places, evidently notes, besides this duration, a threefold difference between those who believe only for a time and true believers, when he declares that the former receive the seed in stony ground, but the latter in the good ground or heart; that the former are without root, but that the latter have a firm root; that the former are without fruit, but that the latter bring forth their fruit in various measure, with constancy and steadfastness.
insight: Meeting in 1618 and 1619 to answer the Remonstrants, the Synod of Dort rejected the claim that temporary faith differs from saving faith only in how long it lasts. Christ's parable of the sower points you to root and fruit, so ask whether your faith is sinking down into him.

text: Who teach: That it is not absurd that one having lost his first regeneration, is again and even often born anew. For these deny by this doctrine the incorruptibleness of the seed of God, whereby we are born again. Contrary to the testimony of the Apostle Peter: "Having been begotten again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible," I Peter 1:23.
insight: Dort rejects the idea that someone can lose regeneration and be born again over and over, because Peter calls the seed of new life 'incorruptible.' If you are in Christ, you need no second new birth after a fall; you need to repent and grow from the seed God has sown.

text: Who teach: That Christ has in no place prayed that believers should infallibly continue in faith. For they contradict Christ himself, who says: "I have prayed for thee (Simon), that thy faith fail not," Luke 22:32; and the Evangelist John, who declares, that Christ has not prayed for the Apostles only, but also for those who through their word would believer: "Holy Father, keep them in thy name," and: "I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil one," John 17:11, 15, 20.
insight: Would the Father ignore a prayer his Son prayed by name? Jesus asked that Simon's faith fail not and that all who believe through the apostles' word be kept from the evil one, and if you believe through their word, you were in that prayer.

text: The Books commonly called Apocrypha not being of Divine inspiration, are no part of the Canon (or rule) of the Scripture, and therefore are of no authority to the Church of God, nor to be any otherwise approved or made use of, then other humane writings.
insight: The books called Apocrypha, 'not being of Divine inspiration,' are no part of the canon and may be used only like 'other humane writings.' You may learn history or wisdom from them as from any old book, but let only the inspired books settle what you must believe and do.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Authority of the Holy Scripture for which it ought to be believed dependeth not upon the testimony of any man, or Church; but wholly upon God (who is truth it self) the Author thereof; therefore it is to be received, because it is the Word of God.
insight: The Bible's authority, the reason it 'ought to be believed,' depends 'wholly upon God' its Author and on no man or church. When you open it, you are hearing from the One 'who is truth it self,' whatever anyone around you thinks of it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: All things in Scripture are not alike plain in themselves, nor alike clear unto all; yet those things which are necessary to be known, believed, and observed for Salvation, are so clearly propounded, and opened in some place of Scripture or other, that not only the learned, but the unlearned, in a due use of ordinary means, may attain to a sufficient understanding of them.
insight: Read the hard chapters without panic, because the 1689 framers promised that what you need for salvation is set out clearly somewhere in Scripture, plain enough for 'the unlearned' using ordinary means. Your lack of a seminary degree is no bar to knowing Christ.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The infallible rule of interpretation of Scripture is the Scripture it self: And therefore when there is a question about the true and full sense of any Scripture (which is not manifold but one) it must be searched by other places that speak more clearly.
insight: Because the true sense of any Scripture 'is not manifold but one,' a hard passage must be 'searched by other places that speak more clearly.' When a verse puzzles you, let plainer texts on the same subject guide you toward its one meaning, and distrust any reading that sets Scripture against itself.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The supream judge by which all controversies of Religion are to be determined, and all Decrees of Councels, opinions of antient Writers, Doctrines of men, and private Spirits, are to be examined, and in whose sentence we are to rest, can be no other but the Holy Scripture delivered by the Spirit, into which Scripture so delivered, our faith is finally resolved.
insight: Councils, ancient writers, doctrines of men, and private spirits all have to be examined by one 'supream judge,' the Holy Scripture delivered by the Spirit.
