Before you settle on what a favorite teacher or a strong impression tells you, test it against Scripture and let Scripture's sentence be the one you rest in.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: In this divine and infinite Being there are three subsistences, the Father the Word (or Son) and Holy Spirit, of one substance, power, and Eternity, each having the whole Divine Essence, yet the Essence undivided, the Father is of none neither begotten nor proceeding, the Son is Eternally begotten of the Father, the holy Spirit proceeding from the Father and the Son, all infinite, without beginning, therefore but one God, who is not to be divided in nature and Being; but distinguished by several peculiar, relative properties, and personal relations; which doctrine of the Trinity is the foundation of all our Communion with God, and comfortable dependance on him.
insight: Dense talk of subsistences and relations lands on two warm words: the Trinity is 'the foundation of all our Communion with God, and comfortable dependance on him.' When you pray, you lean on the Father through the Son by the Spirit, and that ground will hold you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God hath Decreed in himself from all Eternity, by the most wise and holy Councel of his own will, freely and unchangeably, all things whatsoever comes to passe; yet so as thereby is God neither the author of sin, nor hath fellowship with any therein, nor is violence offered to the will of the Creature, nor yet is the liberty, or contingency of second causes taken away, but rather established, in which appears his wisdom in disposing all things, and power, and faithfulness in accomplishing his Decree.
insight: Some hear that God decreed all things and picture a puppet show, yet the 1689 framers wrote that the liberty of second causes is 'established' by the decree and in no way removed. Your choices matter precisely because God's wise plan includes them.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although God knoweth whatsoever may, or can come to passe upon all supposed conditions; yet hath he not Decreed anything, because he foresaw it as future, or as that which would come to pass upon such conditions.
insight: God knows every outcome that could follow from any set of conditions, yet he decreed nothing 'because he foresaw it as future.' His purposes rest on his own will and wait on nothing in you, so if you trust Christ, you can thank God that your faith is the fruit of his purpose and was never its cause.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: By the decree of God for the manifestation of his glory some men and Angels, are predestinated, or fore-ordained to Eternal Life, through Jesus Christ to the praise of his glorious grace; others being left to act in their sin to their just condemnation, to the praise of his glorious justice.
insight: Notice the difference between being 'predestinated' to life and being 'left to act in their sin': God's choosing is active grace, while the lost receive only what their own sin has earned. You can rejoice in mercy without ever suspecting God of cruelty toward anyone.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: These Angels and Men thus predestinated, and fore-ordained, are particularly, and unchangeably designed; and their number so certain, and definite, that it cannot be either increased, or diminished.
insight: Anxiety about slipping out of God's hand finds no footing in a number 'so certain, and definite, that it cannot be either increased, or diminished.' If you rest on Christ, your name was never written in pencil, and no bad afternoon of yours can erase it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Those of mankind that are predestinated to life, God before the foundation of the world was laid, according to his eternal and immutable purpose, and the secret Councel and good pleasure of his will, hath chosen in Christ unto everlasting glory, out of his meer free grace and love; without any other thing in the creature as a condition or cause moving him thereunto.
insight: God chose those predestinated to life 'out of his meer free grace and love,' with nothing in the creature as 'a condition or cause moving him thereunto.' If you have come to Christ, stop searching your record for the reason, because God found none in you; election leaves you nothing to boast of and nothing to earn.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: As God hath appointed the Elect unto glory, so he hath by the eternal and most free purpose of his will, fore-ordained all the means thereunto, wherefore they who are elected, being faln in Adam, are redeemed by Christ, are effectually called unto faith in Christ, by his spirit working in due season, are justifyed, adopted, sanctified, and kept by his power through faith unto salvation; neither are any other redeemed by Christ, or effectually called, justified, adopted, sanctified, and saved, but the Elect only.
insight: Destination and road were mapped together: the God who appointed the elect to glory also fore-ordained the redemption, calling, justification, adoption, and sanctification that bring them there. Your slow walk of growing holiness belongs to that map, and he will keep you on it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Doctrine of this high mystery of predestination, is to be handled with special prudence, and care; that men attending the will of God revealed in his word, and yeilding obedience thereunto, may from the certainty of their effectual vocation, be assured of their eternal election; so shall this doctrine afford matter of praise, reverence, and admiration of God, and of humility, diligence, and abundant consolation, to all that sincerely obey the Gospel.
insight: Approach predestination the way you would carry something both precious and sharp, with 'special prudence, and care.' Start from your own effectual calling and your obedience to the gospel, and the doctrine will give you praise, humility, diligence, and 'abundant consolation.'

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: In the beginning it pleased God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, for the manifestation of the glory of his eternal power, wisdom, and goodness, to Create or make the world, and all things therein, whether visible or invisible, in the space of six days, and all very good.
insight: Every sky you walk under was made by Father, Son, and Holy Spirit together, in six days, and all very good. Before sin touched anything, creation was a display of God's power, wisdom, and goodness, and you can read that display on your morning walk.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: After God had made all other Creatures, he Created man, male and female, with reasonable and immortal souls, rendring them fit unto that life to God; for which they were Created; being made after the image of God, in knowledge, righteousness, and true holyness; having the Law of God written in their hearts, and power to fulfill it; and yet under a possibility of transgressing, being left to the liberty of their own will, which was subject to change.
insight: God made man in his image with a reasonable and immortal soul, 'having the Law of God written in their hearts, and power to fulfill it,' yet with a will 'subject to change.' If even unfallen Adam could fall, you have good reason to lean on grace and distrust your own unaided strength.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Besides the Law written in their hearts, they received a command not to eat of the tree of knowledge of good and evil; which whilst they kept, they were happy in their Communion with God, and had dominion over the Creatures.
insight: 'Whilst they kept' one command about one tree, Adam and Eve were happy in communion with God, and they broke it. Christ kept every command in your place, and if you trust him, your communion with God rests on his obedience, which frees you to obey him out of gratitude.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God the good Creator of all things, in his infinite power, and wisdom, doth uphold, direct, dispose, and govern all Creatures, and things, from the greatest even to the least, by his most wise and holy providence, to the end for the which they were Created; according unto his infallible foreknowledge, and the free and immutable Councel of his own will; to the praise of the glory of his wisdom, power, justice, infinite goodness and mercy.
insight: Nothing escapes the reach of 'from the greatest even to the least': God upholds, directs, disposes, and governs every creature and thing. The spilled coffee and the missed train in your week are ruled by the same wise hand that rules nations.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although in relation to the foreknowledge and Decree of God, the first cause, all things come to pass immutably and infallibly; so that there is not any thing, befalls any by chance, or without his Providence; yet by the same Providence he ordereth them to fall out, according to the nature of second causes, either necessarily, freely, or contingently.
insight: Because God is the first cause, nothing 'befalls any by chance, or without his Providence,' yet he orders events through second causes that act 'necessarily, freely, or contingently.' The chance meeting and the close decision are contingent from your side and never accidents to God, so choose carefully and trust him with the outcome.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God in his ordinary Providence maketh use of means; yet is free to work, without, above, and against them at his pleasure.
insight: Take the medicine, plant the seed, and pray, because God ordinarily works through means. Yet he is free to work 'without, above, and against them,' so you can hold both your efforts and their outcomes loosely in his hands.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Almighty power, unsearchable wisdom, and infinite goodness of God, so far manifest themselves in his Providence, that his determinate Councel extendeth it self even to the first fall, and all other sinful actions both of Angels, and Men; (and that not by a bare permission) which also he most wisely and powerfully boundeth, and otherwise ordereth, and governeth, in a manifold dispensation to his most holy ends: yet so, as the sinfulness of their acts proceedeth only from the Creatures, and not from God; who being most holy and righteous, neither is nor can be, the author or approver of sin.
insight: How can God rule over sin without being stained by it? The 1689 answer is that his counsel reaches even the first fall, by more than 'a bare permission,' while 'the sinfulness of their acts proceedeth only from the Creatures,' so you can trust him with the worst things done to you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The most wise, righteous, and gracious God, doth oftentimes, leave for a season his own children to manifold temptations, and the corruptions of their own heart, to chastise them for their former sins, or to discover unto them the hidden strength of corruption, and deceitfulness of their hearts, that they may be humbled; and to raise them to a more close, and constant dependence for their support, upon himself; and to make them more watchful against all future occasions of sin, and for other just and holy ends.
insight: Discouragement often follows a season when temptation hits harder than it has in years. The 1689 framers name God's purposes in such a season: to humble you, to expose the 'hidden strength of corruption,' and to draw you into closer dependence on himself, so the trial is a Father's work.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: As for those wicked and ungodly men, whom God as a righteous judge, for former sin doth blind and harden; from them he not only withholdeth his Grace, whereby they might have been inlightned in their understanding, and wrought upon in their hearts: But sometimes also withdraweth the gifts which they had, and exposeth them to such objects as their corruptions makes occasion of sin; and withall gives them over to their own lusts, the temptations of the world, and the power of Satan, whereby it comes to pass, that they harden themselves, even under those means which God useth for the softning of others.
insight: Judicial hardening is sometimes pictured as God forcing sin into innocent hearts, yet the text describes him withholding grace and handing sinners to lusts they already love, so that 'they harden themselves.' Answer God's softening means quickly whenever you feel your heart resisting them.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: As the Providence of God doth in general reach to all Creatures, so after a most special manner it taketh care of his Church, and disposeth of all things to the good thereof.
insight: Imagine a gardener who tends the whole estate but keeps a particular eye on one plot: providence reaches every creature, yet 'after a most special manner' it cares for the church. If you belong to Christ's people, the wider world's events are being disposed for your good.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although God created Man upright, and perfect, and gave him a righteous law, which had been unto life had he kept it, and threatned death upon the breach thereof; yet he did not long abide in this honour; Satan using the subtilty of the serpent to seduce Eve, then by her seducing Adam, who without any compulsion, did wilfully transgress the Law of their Creation, and the command given unto them, in eating the forbidden fruit; which God was pleased according to his wise and holy Councel to permit, having purposed to order it, to his own glory.
insight: Blaming the serpent came quickly in Eden, yet the 1689 text records that Adam transgressed 'without any compulsion,' wilfully. God ordered even that fall to his own glory, but when you sin, you cannot shift the weight onto tempters or circumstances.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Our first Parents by this Sin, fell from their original righteousness and communion with God, and we in them, whereby death came upon all; all becoming dead in Sin, and wholly defiled, in all the faculties, and parts, of soul, and body.
insight: Total depravity names a corruption reaching 'all the faculties, and parts, of soul, and body,' so that no corner of a person stayed clean after Adam fell. You need a Savior for your mind, your desires, and your body alike.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: They being the root, and by Gods appointment, standing in the room, and stead of all mankind; the guilt of the Sin was imputed, and corrupted nature conveyed, to all their posterity descending from them by ordinary generation, being now conceived in Sin, and by nature children of wrath, the servants of Sin, the subjects of death and all other miseries, spiritual, temporal and eternal, unless the Lord Jesus set them free.
insight: Federal headship means one man standing 'in the room, and stead of all mankind,' so that Adam's guilt is credited to his children and his corrupted nature passed down. Pray for your children as people who need the Lord Jesus to set them free, just as you did.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: From this original corruption, whereby we are utterly indisposed, disabled, and made opposite to all good, and wholly inclined to all evil, do proceed all actual transgressions.
insight: Weeds keep coming back when you only cut the tops, and actual sins spring from an 'original corruption' that leaves us 'utterly indisposed' to good. Ask God to work at the root of your heart when you confess this week's particular failure.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The corruption of nature, during this Life, doth remain in those that are regenerated: and although it be through Christ pardoned, and mortified, yet both it self, and the first motions thereof, are truely and properly Sin.
insight: Excusing first impulses as harmless because they are pardoned is a comfortable mistake; the 1689 framers call even 'the first motions' of remaining corruption 'truely and properly Sin.' You can be honest about the ugly flicker of envy or lust, because Christ's pardon covers the real thing.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The distance between God and the Creature is so great, that although reasonable Creatures do owe obedience unto him as their Creator, yet they could never have attained the reward of Life, but by some voluntary condescension on Gods part, which he hath been pleased to express, by way of Covenant.
insight: Reasonable creatures owe God obedience as their Creator, yet the distance between them is so great that they could never have attained 'the reward of Life' except by his 'voluntary condescension' in covenant. Every good you hope for from God comes as a gift he chose to promise, so approach him with open hands.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Moreover Man having brought himself under the curse of the Law by his fall, it pleased the Lord to make a Covenant of Grace wherein he freely offereth unto Sinners, Life and Salvation by Jesus Christ, requiring of them Faith in him, that they may be saved; and promising to give unto all those that are ordained unto eternal Life, his holy Spirit, to make them willing, and able to believe.
insight: Offer and ability arrive together in the covenant of grace: God 'freely offereth' life by Christ and promises his Spirit to make the elect 'willing, and able to believe.' If you find you want Christ at all, you are holding evidence that the promise has reached you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This Covenant is revealed in the Gospel; first of all to Adam in the promise of Salvation by the seed of the woman, and afterwards by farther steps, untill the full discovery thereof was compleated in the new Testament; and it is founded in that Eternal Covenant transaction, that was between the Father and the Son, about the Redemption of the Elect; and it is alone by the Grace of this Covenant, that all of the posterity of fallen Adam, that ever were saved, did obtain life and a blessed immortality; Man being now utterly uncapable of acceptance with God upon those terms, on which Adam stood in his state of innocency.
insight: Genesis 3:15 carried the first whisper of the gospel to Adam, and each later promise widened it until the New Testament brought 'the full discovery thereof.' When you read the Old Testament, you are watching one covenant of grace come into focus.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: It pleased God in his eternal purpose, to chuse and ordain the Lord Jesus his only begotten Son, according to the Covenant made between them both, to be the Mediator between God and Man; the Prophet, Priest and King; Head and Saviour of his Church, the heir of all things, and judge of the world: Unto whom he did from all Eternity give a people to be his seed, and to be by him in time redeemed, called, justified, sanctified, and glorified.
insight: In eternity the Father chose the Son to be 'the Mediator between God and Man,' prophet, priest, king, head, and judge, and gave him a people to redeem, call, justify, sanctify, and glorify. Whoever comes to Christ comes to a Mediator the Father appointed before the world began, so you can approach him with confidence.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Lord Jesus in his humane nature thus united to the divine, in the Person of the Son, was sanctified, and anointed with the Holy Spirit, above measure; having in him all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge; in whom it pleased the Father that all fullness should dwell: To the end that being holy, harmless, undefiled, and full of Grace, and Truth, he might be throughly furnished to execute the office of a Mediator, and Surety; which office he took not upon himself, but was thereunto called by his Father; who also put all power and judgement in his hand, and gave him Commandement to execute the same.
insight: Why would the eternal Son need the Holy Spirit? Because in his human nature he was 'anointed with the Holy Spirit, above measure,' thoroughly furnished for his office as a real man, and if Jesus walked in dependence on the Spirit, you have no reason to try living without him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This office the Lord Jesus did most willingly undertake, which that he might discharge he was made under the Law, and did perfectly fulfill it, and underwent the punishment due to us, which we should have born and suffered, being made Sin and a Curse for us: enduring most grievous sorrows in his Soul; and most painful sufferings in his body; was crucified, and died, and remained in the state of the dead; yet saw no corruption: on the third day he arose from the dead, with the same body in which he suffered; with which he also ascended into heaven: and there sitteth at the right hand of his Father, making intercession; and shall return to judge Men and Angels, at the end of the World.
insight: Nobody drafted Jesus into suffering: he 'did most willingly undertake' the office, kept the law, bore the curse, rose with the same body, and now intercedes. When you feel like a burden to him, remember that he took up your cause with open eyes.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Lord Jesus by his perfect obedience and sacrifice of himself, which he through the Eternal Spirit once offered up unto God, hath fully satisfied the Justice of God, procured reconciliation, and purchased an Everlasting inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven, for all those whom the Father hath given unto him.
insight: Christ's obedience and sacrifice 'fully satisfied the Justice of God' and purchased an everlasting inheritance 'for all those whom the Father hath given unto him,' so nothing is left unpaid for them. Come to Christ and rest on him, and you need add no payment of your own to a satisfaction he has already made in full.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although the price of Redemption was not actually paid by Christ, till after his Incarnation, yet the vertue, efficacy, and benefit thereof were communicated to the Elect in all ages successively, from the beginning of the World, in and by those Promises, Types, and Sacrifices, wherein he was revealed, and signified to be the Seed of the Woman, which should bruise the Serpents head; and the Lamb slain from the foundation of the World: Being the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever.
insight: Abraham and David could not see Calvary, yet its benefit reached them through promises, types, and sacrifices pointing to 'the Lamb slain from the foundation of the World.' The Christ they trusted from a distance is the one you trust up close.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Christ in the work of Mediation acteth according to both natures, by each nature doing that which is proper to it self; yet by reason of the Unity of the Person, that which is proper to one nature, is sometimes in Scripture attributed to the Person denominated by the other nature.
insight: Communication of properties is the old name for Scripture's habit of saying the Lord of glory was crucified: what belongs to one nature is credited to the person named by the other. When you pray, the one who hears you both suffered in the flesh and reigns as God.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: To all those for whom Christ hath obtained eternal redemption, he doth certainly, and effectually apply, and communicate the same; making intercession for them, uniting them to himself by his spirit, revealing unto them, in and by the word, the mystery of salvation; perswading them to believe, and obey; governing their hearts by his word and spirit, and overcoming all their enemies by his Almighty power, and wisdom; in such manner, and wayes as are most consonant to his wonderful, and unsearchable dispensation; and all of free, and absolute Grace, without any condition foreseen in them, to procure it.
insight: Worry that Christ bought salvation and left you to finish claiming it meets a firm promise: he 'doth certainly, and effectually apply' redemption, interceding, uniting you to himself, and overcoming every enemy. Nobody he died for is abandoned halfway home.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This office of Mediator between God and Man, is proper onely to Christ, who is the Prophet, Priest, and King of the Church of God; and may not be either in whole, or any part thereof transfer'd from him to any other.
insight: Refuse every offer of a second mediator, whether a saint, a priest, or your own record of devotion, because the office belongs to Christ alone and may not be handed to another 'in whole, or any part thereof.' You can go to God directly through him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This number and order of Offices is necessary; for in respect of our ignorance, we stand in need of his prophetical Office; and in respect of our alienation from God, and imperfection of the best of our services, we need his Priestly office, to reconcile us, and present us acceptable unto God: and in respect our averseness, and utter inability to return to God, and for our rescue, and security from our spiritual adversaries, we need his Kingly office, to convince, subdue, draw, uphold, deliver, and preserve us to his Heavenly Kingdome.
insight: Which of your needs feels loudest right now: ignorance, guilt, or a heart too weak to come back to God? The 1689 framers match each to an office, prophet, priest, and king, and one Savior carries all three for you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God hath indued the Will of Man, with that natural liberty, and power of acting upon choice; that it is neither forced, nor by any necessity of nature determined to do good or evil.
insight: Freedom of the will, in its most basic sense, means your choices are 'neither forced, nor by any necessity of nature determined.' You really do choose, which is why you answer for your choices, and why only grace can turn that freedom toward God.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Man in his state of innocency, had freedom, and power, to will, and to do that which was good, and well-pleasing to God; but yet was mutable, so that he might fall from it.
insight: Envy of Eden is misplaced nostalgia: Adam had freedom and power to do good, 'yet was mutable, so that he might fall from it.' What Christ gives you is better, a life that will not be lost, so you have no reason to wish yourself back in the garden.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Man by his fall into a state of sin hath wholly lost all ability of Will, to any spiritual good accompanying salvation; so as a natural man, being altogether averse from that good, and dead in Sin, is not able, by his own strength, to convert himself; or to prepare himself thereunto.
insight: Evangelism built on the idea that a sinner only needs a nudge misreads the fall, since the natural man cannot 'convert himself; or to prepare himself thereunto.' Pray for the friend you are telling about Christ as someone who needs raising from the dead.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: When God converts a sinner, and translates him into the state of Grace he freeth him from his natural bondage under sin, and by his grace alone, enables him freely to will, and to do that which is spiritually good; yet so as that by reason of his remaining corruptions he doth not perfectly nor only will that which is good; but doth also will that which is evil.
insight: Frustration at wanting good and doing evil in the same afternoon is exactly what the 1689 framers expect after conversion: the freed will 'doth not perfectly nor only will that which is good.' When you feel it, bring both the good desire and the leftover pull to God without despair.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Will of Man is made perfectly, and immutably free to good alone, in the state of Glory only.
insight: Beyond death lies the day your will becomes 'perfectly, and immutably free to good alone.' Run toward that finish line honestly, and you can stop pretending you have crossed it already.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Those whom God hath predestinated unto Life, he is pleased in his appointed, and accepted time, effectually to call by his word, and Spirit, out of that state of sin, and death, in which they are by nature, to grace and Salvation by Jesus Christ; inlightning their minds, spiritually, and savingly to understand the things of God; taking away their heart of stone, and giving unto them an heart of flesh; renewing their wills, and by his Almighty power determining them to that which is good, and effectually drawing them to Jesus Christ; yet so as they come most freely, being made willing by his Grace.
insight: Surgery is the picture: God takes away 'their heart of stone' and gives 'an heart of flesh,' so that sinners 'come most freely, being made willing by his Grace.' Pray for the hardened people you love, asking God to do the willing-making work only he can do.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This Effectual Call is of God's free, and special grace alone, not from any thing at all foreseen in man, nor from any power, or agency in the Creature, coworking with his special Grace, the Creature being wholly passive therein, being dead in sins and trespasses, until being quickned & renewed by the holy Spirit, he is thereby enabled to answer this call, and to embrace the Grace offered and conveyed in it; and that by no less power, then that which raised up Christ from the dead.
insight: Resurrection power is what it took to bring you to life, 'no less power, then that which raised up Christ from the dead,' because a dead sinner is 'wholly passive' until quickened. You can boast of nothing in your conversion except the God who raised you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Elect Infants dying in infancy, are regenerated and saved by Christ through the Spirit; who worketh when, and where, and how he pleaseth: so also are all other elect persons, who are uncapable of being outwardly called by the Ministry of the Word.
insight: Westminster's divines had written nearly the same sentence about elect infants in 1646, and the Baptists of 1689 kept it. If you grieve a little one, you can entrust that child to the Spirit 'who worketh when, and where, and how he pleaseth.'

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Others not elected, although they may be called by the Ministry of the word, and may have some common operations of the Spirit, yet not being effectually drawn by the Father, they neither will, nor can truly come to Christ; and therefore cannot be saved: much less can men that receive not the Christian Religion be saved; be they never so diligent to frame their lives according to the light of nature, and the Law of that Religion they do profess.
insight: Sincerity and diligence in another religion, however earnest, cannot save, and even 'some common operations of the Spirit' under gospel preaching fall short without the Father's drawing. Pray for your sincere neighbors as people who need Christ himself, and tell them about him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Those whom God Effectually calleth, he also freely justifieth, not by infusing Righteousness into them, but by pardoning their sins, and by accounting, and accepting their Persons as Righteous; not for any thing wrought in them, or done by them, but for Christ's sake alone, not by imputing faith it self, the act of beleiving, or any other evangelical obedience to them, as their Righteousness; but by imputing Christs active obedience unto the whole Law, and passive obedience in his death, for their whole and sole Righteousnnss, they receiving, and resting on him, and his Righteousness, by Faith; which faith they have not of themselves, it is the gift of God.
insight: God justifies by 'pardoning their sins, and by accounting, and accepting their Persons as Righteous' for Christ's sake alone, counting nothing wrought in them or done by them as their righteousness. When your own obedience looks thin, rest on Christ's obedience to the whole law and his death, because that is the only righteousness God accepts for anyone.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Faith thus receiving and resting on Christ, and his Righteousness, is the alone instrument of Justification: yet it is not alone in the person justified, but is ever accompanied with all other saving Graces, and is no dead faith, but worketh by love.
insight: Empty hands receive a gift without earning it, and faith is 'the alone instrument of Justification.' Those same hands soon get busy with love, because saving faith always travels with other graces, so look for that company in your own life.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Christ by his obedience, and death, did fully discharge the debt of all those that are justified; and did by the sacrifice of himself, in the blood of his cross, undergoing in their stead, the penalty due unto them: make a proper, real and full satisfaction to Gods justice in their behalf: yet in asmuch as he was given by the Father for them, and his Obedience and Satisfaction accepted in their stead, and both freely, not for any thing in them; their Justification is only of Free Grace, that both the exact justice and rich Grace of God, might be glorified in the Justification of sinners.
insight: Christ made 'a proper, real and full satisfaction' to God's justice, and yet justification is 'only of Free Grace,' because the Father himself gave the Son and accepted his obedience in the sinner's stead. If you rest on Christ, your pardon honors God's justice and displays his grace at once, and no part of it waits on anything you bring.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God did from all eternity decreeto justifie all the Elect, and Christ did in the fulness of time die for their sins, and rise again for their Justification; Nevertheless they are not justified personally, untill the Holy Spirit, doth in due time actually apply Christ unto them.
insight: Speculation that the elect are justified before they believe collapses against a plain line: none are justified personally until the Spirit applies Christ to them in due time. Look for your assurance in the Christ you have trusted, and leave the decree to God.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God doth continue to Forgive the sins of those that are justified, and although they can never fall from the state of justication; yet they may by their sins fall under Gods Fatherly displeasure; and in that condition, they have not usually the light of his Countenance restored unto them, untill they humble themselves, confess their sins, beg pardon, and renew their faith, and repentance.
insight: Run toward your Father after you sin, confessing and begging pardon, because justification can never be lost while the light of his countenance can be dimmed. His fatherly displeasure is the frown of a parent who wants you home.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Justification of Believers under the Old Testament was in all these respects, one and the same with the justification of Believers under the New Tement.
insight: Old Testament believers were justified 'one and the same' way as believers under the New Testament: pardoned and accounted righteous for Christ's sake, through faith. The Christ whom Abraham trusted through promise is the one you are called to trust, and his righteousness, never your faith as a work, is what God reckons to those who rest on him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: All those that are justified, God vouchsafed, in, and for the sake of his only Son Jesus Christ, to make partakers of the Grace of Adoption; by which they are taken into the number, and enjoy the Liberties, and Priveledges of Children of God; have his name put upon them, receive the Spirit of Adoption, have access to the throne of Grace with boldness, are enabled to cry Abba, Father, are pitied, protected, provided for, and chastned by him, as by a Father; yet never cast off; but sealed to the day of Redemption, and inherit the promises, as heirs, of everlasting Salvation.
insight: Family privileges pile up in one long sentence: God's name put on them, bold access, the cry 'Abba, Father,' pity, protection, provision, discipline, and being 'never cast off.' If you are in Christ, you belong in the house as a child, so come to your Father with the freedom of a son or daughter.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: They who are united to Christ, Effectually called, and regenerated, having a new heart, and a new Spirit created in them, through the vertue of Christ's death, and Resurrection; are also farther sanctified, really, and personally, through the same vertue, by his word and Spirit dwelling in them; the dominion of the whole body of sin is destroyed, and the several lusts thereof, are more and more weakned, and mortified; and they more and more quickened, and strengthned in all saving graces, to the practice of all true holyness, without which no man shall see the Lord.
insight: Growth in holiness has a name, sanctification: the Spirit's work of weakening 'the several lusts' of sin and strengthening 'all saving graces' in those already given a new heart. You can expect real change over years, 'more and more,' through Scripture and the Spirit dwelling in you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This Sanctification is throughout, in the whole man, yet imperfect in this life; there abideth still some remnants of corruption in every part, whence ariseth a continual, and irreconcilable war; the Flesh lusting against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the Flesh.
insight: Sanctification reaches 'the whole man' yet stays 'imperfect in this life,' so believers live with a 'continual, and irreconcilable war' of flesh against Spirit. Anyone in Christ should expect that fight to last a lifetime, so keep resisting sin and look to Christ for your hope when the battle goes badly.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: In which war, although the remaining corruption for a time may much prevail; yet through the continual supply of strength from the sanctifying Spirit of Christ the regenerate part doth overcome; and so the Saints grow in Grace, perfecting holiness in the fear of God, pressing after an heavenly life, in Evangelical Obedience to all the commands which Christ as Head and King, in his Word hath prescribed to them.
insight: Are you losing more battles than you win lately? The framers admit remaining corruption 'for a time may much prevail,' yet the regenerate part overcomes through a 'continual supply of strength' from Christ's Spirit, so keep pressing after holiness in the fear of God.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Grace of Faith, whereby the Elect are enabled to beleive to the saving of their souls, is the work of the Spirit of Christ in their hearts; and is ordinarily wrought by the Ministry of the Word; by which also, and by the administration of Baptisme, and the Lords Supper, Prayer and other Means appointed of God, it is increased, and strengthned.
insight: Show up where faith is fed: the preached Word, baptism, the Lord's Supper, and prayer are the tools by which the Spirit increases and strengthens what he first created in you. You will rarely feel a thrill, and you will grow all the same.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This Faith although it be different in degrees, and may be weak, or strong; yet it is in the least degree of it, different in the kind, or nature of it (as is all other saving Grace) from the Faith, and common grace of temporary beleivers; and therefore though it may be many times assailed, and weakned; yet it gets the victory; growing up in many, to the attainment of a full assurance through Christ, who is both the Author and finisher of our Faith.
insight: Shame over weak faith fades when you learn that the least degree of saving faith differs 'in the kind, or nature' from temporary belief. Yours may be assailed and weakened, yet it gets the victory, because Christ is its Author and finisher.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Such of the Elect as are converted at riper years, having sometimes lived in the state of nature, and therein served divers lusts and pleasures, God in their Effectual Calling giveth them Repentance unto Life.
insight: Repentance unto life comes to late converts as a gift within God's effectual call, even after long years spent serving "divers lusts and pleasures." If you came to Christ late, receive your grief over those years as his work in you, and bring the memory of them to him without despair.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Whereas there is none that doth good, and sinneth not; and the best of men may through the power, and deceitfulness of their corruption dwelling in them, with the prevalency of temptation, fall into great sins, and provocations; God hath in the Covenant of Grace, mercifully provided that Beleivers so sinning, and falling, be renewed through Repentance unto Salvation.
insight: The best believers may "fall into great sins," and God has provided in the covenant of grace that those who so fall are renewed through repentance unto salvation. If you have fallen badly, that provision was made with such falls in view, so return to God in repentance without waiting to feel worthy.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This saving Repentance is an evangelical Grace, whereby a person being by the Holy Spirit made sensible of the manifold evils of his sin, doth, by Faith in Christ, humble himself for it, with godly sorrow, detestation of it, and self abhorrency; praying for pardon, and strength of grace, with a purpose and endeavour by supplies of the Spirit, to walk before God unto all well pleasing in all things.
insight: Four things make up saving repentance: the Spirit makes you see your sin, faith sends you to Christ, godly sorrow humbles you, and a purpose forms to walk differently. Remorse that skips Christ and the new purpose is only regret, so when conviction comes, ask for strength as well as pardon.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: As Repentance is to be continued through the whole course of our lives, upon the account of the body of death, and the motions thereof; so it is every mans duty, to repent of his particular known sins, particularly.
insight: Repentance is meant to run through the whole course of life, and it is every person's duty to repent of particular known sins "particularly," one by one. Name before God the specific sin you know of, since a vague sense of failure is easy to carry and hard to turn from.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Such is the provision which God hath made through Christ in the Covenant of Grace, for the preservation of Believers unto Salvation, that although there is no sin so small, but it deserves damnation; yet there is no sin so great, that it shall bring damnation on them that repent; which makes the constant preaching of Repentance necessary.
insight: Even the smallest sin "deserves damnation," yet no sin is so great "that it shall bring damnation on them that repent," because Christ has borne what the penitent deserved. Let the first clause stop you from calling any sin small, and the second stop you from thinking any sin too great to bring to him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Good Works are only such as God hath commanded in his Holy word; and not such as without the warrant thereof, are devised by men, out of blind zeal, or upon any pretence of good intentions.
insight: Test every fresh burst of spiritual zeal against what God has commanded in his Word. Good works are the ones he asked for; blind zeal and good intentions can dress up a human invention, and you could spend years on something he never requested.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: These good works, done in obedience to Gods commandments, are the fruits, and evidences of a true, and lively faith; and by them Believers manifest their thankfullness, strengthen their assurance, edifie their brethren, adorn the profession of the Gospel, stop the mouths of the adversaries and glorifie God whose workmanship they are, created in Christ Jesus thereunto, that having their fruit unto holiness, they may have the end eternal life.
insight: Good works are those "done in obedience to Gods commandments," and they are "fruits, and evidences of a true, and lively faith," the handiwork of God who created believers in Christ Jesus for them. When you obey a plain command of God, take it as fruit of the faith he gave, and thank him as the workman behind it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Their ability to do good works, is not at all of themselves; but wholly from the Spirit of Christ; and that they may be enabled thereunto, besides the graces they have already received, there is necessary an actual influence of the same Holy Spirit, to work in them to will, and to do, of his good pleasure; yet are they not hereupon to grow negligent, as if they were not bound to perform any duty, unless upon a special motion of the Spirit; but they ought to be diligent in stirring up the Grace of God that is in them.
insight: Power for good works comes wholly from the Spirit of Christ, yet believers are warned against waiting for "a special motion of the Spirit" before doing any duty. Ask him for help, and then take up the plain duty in front of you, stirring up the grace God has already given.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: They who in their obedience attain to the greatest height which is possible in this life, are so far from being able to superrogate, and to do more then God requires, as that they fall short of much which in duty they are bound to do.
insight: No believer can do more than God requires, for even the greatest height of obedience possible in this life falls short of much that duty demands. If you are in Christ, let a good stretch of faithfulness send you to thank him for covering what you left undone.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: We cannot by our best works merit pardon of Sin or Eternal Life at the hand of God, by reason of the great disproportion that is between them and the glory to come; and the infinite distance that is between us and God, whom by them we can neither profit, nor satisfie for the debt of our former sins; but when we have done all we can, we have done but our duty, and are unprofitable servants; and because as they are good they proceed from his Spirit, and as they are wrought by us they are defiled and mixed with so much weakness and imperfection that they cannot endure the severity of Gods judgement.
insight: Even your best works cannot merit pardon, because as done by you they are "defiled and mixed with so much weakness and imperfection" that they cannot endure God's judgment. Do your duty gladly, and when you have done all, count yourself an unprofitable servant and look to Christ alone for pardon and eternal life.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Yet notwithstanding the persons of Believers being accepted through Christ their good works also are accepted in him; not as though they were in this life wholly unblameable and unreprovable in Gods sight; but that he looking upon them in his Son is pleased to accept and reward that which is sincere although accompanied with many weaknesses and imperfections.
insight: Acceptance in Christ works in two steps: God receives the person in his Son, and then receives that person's sincere works, weaknesses and all. You are offering a Father an honest child's effort, and he looks at it through Christ, so bring him what you have without waiting for it to be flawless.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Works done by unregenerate men although for the matter of them they may be things which God commands, and of good use, both to themselves and others; yet because they proceed not from a heart purified by faith, nor are done in a right manner according to the word, nor to a right end the glory of God; they are therefore sinful and cannot please God; nor make a man meet to receive grace from God; and yet their neglect of them is more sinful and displeasing to God.
insight: Deeds God commands can serve others well and yet be "sinful" in the unregenerate, because they lack a heart "purified by faith" and the aim of God's glory, though neglecting them "is more sinful." If you have not yet come to Christ, keep doing what God commands, but look to faith in him alone to make you acceptable to God.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This perseverance of the Saints depends not upon their own free will; but upon the immutability of the decree of Election flowing from the free and unchangeable love of God the Father; upon the efficacy of the merit and intercession of Jesus Christ and Union with him, the oath of God, the abiding of his Spirit & the seed of God within them, and the nature of the Covenant of Grace from all which ariseth also the certainty and infallibility thereof.
insight: Perseverance of the saints rests on the Father's unchanging election, Christ's merit and intercession, the oath of God, and the abiding Spirit, and none of these hangs on the believer's free will. If you are in Christ and fear falling away, count those supports on your weak days before you count your own strength.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: And though they may through the temptation of Satan and of the world, the prevalency of corruption remaining in them, and the neglect of means of their preservation fall into grievous sins, and for a time continue therein; whereby they incur Gods displeasure, and grieve his holy Spirit, come to have their graces and comforts impaired have their hearts hardened, and their Consciences wounded, hurt, and scandalize others, and bring temporal judgements upon themselves: yet they shall renew their repentance and be preserved through faith in Christ Jesus to the end.
insight: Grievous falls are named without softening, from hardened hearts and wounded consciences to scandal and temporal judgments, and yet true believers "shall renew their repentance and be preserved through faith in Christ Jesus to the end." If you are in Christ and far from him after a fall, turn back without delay, for he has promised to bring his own home.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although temporary Believers, and other unregenerate men, may vainly deceive themselves with false hopes, and carnal presumptions, of being in the favour of God, and state of salvation, which hope of theirs shall perish; yet such as truely believe in the Lord Jesus, and love him in sincerity, endeavouring to walk in all good Conscience before him, may in this life be certainly assured that they are in the state of Grace; and may rejoyce in the hope of the glory of God which hope shall never make them ashamed.
insight: False hope built on carnal presumption will perish, while those who truly believe in Jesus and love him sincerely may in this life be certainly assured that they are in the state of grace. Ask yourself honestly where your hope rests, and if it rests anywhere but Christ, move it onto him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This certainty is not a bare conjectural, and probable perswasion, grounded upon a fallible hope; but an infallible assurance of faith founded on the Blood and Righteousness of Christ revealed in the Gospel; and also upon the inward evidence of those graces of the Spirit unto which promises are made, and on the testimony of the Spirit of adoption, witnessing with our Spirits that we are the children of God; and as a fruit thereof keeping the heart both humble and holy.
insight: Notice "humble and holy" at the close: real assurance, grounded on Christ's blood and righteousness and the Spirit's witness, leaves a heart lower and cleaner, never swaggering. If your certainty is making you harsh toward other believers, you have borrowed its name without its fruit.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God gave to Adam a Law of universal obedience, written in his Heart, and a particular precept of not eating the Fruit of the tree of knowledge of good and evil; by which he bound him, and all his posterity to personal entire exact and perpetual obedience; promised life upon the fulfilling, and threatned death upon the breach of it; and indued him with power and ability to keep it.
insight: God bound Adam "and all his posterity" to perfect obedience, promising life and threatening death, and gave him real power to keep that law. Adam stood for his whole race when he fell, so your hope lies in the second Adam, whose perfect obedience is received by faith.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The same Law that was first written in the heart of man, continued to be a perfect rule of Righteousness after the fall; & was delivered by God upon Mount Sinai, in Ten Commandments and written in two Tables; the four first containing our duty towards God, and the other six our duty to man.
insight: The law first written on the human heart remained a perfect rule of righteousness after the fall and was delivered at Sinai on two tables, four commandments of duty toward God and six toward others. Let the accusing voice of your conscience drive you to Christ, who kept both tables in full.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Besides this Law commonly called moral, God was pleased to give to the people of Israel Ceremonial Laws, containing several typical ordinances, partly of worship, prefiguring Christ, his graces, actions, sufferings, and benefits; and partly holding forth divers instructions of moral duties, all which Ceremonial Laws being appointed only to the time of reformation, are by Jesus Christ the true Messiah and only Law-giver who was furnished with power from the Father, for that end, abrogated and taken away.
insight: Israel's ceremonial laws were types prefiguring Christ in his graces, sufferings, and benefits, appointed only until the time of reformation and then abrogated by Christ as the only Lawgiver. Read Leviticus looking for him, and let its sacrifices and washings point you to the cross.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: To them also he gave sundry judicial Laws, which expired together with the state of that people, not obliging any now by vertue of that institution; their general equity onely, being of moral use.
insight: Israel's judicial laws expired with that nation's state and bind no one now by that institution, though their general equity keeps its moral use. As you weigh a rule at work or a law in your city, ask what fairness those old statutes protected and whether you are guarding it too.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The moral Law doth for ever bind all, as well justified persons as others, to the obedience thereof, and that not only in regard of the matter contained in it, but also in respect of the authority of God the Creator; who gave it: Neither doth Christ in the Gospel any way dissolve, but much strengthen this obligation.
insight: The moral law binds "justified persons" as well as others, both for what it commands and for the authority of God the Creator who gave it, and Christ in the gospel does "much strengthen this obligation." Justification frees you from the law's curse, so keep its commands as a forgiven child of the God who wrote them.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Neither are the forementioned uses of the Law contrary to the Grace of the Gospel; but do sweetly comply with it; the Spirit of Christ subduing and inabling the Will of man, to do that freely and chearfully, which the will of God revealed in the Law, requireth to be done.
insight: Harmony between law and gospel comes through the Spirit: the two "sweetly comply" as he subdues your will, so that what the law requires you begin to do freely and cheerfully. When obedience feels like a weight you drag, ask him for that sweetness and expect him to change what you want.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Covenant of Works being broken by Sin, and made unprofitable unto Life; God was pleased to give forth the promise of Christ, the Seed of the Woman, as the means of calling the Elect, and begetting in them Faith and Repentance; in this Promise, the Gospel, as to the substance of it, was revealed, and therein Effectual, for the Conversion and Salvation of Sinners.
insight: After the covenant of works was broken by sin, God gave the promise of Christ, the Seed of the Woman, and the whole substance of the gospel was revealed in that first word of hope. If your own broken promises weigh on you, lean on his, for God kept that promise and offers Christ to you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: This Promise of Christ, and Salvation by him, is revealed only by the Word of God; neither do the Works of Creation, or Providence, with the light of Nature, make discovery of Christ, or of Grace by him; so much as in a general, or obscure way; much less that men destitute of the Revelation of him by the Promise, or Gospel; should be enabled thereby, to attain saving Faith, or Repentance.
insight: Creation and providence display God's power, yet they never disclose Christ or grace through him, even in an obscure way; that news comes only by the Word. If a friend says they meet God in nature, open the Scriptures with them so they can meet the Mediator too.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Revelation of the Gospel unto Sinners, made in divers times, and by sundry parts; with the addition of Promises, and Precepts for the Obedience required therein, as to the Nations, and Persons, to whom it is granted, is meerly of the Soveraign Will and good Pleasure of God; not being annexed by vertue of any Promise, to the due improvement of mens natural abilities, by vertue of Common light received, without it; which none ever did make, or can so do: And therefore in all Ages the preaching of the Gospel hath been granted unto persons and Nations, as to the extent, or streightning of it, in great variety, according to the Councell of the Will of God.
insight: The gospel reaches nations and persons by God's sovereign will and good pleasure, and no people ever earned it by using their natural light well. Thank him that the good news has come to you, and pray for peoples who have yet to hear it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Although the Gospel be the only outward means, of revealing Christ, and saving Grace; and is, as such, abundantly sufficient thereunto; yet that men who are dead in Trespasses, may be born again, Quickned or Regenerated; there is moreover necessary, an effectual, insuperable work of the Holy Spirit, upon the whole Soul, for the producing in them a new spiritual Life; without which no other means will effect their Conversion unto God.
insight: The gospel is the only outward means of revealing Christ and fully sufficient as such, yet those dead in trespasses need an effectual, insuperable work of the Spirit on the whole soul to be born again. Keep telling your unmoved friend about Christ, and pray for the Spirit to give life while you speak.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Liberty which Christ hath purchased for Believers under the Gospel, consists in their freedom from the guilt of Sin, the condemning wrath of God, the Rigour and Curse of the Law; and in their being delivered from this present evil World, Bondage to Satan, and Dominion of Sin; from the Evil of Afflictions; the Fear, and Sting of Death, the Victory of the Grave, and Everlasting Damnation; as also in their free access to God; and their yielding Obedience unto him not out of a slavish fear, but a Child-like love, and willing mind.
insight: Christian liberty has two sides: freedom from guilt, wrath, the curse of the law, bondage to Satan, and the sting of death, and freedom for access to God with "a Child-like love, and willing mind." If you are in Christ, come to your Father without a slave's dread and serve him gladly.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God alone is Lord of the Conscience, and hath left it free from the Doctrines and Commandments of men, which are in any thing contrary to his Word, or not contained in it. So that to Believe such Doctrines, or obey such Commands out of Conscience, is to betray true liberty of Conscience; and the requiring of an implicit Faith, and absolute and blind Obedience, is to destroy Liberty of Conscience, and Reason also.
insight: God alone is Lord of the conscience and has left it free from human doctrines and commands that contradict his Word or go beyond it, so a demand for "absolute and blind Obedience" destroys both conscience and reason. If a leader binds you where Scripture is silent, you may decline with a clear conscience and a kind answer.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: They who upon pretence of Christian Liberty do practice any sin, or cherish any sinfull lust; as they do thereby pervert the main design of the Grace of the Gospel, to their own Destruction; so they wholy destroy the end of Christian Liberty, which is, that being delivered out of the hands of all our Enemies we might serve the Lord without fear in Holiness, and Righteousness before him, all the days of our Life.
insight: Anyone who uses Christian liberty to cherish a sinful lust perverts the design of the gospel and destroys the very end of that liberty, which is serving the Lord without fear in holiness all our days. Name the sin you have been excusing with grace, and give it up to him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The light of Nature shews that there is a God, who hath Lordship, and Soveraigntye over all; is just, good, and doth good unto all; and is therefore to be feared, loved, praised, called upon, trusted in, and served, with all the Heart, and all the Soul, and with all the Might. But the acceptable way of Worshipping the true God, is instituted by himself; and so limited by his own revealed will, that he may not be Worshipped according to the imaginations, and devices of Men, or the suggestions of Satan, under any visible representations, or any other way, not prescribed in the Holy Scriptures.
insight: Nature teaches that God is to be feared, loved, and served with all the heart, yet the acceptable way of worshipping him is instituted by himself and limited by his revealed will. Before you add something new to your church's worship, ask whether Scripture prescribes it.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Religious Worship is to be given to God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and to him alone; not to Angels, Saints, or any other Creatures; and since the fall, not without a Mediator, nor in the Mediation of any other but Christ alone.
insight: Worship goes to Father, Son, and Spirit alone, and since the fall it comes only through the mediation of Christ alone, with no angel or saint in between. Bring your requests straight to God through his Son, who has opened the way for all who come by faith.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Prayer with thanksgiving, being one special part of natural worship, is by God required of all men. But that it may be accepted, it is to be made in the Name of the Son, by the help of the Spirit, according to his Will; with understanding, reverence, humility, fervency, faith, love, and perseverance; and when with others, in a known tongue.
insight: Prayer with thanksgiving is "by God required of all men," and when offered with others it must be "in a known tongue," so that those listening can understand and say amen. When you lead others in prayer, use words they can follow, and pray in the Son's name with the Spirit's help.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Prayer is to be made for things lawful, and for all sorts of men living, or that shall live hereafter; but not for the dead, nor for those of whom it may be known that they have sinned the sin unto death.
insight: Prayer is to be made for things lawful and for all people living or yet to live, but the dead lie beyond our intercession. If grief makes you want to pray for someone who has died, entrust them to the Judge of all the earth and pour that love into praying for the living around you.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The reading of the Scriptures, Preaching, and hearing the word of God, teaching and admonishing one another in Psalms, Hymns and Spiritual songs, singing with grace in our Hearts to the Lord; as also the Administration of Baptism, and the Lords Supper are all parts of Religious worship of God, to be performed in obedience to him, with understanding, faith, reverence, and godly fear; moreover solemn humiliation with fastings; and thanksgiving upon special occasions, ought to be used in an holy and religious manner.
insight: Every part of worship, from reading and preaching the word to baptism and the Lord's Supper, is to be performed "with understanding, faith, reverence, and godly fear." Singing belongs among them as "teaching and admonishing one another," so when you sing with the church, sing the words to the people beside you as well as to the Lord.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Neither Prayer, nor any other part of Religious worship, is now under the Gospel tied unto, or made more acceptable by, any place in which it is performed, or towards which it is directed; but God is to be worshipped every where in Spirit, and in truth; as in private families daily, and in secret each one by himself, so more solemnly in the publick Assemblies, which are not carelessely, nor wilfuly, to be neglected, or forsaken, when God by his word, or providence calleth thereunto.
insight: Under the gospel no place makes prayer or worship more acceptable, for God is to be worshipped everywhere in spirit and truth: daily in families, in secret alone, and more solemnly in the public assemblies. Pray at your kitchen table and gather with the church on the Lord's Day, and neglect neither.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: As it is of the Law of nature, that in general a proportion of time by Gods appointment, be set a part for the Worship of God; so by his Word in a positive-moral, and perpetual Commandement, binding all men, in all Ages, he hath particularly appointed one day in seven for a Sabbath to be kept holy unto him, which from the beginning of the World to the Resurrection of Christ, was the last day of the week; and from the resurrection of Christ, was changed into the first day of the week which is called the Lords day; and is to be continued to the end of the World, as the Christian Sabbath; the observation of the last day of the week being abolished.
insight: One day in seven is appointed by "a positive-moral, and perpetual Commandement," and from the resurrection that day moved from the last of the week to the first, "the Lords day." Keep Sunday set apart for God, knowing that the day you keep is tied to the morning Christ rose.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Sabbath is then kept holy unto the Lord, when men after a due preparing of their hearts, and ordering their common affairs aforehand, do not only observe an holy rest all the day, from their own works, words, and thoughts, about their worldly employment, and recreations, but also are taken up the whole time in the publick and private exercises of his worship, and in the duties of necessity and mercy.
insight: Plan Saturday so that Sunday is free: order your common affairs beforehand, so the day can be given to holy rest, public and private worship, and duties of necessity and mercy. A Lord's Day planned this way leaves you room to visit the lonely and to linger over Scripture.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: A lawful Oath is a part of religious worship, wherein the person swearing in Truth, Righteousness, and Judgement, solemnly calleth God to witness what he sweareth; and to judge him according to the Truth or falseness thereof.
insight: A lawful oath is itself an act of religious worship, in which the one swearing calls God to witness what he says and to judge him by its truth or falseness. If you are asked to take an oath or make a vow, speak each word as someone standing in God's presence.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Name of God only is that by which men ought to swear; and therein it is to be used, with all Holy Fear and reverence, therefore to swear vainly or rashly by that glorious, and dreadful name; or to swear at all by any other thing, is sinful and to be abhorred; yet as in matter of weight and moment for confirmation of truth, and ending all strife, an Oath is warranted by the Word of God; so a lawful Oath being imposed, by lawful Authority, in such matters, ought to be taken.
insight: Swearing rashly by God's name, or by anything besides his name, is sin to be abhorred, yet in weighty matters a lawful oath imposed by lawful authority ought to be taken. If a court asks you to swear, you may give your oath with a clear conscience and in the fear of the Lord.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Whosoever taketh an Oath warranted by the Word of God, ought duely to consider the weightiness of so solemn an act; and therein to avouch nothing, but what he knoweth to be the truth; for that by rash, false, and vain Oaths the Lord is provoked, and for them this Land mournes.
insight: Look at the closing words: "for them this Land mournes." Rash and false oaths provoke God and injure a whole people, which is why you should avouch nothing under oath but what you know to be true. Slow down before your next solemn promise and make sure every word will stand.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: An Oath is to be taken in the plain, and common sense of the words; without equivocation, or mental reservation.
insight: An oath is to be taken in the plain and common sense of its words, without equivocation or mental reservation, the private qualifier that quietly changes what was said aloud. Let your yes mean what your hearer takes it to mean, in contracts and casual promises alike.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: A Vow which is not to be made to any Creature, but to God alone, is to be made and performed with all Religious care, and faithfulness: But Popish Monastical Vows, of perpetual single life, professed poverty, and regular obedience, are so far from being degrees of higher perfection, that they are superstitious, and sinful snares, in which no Christian may intangle himself.
insight: Vows of "perpetual single life, professed poverty, and regular obedience" are no higher perfection but "superstitious, and sinful snares," binding what God left free. Make your vows to God alone, and keep with care the ones you have lawfully made.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: God the supream Lord, and King of all the World, hath ordained Civil Magistrates to be under him, over the people for his own glory, and the publick good; and to this end hath armed them with the power of the Sword, for defence and encouragement of them that do good, and for the punishment of evil doers.
insight: Every police officer's sidearm and every judge's gavel sits under a higher throne: God, King of all the world, ordained magistrates and armed them with the Sword to defend those who do good and punish evildoers. When you see that power used well, thank him; when you see it abused, pray, because the office belongs to him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: It is lawful for Christians to Accept, and Execute the Office of a Magistrate when called thereunto; in the management whereof, as they ought especially to maintain Justice, and Peace, according to the wholsome Laws of each Kingdome, and Commonwealth: so for that end they may lawfully now under the New Testament wage war upon just and necessary occasions.
insight: A Christian may lawfully accept the office of magistrate, maintaining justice and peace under the laws of their land, and may under the New Testament wage war on just and necessary occasions. If God calls you into public office or military service, you can take it up as service to him.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Civil Magistrates being set up by God, for the ends aforesaid; subjection in all lawful things commanded by them, ought to be yeilded by us, in the Lord; not only for wrath but for Conscience sake; and we ought to make supplications and prayers for Kings, and all that are in Authority, that under them we may live a quiet and peaceable life, in all godliness and honesty.
insight: Subjection to civil rulers in all lawful things is owed "in the Lord," for conscience' sake as well as for fear of wrath, along with prayer for all in authority that we may live quiet and peaceable lives. Pray by name for those who govern you, including the ones you voted against.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Marriage is to be between one Man and one Woman; neither is it lawful for any man to have more then one Wife, nor for any Woman to have more then one Husband at the same time.
insight: God's design joins "one Man and one Woman," with no second wife or second husband "at the same time," so the marriage bond is exclusive by its very shape. If you marry, you give your whole self to one spouse, and you may expect the same undivided pledge in return.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Marriage was ordained for the mutual help of Husband and Wife, for the increase of Man-kind, with a legitimate issue, and for preventing of uncleanness.
insight: Mutual help between husband and wife stands first among the ends of marriage, ahead of children and the guard against uncleanness. If you are married, look for one concrete way to lighten your spouse's load, since helping each other is part of what God made marriage for.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: It is lawful for all sorts of people to Marry, who are able with judgment to give their consent; yet it is the duty of Christians to marry in the Lord, and therefore such as profess the true Religion, should not Marry with Infidels, or Idolaters; neither should such as are godly be unequally yoked, by marrying with such as are wicked, in their life, or maintain damnable Heresie.
insight: Anyone able to consent with judgment may lawfully marry, yet Christians are to marry in the Lord and avoid being unequally yoked with unbelievers or the openly wicked. If you are considering marriage, weigh a prospective spouse's faith first, and talk with a pastor early.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: Marriage ought not to be within the degrees of consanguinity, or Affinity forbidden in the word; nor can such incestuous Marriage ever be made lawful, by any law of Man or consent of parties, so as those persons may live together as Man and Wife.
insight: A marriage within the forbidden degrees can never be made lawful "by any law of Man or consent of parties," because God's word sets that boundary, and neither a state nor a willing couple can move it. Where a statute and Scripture differ on whom you may marry, you are bound by Scripture whatever the statute allows.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.

text: The Catholick or universal Church, which (with respect to the internal work of the Spirit, and truth of grace) may be called invisible, consists of the whole number of the Elect, that have been, are, or shall be gathered into one, under Christ the head thereof; and is the spouse, the body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.
insight: The invisible church "consists of the whole number of the Elect" from every age, gathered into one under Christ as his spouse and body, and God alone sees that company whole. Your comfort lies with its head, who will lose none the Father gave him, so seek him by faith and meet his people in a visible church.

witness.voice: Andrew Gifford, Benjamin Keach, Charles Archer et al.
